items.title: GOAL: become the reproducible steward of at least one drifting record inventory (re-verification CI + public status surface)
items.note: Stewardship-not-search: adopt a record surface (bounds/constants/certificates), stand up automated re-fetch + re-verification + drift detection. Extension path if the pattern works: ML benchmark rot (same shape, different records). Source: skylark-site/docs/research-library/2026-07-22-portfolio-verifier-rich-domains.md.
items.closeWhen: One record inventory under automated re-verification, with (a) the drift alarm demonstrably ARMED AND FUNCTIONING for 30 consecutive days, and (b) at least one externally-acknowledged correction or confirmation.
items.note5: *** THE NORTH STAR MOVED. PR #141 WAS MERGED 2026-08-11T17:18:12Z BY teorth (Terence Tao, the repo owner). EXTERNALLY-ACKNOWLEDGED CORRECTIONS: 0 -> 1. *** Discovered 2026-08-12 while preparing A-14's draft, NOT by a check we ran -- see the self-criticism below, which matters as much as the win. Evidence, from the GitHub API not from memory: PR #141 'Fix five citation keys in 15a.md that do not match the page's reference list', opened 2026-08-05T20:45:04Z by u00dxk2, state MERGED, mergedBy teorth, 1 file, 6 additions / 6 deletions, merge commit 25cb93049b0900e7b23d6243d902574776346fa1 dated 2026-08-11T17:16:28Z touching only constants/15a.md. This is a public, dated, attributable acknowledgement by the maintainer of the surface we steward -- exactly what G-1's second close condition asks for, and it cannot be argued into ambiguity the way an unanswered email can. G-1's ACK CONDITION IS NOW MET; the item stays OPEN on the 30-day green-CI streak alone (day 20 of 30 as of 2026-08-12, day 1 = 2026-07-24). NOTE THE CHANNEL DISTINCTION: this is the PR channel (A-6's argument, 'a PR puts the metric behind a merge button' instead of behind an inbox). W-3, the watch on the erdosproblems.com EMAIL, is untouched and still unanswered -- do not conflate them and do not close W-3 on this. TWO FAILURES OF OUR OWN, recorded because a win found by accident is a process defect wearing a crown: (1) OUR ALARM DETECTED THIS MERGE AND WE MISREAD IT. The 2026-08-11 evening drift in constants/15a.md -- 'five bibliography keys normalised, every bound value byte-identical', which we verified carefully and attributed to upstream housekeeping -- WAS OUR OWN PR LANDING. Our d30d4e4 changed exactly that file with 6 insertions / 6 deletions, matching the PR. The instrument worked perfectly and the interpretation was wrong, which is the failure mode this lane exists to catch in other people. LESSON: when a drift lands on a file we have an open PR against, check the PR before writing the attribution -- a one-line `gh pr view` would have caught it that night. (2) THE 2026-08-12 DAILY REPORT ASSERTED 'PR #141 open and untouched since 5 August; checked, not nudged' WITHOUT CHECKING -- the phrase was inherited from the cold-start primer and carried forward as if executed. 'Check, do not poll' was read as licence not to look. A standing instruction not to nudge is not an instruction not to READ; verify by executing, never by inheriting.

items.note6: TIER-1 LEADING INDICATOR SHIPPED 2026-08-13: verified catches on named records, per week (scripts/catch-rate.mjs, `npm run catches`). Approved 8/12, unbuilt until today. WHY IT EXISTS: G-1 has no gradient. The north-star count sat at 0 for 21 days and then jumped to 1, which told us nothing on any day in between; this answers the question that count cannot -- IS THE ADOPTED SURFACE STILL ALIVE ENOUGH TO BE WORTH STEWARDING. A month of zeros is the signal to adopt a SECOND surface, not to try harder on this one. DERIVED FROM GIT HISTORY, never hand-maintained, for the same reason README's state block is generated: a figure a human retypes weekly is stale between retypes. DEFINITION: a catch is a GENERATED pin whose `expect` string changed in a commit. That is not a proxy for record movement, it IS record movement -- generated pins are rewritten wholesale by extract-pins.mjs from the mirror, so the only way one changes is that its bounds-table row moved upstream. The editorial/record distinction falls out for free and reproduces the ledger's own recorded history exactly: 50c8096 (7/28 editorial drift -- dead cross-link, missing C in LaTeX) never touched claims.json, pins byte-identical, ZERO catches even though the mirror really drifted and the alarm really fired; da17be3 (8/02, 'first pure record movement') moved exactly the three pins its note names (10c, 38a, 71a). LIVE READING AT SHIP: 8 distinct records across 3 weeks -- w/o 7/20 = 0 (two real drifts, both editorial-or-additive), w/o 7/27 = 4 (pin:3a:L, 10c:L, 38a:L, 71a:L), w/o 8/10 = 4 from 6 movements (pin:10a:L, 10a:U, 15a:U, 2a:U). TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT WHILE BUILDING IT, both fixed, both worth keeping: (1) the first version counted pin:2a:U THREE TIMES for the 8/12 burst in which upstream reworded one attribution paragraph on three pushes -- exactly the inflation CLAUDE.md's burst rule names THIS indicator as the victim of, and I built it in anyway. Headline is now DISTINCT RECORDS per week; the raw movement count stays visible in parentheses so the burst is not hidden either. (2) pin:15a:U moved on a CITATION-KEY RENAME where every bound value was byte-identical -- so a pin can move without a record moving, and that same pin was OUR OWN PR #141 landing rather than a catch at all. NOT FIXED BY DESIGN: separating those would need to parse the value out of the cell, which symbolic cells ($K_{DR}+10^{-26}$), negatives and O(.) asymptotics defeat, and would put an unverified mathematical judgment in our own ledger. THE PIN RULE APPLIES TO THE INDICATOR BUILT ON IT -- it asserts LISTING POSITION MOVED, never 'a record moved'. The figure is therefore an UPPER BOUND and says so on every run rather than in a doc nobody re-reads. KP-78 BOTH ANSWERS: selftest fires on a moved generated pin and is silent on unchanged / added (upstream adding 86a is not a catch) / removed / hand-claim edits / the commit before the file existed. Fixtures not git history, deliberately -- actions/checkout is depth-1, so a history-walking selftest would pass locally and be untestable in CI, which is the test-it-from-the-environment-that-runs-it rule. The CI-wiring guard was itself negative-controlled: deleting the new workflow step makes reverify.test.mjs exit 1 naming `node scripts/catch-rate.mjs --selftest`, restoring it exits 0 at 19 workflow steps / 13 selftests, with `git diff --numstat` proving the mutation landed first. The indicator itself never runs in CI: it renders a figure and no verdict, so there is nothing for a build to fail on -- same class as traffic-snapshot.mjs and gap-table.mjs. TIGHTENED SAME DAY after orchestrator management feedback on the P1 retro (msgId 5d328105), three changes, all shipped: (i) THE EMITTED LINE IS NOW SELF-DESCRIBING -- header reads 'Record-listing MOVEMENTS per week -- a CEILING on catches, not a count of them', because a reader who skips the caveat quotes whatever the header called it, and as built the figure asserts listing position moved and includes our own PR #141. The asymmetry that makes this safe is worth stating: THE POSITIVE SIDE IS AN ACTIVITY CEILING, THE ZERO SIDE IS EXACT -- a zero on an upper bound is a true zero -- and the decision rule attached to it ('a month of zeros means adopt a second surface') consumes only the zero side. (ii) THE PER-WEEK-QUOTE CONVENTION IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, in CLAUDE.md and in the script's own output: quote the PER-WEEK figure, never the running total, which answers no question we ask of it and only ever grows, so it reads as progress by construction. This closes the gap the retro itself named as 'not written down anywhere'. (iii) DEDUCTION TRIGGER RECORDED, deliberately not built: deduct our own merged PRs from the positive figure BEFORE ANY POSITIVE FIGURE GOES OUTWARD, or once own-PR pins exceed roughly one a month. At N=1 (pin:15a:U, PR #141) the deduction is not worth building, and git cannot see whose commit upstream merged, so the mechanism would be a list of our own merged PR shas kept here. STANDING PATTERN NAMED BY THE SAME FEEDBACK, worth more than this item: WHEN A RULE NAMES A SPECIFIC CORRUPTION, ADOPTION MEANS A TEST THAT ASSERTS IT, not a resolution to re-read the rule. The burst-inflation rule was prose on 8/12 and I built the inflation in anyway on 8/13; it is a mechanism now.
items.note7: TIER-1 INDICATOR DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-15, in the instrument shipped two days earlier. FOUND BY READING ITS OWN PRINTED OUTPUT during the steward cadence, not by a check: `npm run catches` showed THREE week rows for a FOUR-week repo. catch-rate.mjs built its week buckets from `git log -- ledger/claims.json`, so a week in which nothing committed that file was ABSENT rather than ZERO -- the week of 2026-08-03 simply did not exist in the table (git log confirms no commit touched the file between da17be3 on 2 Aug and 7018cce on 11 Aug, so that week was genuinely dry). THE COSMETIC HALF IS ONE MISSING ROW; THE LOAD-BEARING HALF IS THE COUNTER. The trailing dry-week count walked those same buckets, so it could only count weeks that were PRESENT -- and in a real drought NOTHING commits claims.json, because that file is rewritten only by extract-pins.mjs after a --snapshot and a snapshot happens only on drift. The quiet weeks never entered the map, the backward walk hit the last ACTIVE week immediately, and the count stopped at 1. The rule this indicator carries is 'a month of zeros is the signal to adopt a SECOND surface'. A month is four. THE COUNTER COULD NOT REACH TWO. This is the lane's founding defect for the third time -- an alarm that could not fire (7/24), a checker that read a sign-in page as a stale brief (8/02), and now a counter whose maximum sat below its own threshold; all three printed something that looked informative. BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED (KP-78): pre-fix, executed against one active week plus four calendar weeks of silence, 'weeks printed: 2026-07-06 2026-08-03 / dryWeeks reported: 1 / actual quiet weeks: 4'; post-fix the same shape asserts five keys plus the current week with trailingDry 4, with the negative controls asserted beside it (an unbroken run gains no rows; a movement in the newest week reads 0 dry). CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW LANE, first use in this lane and it paid for itself: catch-rate.mjs is a TRUSTED-PRINT INSTRUMENT (a script whose printed line a later reader believes) and also composes stored state across time, so the branch was held from main and the review requested (bus f2cbd000) before merging. Verdict SURVIVES with one pre-merge fix and two P2 edges, all three applied. F1, MATERIAL AND THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE THING TODAY: fillDryWeeks fills up to AND INCLUDING the current week and my trailingDry counted it, so on the Monday a drought completed its THIRD week the counter would read 4 and fire the adopt rule up to six days early. The printed table labels that row '(current, partial)' -- but THE LABEL SITS ON THE SURFACE A HUMAN READS WHILE THE RULE ACTS ON THE NUMBER. I had just shipped a fix whose entire argument was that the caveat was on the wrong surface, and put the next caveat on the wrong surface in the same file. A reviewer who had never seen the decision rule caught it; a self-review of my own rule did not. Fixed: trailingDry now takes the current week and skips it, and skips anything dated after it, so the rule needs four COMPLETED weeks; a movement still breaks the streak wherever it lands, because if the surface moved this week it is not dry whatever the completed-week count would say. F2: commit weeks came from git's %as, the author-LOCAL date, while 'today' came from a UTC clock, so a Sunday-evening commit in a negative-offset zone could read as an immediate dry week -- both sides now use the local calendar date. F3: a future-dated key from author clock skew sat beyond the fill target with a gap in front of it -- the fill now runs to whichever of the current week and the last key is later, and out-of-range weeks are EXCLUDED FROM THE COUNT rather than dropped from the table, because a phantom row is a display problem and silently discarding data would be worse. Commits c64fcd9 (fix) + 1179961 (review findings), merged --no-ff as 8ca908a so c64fcd9 keeps the sha the daily report cites; 13/13 self-tests and CI green on the merge commit. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-15-the-dry-week-counter-could-not-count-a-drought.md. STANDING CONSEQUENCE: request the review lane for the next in-class diff without being asked -- one posted line and about forty minutes of waiting returned a boundary error in the exact figure a decision rule consumes.
items.closeWhenPrevious: One record inventory under automated re-verification with 30-day green CI and at least one externally-acknowledged correction or confirmation.
items.closeWhenNote: REWORDED 2026-08-17 (leg (a) only; leg (b) untouched). Orchestrator-approved with conditions in the P1 management feedback of 2026-08-17T15:47:00.896Z, which also flags the 8/22 close question upward to David. Previous wording preserved verbatim in closeWhenPrevious.  WHY: leg (a) previously read "30-day green CI". THAT IS NOT WHAT HAS BEEN COUNTED, and the gap was never a mistake -- it was the operating rule, undocumented. The 2026-08-14 scheduled run FAILED on genuine upstream drift (upstream added Martinet constant, resolved in 433091b) and the streak was deliberately NOT reset, because this lane rules that a red drift run is the alarm working. On 2026-08-17 four more reds were filed on transport failures (HTTP 429/502 reaching the mirror sources) and likewise do not reset it. A literal reading of the old wording would have reset the streak twice and G-1 could effectively never close while the project was SUCCEEDING at its purpose. The reword documents the rule; it does not move the bar. That distinction is the whole reason this was surfaced rather than edited quietly five days before the leg fires.  WHAT COUNTS AS ARMED AND FUNCTIONING: the alarm carried information every day -- it could have gone red and did go red exactly when its inputs moved. A red does NOT reset the streak when its cause is (i) a record actually moving, or (ii) a cited source being unreachable, because unreachable means unverified and reporting green there would launder an unverifiable result into a pass. A red DOES reset the streak when the cause is OUR OWN INSTRUMENT failing -- a broken checker, or worse, a GREEN THAT COULD NOT HAVE GONE RED. That second case is why day 1 is 2026-07-24 and not the 2026-07-23 CI ship date: the 7/23-7/24 greens were green-by-construction because piped steps masked exit codes, so they carried no information and the clock was restarted (see note2).  DAY 1 = 2026-07-24. DAY 30 = 2026-08-22. As of 2026-08-17 the streak is day 25 and leg (b) has been satisfied since the 2026-08-11 merge of teorth/optimizationproblems#141, so BOTH legs are on course to be met on 2026-08-22. Closing G-1 remains a surfaced decision, not a self-approval.
items.signalPrestaged: PRE-STAGED 2026-08-17 so the 2026-08-22 read is a DECISION and not the start of a dig, and because the overdue-signal scan found this project had NO structured signal date on ANY open item -- so a gate five days out was invisible to every date-based check. That is the exact slip the scan exists to prevent, and the scan could not have caught it: a detector with no input can never fire.  LEG (a), the 30-day armed-and-functioning streak. Evidence pulled from the GitHub API, not memory: 25 SCHEDULED runs of reverify.yml between 2026-07-24 and 2026-08-17 inclusive -- ONE PER DAY, NO MISSING DAYS, which is itself the armed-and-functioning claim. 23 success, 2 failure. The two failures are both a RECORD ACTUALLY MOVING, i.e. the alarm working, and under the reworded closeWhen neither resets the streak:   - 2026-08-01, sha 3c0e217, run 30694707057 -> issue #7. The third drift and the largest: 12 files,     upstream c4f8386 -> 621429c, all 12 verified by execution before snapshot (A-2 note5).   - 2026-08-14, sha c83f94a. Upstream ADDED Martinet constant C_87; resolved in our 433091b     (chore(drift): resolve to e70b4a4 -- upstream added C_87, Martinet constant). ZERO of the 25 were an instrument failure, and none was a green-that-could-not-have-gone-red (the condition that restarted the clock on 2026-07-24). So leg (a) is on course to be MET on 2026-08-22 at 30 runs / 30 days. DO NOT count the 2026-08-17 push-run reds toward this: they were push and workflow_dispatch events, not scheduled, and all four were transport failures (HTTP 429/502) that moved no record -- verified as 0 BROKEN claim lines and 0 mirror verdicts in each run log, with upstream HEAD confirmed byte-identical to our manifest by an authenticated API read.  LEG (b), an externally-acknowledged correction: ALREADY MET since 2026-08-11 -- teorth merged teorth/optimizationproblems#141 (see note5/note-on-north-star above).  WHAT REMAINS ON 2026-08-22: re-run the same API query and confirm runs 26-30 (2026-08-18 through 2026-08-22) each exist and are either success or a documented record-movement red. Command: gh run list --workflow reverify.yml --limit 200 --json event,conclusion,headSha,createdAt then filter event==schedule. If all five land clean, BOTH legs are met and G-1 CLOSING IS A SURFACED DECISION FOR DAVID -- never a self-approval, and never a self-rating. OUTAGE CAVEAT, added after the 15:50Z fleet incident update: the GitHub outage opened 2026-08-17T13:40:03Z and the fleet rule is that CI conclusions inside that window read UNKNOWN rather than red or green. That does NOT weaken this streak evidence, and the reason is worth stating so nobody re-derives it: all 25 scheduled runs fired at roughly 09:2x UTC on their respective days, today's at 09:27Z, so every one predates the outage window. The four transport-failure reds today were push and pull_request events INSIDE the window and are excluded from the streak on BOTH grounds -- wrong event type for this leg, and an untrustworthy verdict. PRE-REGISTERED for the 2026-08-22 read: if the outage is still open on that date, record the affected days UNKNOWN and say so rather than counting them toward 30.
items.streakDayRule: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-17, BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS KNOWN, and deliberately in the direction that costs us.  THE HOLE THIS CLOSES, which I created earlier today: the reworded leg (a) says a red does not RESET the streak when its cause is an unreachable source. It did NOT say whether such a day COUNTS toward the 30. That omission was invisible until GitHub went into a critical outage (opened 2026-08-17T13:40:03Z, still unresolved at 16:36Z) five days before the leg completes, which makes it likely rather than hypothetical that one of runs 26-30 cannot fetch its sources. Deciding this on 2026-08-22, with a goal on the line and an obvious incentive to count generously, is exactly the decision nobody should be making under pressure.  THE RULE. A day counts toward the 30 if and only if that day's SCHEDULED run REACHED A VERDICT -- it completed and either confirmed no drift, or detected drift. Both are the alarm answering the question. A day whose scheduled run COULD NOT REACH A VERDICT -- it failed to fetch the cited sources, so nothing was actually verified -- does NOT count toward the 30, and does NOT reset it either. It PAUSES the clock, pushing the completion date out by one day per such day.  WHY PAUSE RATHER THAN COUNT OR RESET. Armed and functioning means the alarm ANSWERED the question. A run that could not fetch did not answer it, so counting it would inflate the streak with days that verified nothing -- the same laundering of an unverifiable into a pass that this repo refuses everywhere else (manual:true claims report UNVERIFIED, the brief check reports UNVERIFIABLE, the shallow-clone catch count reports UNKNOWN). Resetting would be equally wrong: nothing about our instrument failed, and a reset would punish us for someone else's outage and make the leg effectively unreachable during any multi-day infrastructure incident. Pause is the only reading that is honest in both directions, and it is the one that delays our own goal, which is why it is being written down now instead of on 08-22.  MECHANICAL TEST for could-not-reach-a-verdict, so this is not a judgment call later: the run's log carries an `error: fetch` line or UNREACHABLE claim lines, AND zero BROKEN claim lines, AND zero CHANGED/ADDED/ REMOVED mirror verdicts. That is precisely the signature of all six failures on 2026-08-17. A run with any BROKEN line or any mirror verdict DID reach a verdict and counts.  STATUS AS OF 2026-08-17: 25 of 25 days counted -- every scheduled run 07-24..08-17 reached a verdict (23 no-drift, 2 drift-detected), and all of them fired around 09:2x UTC, before today's outage window. Day 30 is 2026-08-22 IF runs 26-30 all reach verdicts. Each that does not moves the date out by one day.  NOT YET MECHANISED: a script that classifies each scheduled run against the test above and prints the streak day. It is a trusted-print instrument feeding a goal-close decision, so it routes through the cross-family review lane rather than being written on impulse -- and two of this lane's diffs are already queued there. Until it exists the classification is done by reading run logs, which is what produced the figures above. The RULE not existing was the risk; the script is a convenience.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-22, confirm leg (a) reached day 30 under the pre-registered streakDayRule (a day counts only if its scheduled run reached a verdict; a run that could not fetch PAUSES the clock rather than counting or resetting), then CLOSE G-1 citing David's 2026-08-20 approval. DO NOT RE-ASK HIM — he has already answered. If the streak paused and day 30 has not landed, say so plainly and close on the day it does; his approval is of the outcome, not of a date. On close, G-3 becomes Tier-0. THE CLOSING COMMIT CARRIES TWO MORE STEPS, both named here because a close procedure that stops at "mark it closed" is how this lane's stale-text pattern keeps recurring. (1) RE-POINT THE DAILY REPORT FRONTMATTER IN THE SAME COMMIT: north_star_metric, north_star_value, north_star_status and north_star_classification all still describe G-1, whose value is 1/green. G-3 will legitimately read ZERO for months. Left alone, the default outcome is a headline field reporting 1/green for a CLOSED goal while the live Tier-0 goal reads zero -- the most flattering possible number, and it means nothing. Orchestrator-approved 2026-08-21; the success signal is that the closing diff moves those fields and no daily ever renders the closed goal's value as its headline. (2) SWEEP FOR TEXT THAT CITED G-1 -- README, docs/lane-brief.md, docs/key-user-flows.md, the primer and any open item quoting "the 30-day streak" or "the north star" as a LIVE gate. This repo's own rule says closing a gate must include a sweep for text that cited it, and the rule has now failed FOUR times (F-2's public-flip blocker, A-7's private-repo claim, F-2's review-lane deferral, and A-16's own onTrigger, found stale in P2 on 2026-08-21). G-1 is the most-cited row in the repo, so this is the largest such sweep the lane will ever do. Do not skip it because the close feels ceremonial.
items.note_davidClose: DAVID APPROVED THE CLOSE, 2026-08-20: asked what he was waiting on, he answered "close it". THE APPROVAL IS RECORDED; THE STATUS IS NOT FLIPPED YET, and that is deliberate. Leg (a) requires the alarm armed and functioning for 30 CONSECUTIVE days, and today is day 28. Closing now would mark a goal complete two days before its own condition, which is precisely the self-marking this lane exists to refuse — and it would do it on the one goal whose entire point is that a claim rests on evidence. His approval means NO FURTHER APPROVAL IS NEEDED, not that the arithmetic changed.

items.note13: GATE DISPOSITIONED 2026-08-31. THE READ: run through the gate runner rather than by hand — node ../skylark-site/scripts/check-due-gates-dispositioned.mjs --run A-2 — exit 0 in 4836ms, output No drift. 113 files match upstream 3a1491040076a3f67a52719e366f5e6b139e5c24 (an upstream teorth/optimizationproblems sha; it does not resolve in this repo). NO CYCLE IS OWED. Upstream moved from 5c4aeee since 2026-08-25 without touching a mirrored byte, which is the case the new invariant clause on readCommand exists to stop anyone reading as drift. THE DECISION on note12 (the orchestrator standing-row-with-a-date question): NO schema change, and the population is now ONE, not two. A-2 never actually lacked a satisfiable condition — it had one (the adopted surface being dropped) sitting BEHIND four words that read as unsatisfiable, so this was a WORDING defect and closeWhen is reworded above. W-4 is the genuine case: Standing watch -- does not close, re-read before shipping any new detector, with no closing event named anywhere in it. So the fleet schema question the orchestrator raised is real but its population here is a single watch row, it remains LATENT (check-closewhen-drift still passes), and it still ships with its reader rather than as a lane edit — introducing a type nothing reads is the half-visible-to-two-instruments defect recorded 2026-08-28. WHY THE RUNNER HAD NEVER STAMPED THIS ROW, which was the more useful finding: 0 of 18 open rows carried readCommandLastRun, and the cause was not neglect. The runner executes the WHOLE readCommand field with shell # comments stripped, while this lane house-style writes command — prose after an em dash, so every row extracted 1267 bytes of prose as its command. Changing the separator from an em dash to # made the extraction exactly node scripts/reverify.mjs --check, 33 bytes, and it stamped on the first try. That is the convention for every readCommand from now on.

items.note2: PIN EXTENSION SHIPPED 2026-07-24 eve (David unheld the 7/23 feature hold in-pane, saying the hold had been accidental and to proceed): scripts/extract-pins.mjs generates 216 claim pins covering all 109 constants (1b.md stays hand-pinned as C-1/C-3) — ledger/claims.json now 7 hand + 216 generated = 223 claims, 222/222 fetchable HOLD live, C-7 UNVERIFIED by design. DESIGN DECISION: pins assert the LAST-LISTED row of each bounds table (verbatim raw line), NOT 'the record' — numeric record-ranking is defeated by symbolic cells ($K_{DR}+10^{-26}$), negatives, O(.) asymptotics (verified against the corpus; a min/max prototype mis-picked 10a/21a/41a), and auto-asserting 'record' 216x would put unverified statements in our own ledger. Last-listed is true by construction; an appended new record trips the mirror diff instead. NEW DISCIPLINE: after any deliberate --snapshot, re-run extract-pins.mjs and commit the regenerated pins — pins are the post-snapshot ratchet (a moved row stays BROKEN until deliberately re-pinned). check-claims.mjs now per-URL fetch-caches and counts (not lists) held claims so a real BREAK can't drown below the fold. items.note4: SECOND DRIFT 2026-07-28 21:57Z, 21 minutes after the first (937f4e5 -> c4f8386) — upstream pushed twice in ~20 min. constants/85a.md was another markdown-escape removal (\\{ -> \{, 1\_{B(H)} -> 1_{B(H)}); mathematically identical once unescaped. items.note9: SIXTH DRIFT CYCLE 2026-08-12 -- two record movements resolved in one cycle, both PURE RECORD MOVEMENT on named constants. NUMBERING CONVENTION, fixed here because this note originally said 'fifth and sixth drifts' and collided with d30d4e4 already being the fifth: COUNT RESOLUTION CYCLES (one commit that returns the mirror to green), not changed files and not upstream pushes, and state the file count inside the entry. The seven cycles are 50c8096, e856de9, 60a044e, da17be3, d30d4e4, ec01082, and the SEVENTH also on 2026-08-12 -- upstream pushed FOUR times today (400a9bb -> fe7bf53 -> 19694a8 -> 0ffbf1a) and cycle seven is a PRIORITY CORRECTION, a class we had not seen: no bound moved and 2a was already recorded as settled; what changed is WHO IS CREDITED with settling it, upstream adding a second independent claimed proof (Jin, preprints.org 202607.1919) posted eight days before Lorist-Schwenninger. Caught by CI going red on the very next push after cycle six resolved, with pin:2a:U BROKEN -- the alarm working, and an independent demonstration of the method lesson below. VERIFICATION TRAP WORTH KEEPING: preprints.org returns HTTP 200 for a 2673-byte bot-protection interstitial whose title is a non-breaking space and which contains the word Crouzeix zero times, so a status-code check would have recorded the citation as verified. Confirmed instead via CROSSREF CONTENT NEGOTIATION, which never touches the walled server: api.crossref.org/works/10.20944/preprints202607.1919.v1 returns title 'The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set' (which IS Crouzeix's conjecture stated as a theorem, so the subject matches although the name is absent), author Shanmu Jin, posted 2026-07-27, publisher MDPI AG, type posted-content -- confirming author, venue, date AND the priority claim (27 Jul precedes 4 Aug by eight days). Crossref is now the known route to citation metadata for a bot-walled preprint server. Cycle seven: 2 files, exactly 1 pin moved (pin:2a:U), ledger unchanged at 231/229/0/2. EIGHTH CYCLE followed within the hour (0ffbf1a -> 603052d): upstream reworked the same attribution paragraph a third time, Jin now primary with LS described as a second proof 'which acknowledges Jin'. 2 files, 1 pin (pin:2a:U). THE NEAR-MISS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING RECORDED TODAY: that acknowledgement clause is a checkable claim about a third party's paper, so it was checked -- the arXiv abs page for 2608.03841 shows only v1, comments '5 pages', and no mention of Jin; ar5iv then returned HTTP 200 / 38662 bytes with zero occurrences of 'Jin', and I was one step from writing that upstream's claim is unsupported, which would have been a public accusation about a real mathematician's paper on a repo we want taken seriously. Asserting the response IS the artifact caught it: ar5iv had FALLEN BACK TO THE ARXIV ABSTRACT PAGE (562 words, 'Skip to main content', 'View a PDF of the paper titled'). I had read the abstract page twice and drawn a conclusion from its silence. CORRECT STATE: upstream's acknowledgement claim is UNVERIFIED BY US, NOT CONTRADICTED -- we have not read the paper body and cannot from here without a PDF parser. GENERAL RULE, worth more than the incident: a POSITIVE match is self-validating (the content you wanted is present, as with Crossref returning Shanmu Jin); a NEGATIVE match proves nothing until you have separately proven you were looking at the right document. Before concluding 'X is absent from the source', check that something which MUST be there IS there -- here 'numerical range' and 'spectral set' were also absent, which for a paper about the numerical range being a spectral set should have been the tell. Twice in one day a 200 was not the artifact (preprints.org bot wall, then ar5iv fallback); the first was obvious junk, the second was real, relevant, correctly-titled HTML about the right paper and nearly passed. ON THE BURST: five upstream pushes in ~6 hours, three of them iterating one paragraph. A red run during an upstream editing burst is the alarm working and does NOT oblige same-minute resolution -- the mirror's contract is byte-fidelity at a known sha, not at every instant, and the 30-day streak is measured on the scheduled run. A lane whose product is noticing when numbers drift must not run two incompatible counters for its own headline figure -- and upstream pushed a THIRD time mid-resolution. Overnight scheduled run was green at 09:40Z (400a9bb, 112 files, 231 claims). Local check at 14:18Z red on 2 files: constants/10a.md + README.md, the real Grothendieck constant, BOTH ENDS improved by one paper -- lower K_DR+10^-12 (anchor ~1.67696) -> 6pi/11 ~ 1.71360, upper pi/(2ln(1+sqrt2))-6.039e-5 -> pi/(2ln(1+sqrt2))-10^-4, cited [SLXCKKM26] arXiv:2608.11158 (Saha/Li/Xue/Chaudhuri/Klivans/Kothari/Meka, 11 Aug 2026), settling the tenths digit of K_G as 7. VERIFIED BEFORE SNAPSHOT BY EXECUTION: primary source fetched HTTP 200 and the ABSTRACT STATES THE BRACKET VERBATIM (the opposite of the 2026-07-24 case where no cited abstract stated its bound -- do not generalise either way); 6pi/11 = 1.713595992867160 and pi/(2ln(1+sqrt2))-10^-4 = 1.782113978191369 both recomputed to match the stated decimals; the OLD formula pi/(2ln(1+sqrt2))-6.039e-5 = 1.782153588191369 reproduces the previous README decimal 1.78215358819137 to 15 sig figs, cross-checking our prior mirror state against upstream's closed form; both directions improve; [1.71360,1.78211] is inside [1.7,1.8) so the tenths-digit claim follows from the interval (we verify the interval forces the digit, NOT the theorems producing it); citation keys 12 used / 12 defined / 0 dangling and the old permuted key [LSXKKMC26] is fully absent, so a completed rename not a half-renamed state. NOT A DEFECT, recorded so it is not re-filed: upstream's note line says <= 1.78212 while the row says ~1.78211; the true value 1.782113978... rounds to 1.78211, and rounding an UPPER bound up is bound-safe, so 1.78212 is true. Second time a rounding convention has looked like a typo in this lane (W-2 Haugland was the first). SECOND DRIFT, caught four minutes later by the confirm-green run: constants/2a.md + README.md, Crouzeix's conjecture CLAIMED SOLVED -- upper 1+sqrt2 ~ 2.41421 [CP2017] -> 2 [LS2026], matching the trivial lower bound so C_2 = 2; arXiv:2608.03841 (Lorist, Schwenninger, 4 Aug 2026) fetched HTTP 200, title/authors/date match and the abstract describes exactly the method upstream paraphrases (perturbation lemma for 2-dilations applied to iterates f^n in the double-layer potential representation); keys 10/10, 0 dangling. WE DO NOT ASSERT THE CONJECTURE IS SETTLED -- upstream's own words are 'claimed proof' and '(claimed to be) settled', and our generated pins assert LISTING POSITION only. If the proof is withdrawn the row reverts and our alarm fires, which is correct. That is the pin rule earning its keep on the highest-profile row it has ever covered. RESOLVED: 400a9bb -> fe7bf53 -> 19694a8, mirror stays 112 files, exactly 3 generated pins moved (pin:10a:U, pin:10a:L, pin:2a:U -- read off the changed lines, not the diff hunk, which also shows pin:10b:U and pin:2a:L as unchanged context), ledger unchanged at 231 claims / 229 hold / 0 broken / 2 unverified. METHOD LESSON: a --snapshot proves the mirror matched upstream AT FETCH TIME, not now; the evidence of sync is an `npm run check` exiting 0 AFTER the last snapshot, read as an exit code and not through a pipe. Ending at the ratchet's own output would have committed 'drift resolved' over an already-stale mirror. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-12-two-record-movements-in-one-cycle.md

items.onTrigger: When the drift alarm goes red: run the drift cycle in CLAUDE.md — verify against PRIMARY sources first, then `npm run resnap` (snapshot + extract-pins + render-state-block, in that order), commit deliberately, close the GitHub issue naming the resolving sha, and log the cycle here. Never snapshot to silence the alarm. A red is the alarm working; editorial drift is still real drift.
items.nextCheckDateNote: DATED 2026-08-22 with nextCheckDate, NOT expectedSignalBy — same distinction applied to A-9 and W-4 the same day. A signal date promises a verdict and this row has none: it is the standing drift-resolution log and does not close. A re-read date promises only that someone looks. 2026-08-31 is the next Monday (CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this field read "2026-08-24 is the next Sunday" and 2026-08-24 is a MONDAY, as was the 08-17 pass it cites — the same weekday-label slip corrected in the 08-23 primer, found here by the W-7 instrument-audit step on its first run), matching the weekly forced-decision pass this row already records (see the weeklyPass2026_08_17 fields) — so the date describes a cadence that was ALREADY happening and was simply not machine-visible, rather than inventing a new obligation. It surfaced only after A-9 and W-4 were dated, because the checker reports against the ratio of dated rows; fixing two made the third visible. Worth noting as instrument behaviour: a warning list that shortens as you fix it can hide its own tail, so re-run after every fix rather than assuming one pass cleared the class.
items.note10: ELEVENTH DRIFT CYCLE, 2026-08-24 — editorial, six files, no record moved. The overnight scheduled run went RED at 09:30Z and filed issue #29; it sat unread for four and a half hours until the session opened, which is the cadence working at its designed resolution and not a miss. Upstream 5c4aeee (an upstream sha; it does not resolve in this repo), Terence Tao, 2026-08-23T18:13:55Z, "Fix inline-math rendering on six pages, and document the rule": escapes the markdown-active characters inside inline math on 10c, 16a, 3a, 53a, 56a and 85a, plus a rule written into upstream CONTRIBUTING.md, which is outside our mirror scope. PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION BEFORE SNAPSHOT: the upstream commit's own file list shows balanced additions/deletions per file (10c 5/5, 16a 1/1, 3a 1/1, 53a 7/7, 56a 1/1, 85a 3/3), so no table row was added or removed; every numeric value in the diff is byte-identical on both sides, with 7/64=0.109375 in 56a and 1.1835129324 in 3a named as the positive controls. Two generated pins broke on the escaping alone (pin:53a:L, pin:56a:U) and re-pin to the same numbers — the clearest demonstration yet of why editorial drift is real drift: the pin is a byte comparison, so a backslash moves it while the record does not. Full ratchet via npm run resnap; mirror 113 files at 5c4aeee, 233 claims, 231 hold, 2 UNVERIFIED (C-7/C-9, manual by design); npm run verify exit 0. Resolved at f5b5589, pushed. INSTRUMENT NOTE: issue #29 was AUTO-CLOSED by the green run at 14:01:56Z naming no resolving sha, so the repo rule "close naming the sha that resolved it" was satisfied mechanically while a reader learned that it ended and not how; the sha was added by hand as a comment. That is the same shape as the rest of this file's instrument findings and is the first entry logged under the W-7 cadence step adopted today.
items.readCommand:
node scripts/reverify.mjs --check # the drift alarm itself. Literal output 2026-08-25: "No drift. 113 files match upstream 5c4aeee95699d72e1603d04d0987b1a7b6097535." (that 40-hex token is an UPSTREAM teorth/optimizationproblems commit; it does not resolve in this repo), exit 0. Any non-zero exit means a cycle is owed and this row is the log for it. Positive control that the command can say otherwise: reverify.test.mjs plants synthetic drift in 10a.md every run and asserts it is detected, so the detecting path is exercised on every npm test. WHICH PART OF THE QUOTED LITERAL IS THE INVARIANT (added 2026-08-31): the invariant is the words No drift. plus the FILE COUNT. The 40-hex upstream sha in that sentence MOVES ON ITS OWN — upstream commits that touch no mirrored file change it while every mirrored byte holds, which is exactly what happened between 2026-08-25 (5c4aeee) and 2026-08-31 (3a14910), 113 files both times. A changed sha alone is NOT a catch and must not be read as one. Recorded because the 2026-08-25 rule that a verification note records literal output rather than a paraphrase — adopted to stop a false PASS — sets up a false ALARM wherever the literal contains a moving token, and the rule carried no clause saying which tokens those are.

items.title: Alarm files NO finding issue when the job fails before the drift/claims steps run (self-test failure path)
items.note: Found by the 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep by EXECUTING reverify.yml's `Open finding` body under GitHub's exact shell semantics (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`), not by reading it. When either self-test step fails, `finding.txt` is never created; the step's `cat finding.txt` then exits 1 under `-eo pipefail`, so the step dies BEFORE `gh issue create` and no finding issue is filed. Two consequences: (1) an instrument failure produces a red job but no issue — the drift alarm is silent about its own breakage, which is the same family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect; (2) the only diagnostic emitted is `cat: finding.txt: No such file or directory`, which points at the wrong thing. NOT a drift-masking bug: the job still goes red and the workflow-failure notification still fires, so a real drift is never hidden. Severity LOW. Evidence: with finding.txt absent the step exits 1; with a real synthetic drift present it produces title `Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)`, and with a real BROKEN claim it produces `Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)` — both branches of the title extractor verified FIRING against real tool output.
items.closeWhen: The Open-finding step either files a legibly-titled instrument-failure issue when finding.txt is absent, or a deliberate decision is recorded that a red job alone is sufficient for self-test failures.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25, same day, David-decided. He chose filing an instrument-failure issue over treating a red job as sufficient — rationale: a red CI run on a once-a-day lane is easy to scroll past, and the failure mode being hidden is our own instrument going quiet, which is precisely what this lane claims to catch. The Open-finding step now branches on `[ -s finding.txt ]`: with check output it behaves exactly as before ('Drift: <what moved>'); without it, it files 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (<date>)' with an explicit '(no check output — the job failed before the drift/claims steps ran)' body instead of dying at `cat` and filing nothing. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: the step body was extracted verbatim from the deployed YAML, the `gh issue create` call stripped, and run under GitHub's exact shell (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`) against all three real inputs — absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; real injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; real broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. No regression on the two paths that already worked; pipefail guard still passes (step keeps `shell: bash`).
items.note2: SUPERSEDED — read `resolution` above; this fix SHIPPED 2026-07-25 and is live in .github/workflows/reverify.yml (the `[ -s finding.txt ]` branch + the `Instrument failure:` title). Kept only as the pre-fix reasoning. ORIGINAL: READY FIX (deliberately NOT shipped in the sweep — it changes WHEN the alarm files, and the alarm surface is this lane's most load-bearing artifact; 7/24's lesson is that changes here get deliberated): guard the cat and make the title honest, e.g. `cat finding.txt 2>/dev/null || echo '(no check output — job failed before the drift/claims steps ran; see the failed step above)'` plus a title fallback that says instrument-failure rather than `Drift:`. Decide first whether a self-test failure SHOULD file an issue at all — arguably yes, since a steward whose instrument breaks silently is the exact failure mode this lane exists to prevent.

verifyBy.method: re-run the Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` with finding.txt absent and confirm it reaches the issue-create call with a non-misleading title

items.title: Alarm labelled a transient network failure 'Drift:' and omitted the reason entirely (production issue #2)
items.note: CAUGHT IN PRODUCTION 2026-07-25, not by review. CI run 30168372746 (push of 8856fb3, 17:48Z) failed and auto-filed issue #2 titled 'Drift: bounds-ledger re-verification (2026-07-25)' over a body reading '223 claim(s): 222 hold, 0 broken/unreachable' — self-contradictory. No record drifted: reverify.mjs --check hit a transient network error, printed 'error: fetch failed', exited 2; the claims step then ran via if:'!cancelled()' and everything held; the next push ten minutes later was green. TWO DEFECTS. (1) A tool error was titled 'Drift:', asserting a mathematical record moved when none did — the title extraction found no CHANGED/ADDED/REMOVED and no BROKEN/UNREACHABLE lines and fell through to the generic default, which is still prefixed 'Drift:'. (2) The reason was invisible: reverify.mjs reports errors via console.error (stderr) but the step piped only stdout (`| tee`), so 'error: fetch failed' reached the CI log and never the issue body. Same failure family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect from the opposite direction — that alarm could not speak, this one spoke and said the wrong thing. Cost model: a false 'Drift:' burns a reader's time hunting a record change that never happened, and repeated flakes train us to skim past Drift: issues, which is how a REAL drift gets missed. Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-25-alarm-called-a-network-flake-a-drift.md.
items.closeWhen: A tool/network error produces an honestly-titled issue that states the cause, and a real drift still titles as a drift.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25 same day. (a) `2>&1` added to both piped check steps so stderr lands in finding.txt and therefore in the issue body; (b) the title now branches three ways instead of falling through — 'Drift: <what moved>' on real drift/claim lines, 'Check error: … could not complete' when finding.txt contains an ^error: line, 'Re-verification failed' otherwise (A-4 supplies a fourth, 'Instrument failure', when finding.txt does not exist at all). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION under GitHub's exact shell (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail) against four real inputs including a byte-accurate replay of run 30168372746: replay => 'Check error: bounds-ledger re-verification could not complete (2026-07-25)'; absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. npm test green; all 5 piped workflow steps still carry shell: bash.
items.note2: RESOLVES TWO SWEEP UNKNOWNS, for free and within the hour. The 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep marked the composite CI failure path (if: failure() -> gh issue create) and if:'!cancelled()' on the claims step as UNKNOWN, because closing them would have required pushing a corrupted mirror. Production answered both: the issue-filing path FIRES (issue #2 exists) and !cancelled() FIRES (claim output appears in the body although the mirror step had already failed) — and the output was WRONG, which a green could never have revealed. Method lesson worth keeping: the honest UNKNOWN left the question open, so the evidence was recognised when it arrived; a fabricated green would have closed it and issue #2 would have been read as a real drift.
items.note3: DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: retry/backoff on a transient fetch failure. One flake in four days does not justify it, and suppressing the alarm is the wrong direction. If check-error issues become frequent, add retry inside reverify.mjs — never silence the step.

verifyBy.method: replay the deployed Open-finding body under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` against a finding.txt containing an ^error: line and confirm the title says Check error, not Drift

items.note4: RECURRED AND RE-FIXED 2026-08-17, and the recurrence says this item was CLOSED ON A PARTIAL FIX. A-5 closeWhen reads "a tool/network error produces an honestly-titled issue that states the cause". That was true of the path A-5 actually examined -- an ^error: line in finding.txt -- and false of the other path into the same failure. check-claims.mjs reports a source it could not fetch as UNREACHABLE, and the title extractor grouped UNREACHABLE with BROKEN. Those are different events: BROKEN means the cited source WAS read and the pinned string was gone (a record moved); UNREACHABLE means it was never read. Because UNREACHABLE populated , it matched BEFORE the elif that tests for ^error:, so the A-5 fix was unreachable code for this input class -- reverify own "error: fetch constants/11a.md: 429" sat in the same finding.txt, unread.  FOUND IN PRODUCTION, not by a check, and while doing something else: dispatching reverify.yml on the held guard branch (workflow_dispatch is the ONLY route -- the workflow declares push: branches:[main], so a feature branch gets zero runs from pushing). The job hit HTTP 429 from raw.githubusercontent.com and filed issue #15 titled "Drift: claims C-1,pin:12a:U pin:37a:U,pin:37a:L pin:3c:U,pin:3c:L" -- asserting six records moved. A local npm run check four minutes earlier read 113 files in sync and 231 of 233 claims holding, so zero had. A second dispatch filed #17 naming ~30 pins.  SECOND, LATENT DEFECT IN THE SAME LINE: paste -sd", " does not join with ", ". -d takes a LIST of delimiters applied CYCLICALLY, so 3+ items came out "a,b c,d". Visible in #15 own title, and latent in every multi-file drift title before it (2 items consume only the first delimiter, which is why nobody saw it). Fixed with paste -sd, - | sed s/,/, /g.  FIX: precedence is now mirror movement (CHANGED/ADDED/REMOVED) -> claim movement (BROKEN) -> unreachable sources -> tool error -> generic, and UNREACHABLE gets its own title, "Check error: bounds-ledger could not reach N cited source(s)". GUARDED in reverify.test.mjs, which EXTRACTS the step body from the deployed YAML rather than restating it -- a copy would test the transcription and not the alarm, which is A-4 method. Seven cases under GitHub exact shell, including that a real move OUTRANKS a concurrent flake (a 429 must never mask a genuine drift). Negative control: restoring UNREACHABLE to the drift group fails the test, mutation proven to land first (git diff --numstat 20 2).  THE GUARD FOOLED ITSELF FIRST AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING: its first version resolved bash from PATH, which this machine PowerShell does not have. The spawn failed, the harness returned an empty string, and assert.doesNotMatch(title, /^Drift:/) PASSED ON THE EMPTY STRING -- a guard reporting success because it had not run. KP-78 is usually read as "prove it fires"; this is the other half, prove that a non-firing result means the CONDITION is absent rather than the INSTRUMENT. It now asserts a title was emitted at all, resolves bash via git --exec-path, and prints SKIPPED naming what went unchecked if it cannot -- the same refusal to launder an unanswerable question into a pass that the manual:true claims (UNVERIFIED), the brief check (UNVERIFIABLE) and the shallow-clone catch count (UNKNOWN) already make.  THE RED WAS CORRECT AND STAYS CORRECT. An unreachable source means we could not verify; a green there would launder an unverifiable into a pass. Only the title was wrong and only the title changed. Do NOT make 429 non-fatal. Whether the fetch layer should RETRY on 429 is a separate and real question -- that extends reach rather than softening a verdict -- and it touches two trusted instruments network paths, so it belongs behind the cross-family review lane.  CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (this note first asserted SELF-INFLICTED CAUSE, recorded: I caused the rate limit -- THAT WAS WRONG and is retracted). Two dispatches in ten minutes, ~220 fetches each, on top of the daily scheduled run. Dispatching this workflow spends a shared budget the SCHEDULED run depends on, and the first run had already answered the question. Also: a throwaway debug one-liner escaping failed to strip gh issue create before executing the step body and filed a real issue (#16) against the public repo, closed within minutes; the in-repo harness asserts the strip succeeded before running anything, the debug script did not.  HOUSEKEEPING DONE THE SAME DAY: seven issues closed, open count now 0 (verified via REST after the GraphQL listing returned 503 -- a failed query is not evidence of absence). Five of them (#10-#14) were RESOLVED drifts from 11/12/14 August that nobody closed at resolution time, each closed naming its resolving commit (d30d4e4, ec01082, 4d06395, 433091b). Five standing Drift: issues on a repo whose pitch is noticing stale things teaches the next reader that Drift: issues can be ignored, which is the precondition for missing a real one. CLOSING ON RESOLUTION IS PART OF THE DRIFT CYCLE, not optional tidying.  STATUS: fix committed on branch alarm-title-honesty (4153c00), NOT merged -- held for the cross-family review lane, because the alarm issue title is the most-read line this repo produces and is squarely in the trusted-print class. Merge it BEFORE guard-catch-count-v2 so main alarm is honest before any push-triggered run can mis-title a flake. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-17-the-alarm-called-a-rate-limit-a-record-movement.md
items.note5: ATTRIBUTION RETRACTION 2026-08-17, filed the same day and worth more than the fix it corrects. note4 above, the finding, the commit message, CLAUDE.md gotcha and two issue-closing comments all stated flatly that I CAUSED the rate limit by dispatching reverify.yml twice in ten minutes. THAT ATTRIBUTION IS RETRACTED. GitHub was in a CRITICAL OUTAGE from 2026-08-17T13:40:03.629Z -- verified by reading githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents/unresolved.json directly rather than inheriting the orchestrator broadcast; impact critical, Actions degraded from 13:42Z, roughly 20% error rates across API / Issues / PRs / Actions. MY FIRST DISPATCH WAS 14:32Z, FIFTY-TWO MINUTES AFTER THE OUTAGE BEGAN, and Actions was already degraded before it.  THREE PIECES OF DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE WERE IN HAND AT THE TIME AND WERE NOT ASSEMBLED: (1) a LOCAL npm run check issuing ~450 raw fetches ran FULLY GREEN at 14:28Z -- 48 minutes into the outage and four minutes before the first dispatch, so volume was plainly not yet the problem; (2) a LATER local check 429d, and my dispatches were RUNNER-side, sharing no egress with this machine, so they cannot explain a residential-IP failure; (3) the errors included 502 AND 503, which no volume of requests produces. I actually WROTE "the 502 is not explainable that way" in a bus note and left the self-blame standing everywhere else.  WHAT SURVIVES: two dispatches in ten minutes is still poor practice -- each run is ~450 requests -- and the do-not-dispatch-repeatedly guidance stands. It stands as PRACTICE, not as the diagnosis of this incident. b1 (pull_request trigger, shipped today) removes most of the reason to dispatch at all.  WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE TITLE FIX IT SITS BESIDE: this lane exists to catch confident causal stories attached to record movements that were never verified. I published one about my own infrastructure, in the same document where I fixed the alarm for doing the equivalent. SELF-BLAME FELT LIKE RIGOUR AND WAS JUST ANOTHER UNVERIFIED ATTRIBUTION -- and it is the more seductive kind, because nobody challenges you for blaming yourself. The repo already had the governing rule: a POSITIVE CONTROL before any absence or cause claim. Apply it to causes you find flattering to admit.  CI CONSEQUENCE, per the fleet incident guidance: every CI conclusion in the 13:40Z-onward window is UNKNOWN, never red and never green. The two PR runs that completed success at 16:11Z did execute every step including the network legs -- positive evidence, and a positive match is self-validating -- but they are recorded UNKNOWN-with-timestamp rather than green, because a conclusion drawn from a majorly-degraded Actions service is not one this repo should lean on. Note the RED-vs-CODE distinction still holds separately: the run correctly reported it could not verify, which is our alarm working, and is not a verdict about our code either way.

items.title: OPPORTUNITY: adopt erdosproblems.com as the second stewarded surface — and route corrections as PRs to teorth/erdosproblems instead of email
items.note: Filed 2026-07-25. VERIFIED FACTS: (a) github.com/teorth/erdosproblems is PUBLIC and actively maintained (pushed 2026-07-25T17:27Z, ~16.7MB), described as the community database behind erdosproblems.com — reachable from anywhere via api.github.com/raw, so it is NOT affected by the site's datacenter-IP block; (b) it ships data/problems.yaml (396KB, 19742 lines), schema/, scripts/ and a 21KB CONTRIBUTING.md, i.e. it ACCEPTS CONTRIBUTIONS; (c) problems.yaml carries METADATA only (number, prize, status, oeis, formalized, tags) — the numeric bounds live in the site page prose/LaTeX. CORRECTION vs this item's first draft: I initially wrote that the whole site is machine-readable. It is not, from CI — erdosproblems.com 403s datacenter IPs (see W-3 note2). The GITHUB REPO is machine-readable from anywhere; the SITE is only readable from a residential IP. Any design here must be built on the repo, not on scraping the site from CI.
items.note2: WHY THIS MATTERS FOR G-1, which is the real point. G-1 needs at least one EXTERNALLY-ACKNOWLEDGED correction and that metric is currently 0, resting entirely on one email to one busy maintainer who owes us nothing. Two independent improvements are now available: (1) SCALE THE CATCHES — erdosproblems.com is the most-used index in the field and we already know it goes stale (that is the lane founding finding). Systematically diffing its bounds against Tao curated table across many problems turns one lucky catch into a repeatable pipeline of correction candidates. (2) CHANGE THE CHANNEL — a PR against a community database with a CONTRIBUTING.md is mechanically reviewable and leaves a public, dated, attributable record. An accepted PR IS an external acknowledgement, and unlike an email it cannot be silently ignored into ambiguity. Email put the north-star metric behind an inbox; a PR puts it behind a merge button.
items.note3: SEQUENCING / CAUTION. Real feature build, not cleanup — do not start it inside a close-out. items.note5: FOUR OF THE FIVE CONTROLS SHIPPED 2026-08-09, commit 0a29081 — the orchestrator answered the same day the escalation went out and ruled under default-decision authority: proceed per-repo now, do NOT wait for the self-imposed 8/16 date, the Stage-0 wave treats already-set config as idempotent. Its escalate-if (cross-repo coordination / paid plan / credential mint) was checked against each control and NONE tripped it — branch protection is free on a PUBLIC repo, which is the constraint that had parked it while private. EVIDENCE IS gh api OUTPUT, per the ruling, not a settings page. R16: repository ruleset `main-history-integrity` id 20607202, `enforcement: active`, `bypass_actors: []`, `current_user_can_bypass: never`, rules `[deletion, non_fast_forward]`, include `[~DEFAULT_BRANCH]`. No required-review rule and that is deliberate: single contributor, so requiring PRs adds friction without adding a reviewer. A future deliberate history rewrite must now disable the ruleset first — intended friction on an irreversible action, and worth knowing before someone reads a rejected push as a broken remote. R5: `git config core.hooksPath` → `.githooks`; the hook runs `history-sweep.mjs --staged`, a NEW MODE OVER THE SAME PATTERN SET rather than a second scanner — two secret matchers drift apart and the one nobody watches is the one that goes quiet. R4: repo-health.json at root (4967 bytes, readable via the contents API), written for a PUBLIC reader — it states the controls that are in place and names gaps by tracker ID only, deliberately publishing no weakness inventory, because doing exactly that was one of the eight blockers of the 2026-08-05 pre-publication review. R17/R18: package-lock.json committed (189 bytes) and CI now runs `npm ci`; the dependency set is empty so it installs nothing today, which is the point — `npm ci` fails on a package.json/lockfile mismatch, so a future package must arrive with its lockfile entry. DEMONSTRATED BOTH WAYS at the real boundary, not just against the function: ordinary prose staged → CLEAN exit 0; a planted ghp_ token staged → `git commit` REFUSED exit 1 with nothing landing; and our own real commit of this work printed CLEAN as it went through. The ruleset's silent half is demonstrated too — the push of 0a29081 was a fast-forward and succeeded.
items.note6: ONE DEMONSTRATION IS OWED ON R16, and it is not being quietly skipped. Proving the ruleset FIRES requires attempting a real force-push, and the Claude Code auto-mode classifier REFUSED that command. Per the 2026-08-08 standing rule I did not substitute a smaller equivalent operation (a rewind push, a rebase, an amend) to get around the refusal — that defeats the gate's intent, and the hand-off is a ~2-minute detour. So the state read stands as evidence that the rule is CONFIGURED AND ACTIVE and is NOT evidence that it fires, exactly the distinction drawn for secret scanning and push protection on 8/08. THE OWED DEMONSTRATION, one command, safe and recoverable: `git push --force origin HEAD~1:main` — expected to be REJECTED with a ruleset violation; if it somehow succeeded, main rewinds one commit and `git push origin main` restores it in seconds. David can run it with the in-session `! <command>` form. DELIBERATELY NOT ATTEMPTED, and this is a scoping judgment rather than an oversight: the `deletion` rule was not separately exercised, because the failure mode of an unenforced test is deleting main on a public repo, and a probe licenses its own claim and nothing wider (the 8/04 F-4 lesson) — so do NOT read a demonstrated non-fast-forward rejection as proof the deletion rule fires.

redProofWaived.reason: R16 FIRE DEMONSTRATION WAIVED 2026-08-09 by orchestrator ruling, with reason recorded rather than the requirement quietly dropped. GROUNDS: the rule-suite records are WITHIN-PATH evidence, a rung above a config read — suites 3612293601 and 3612300581 (both `result: pass`, refs/heads/main) show GitHub's enforcement engine adjudicating every push to main, so the rule is demonstrably in the push path and not merely present in settings. Producing a REJECTION would require attempting exactly the operation the ruleset exists to prevent; the Claude Code classifier refuses it, and the ruling explicitly endorsed the refusal to substitute a smaller equivalent operation. DIRECTED NOT TO HAND THIS TO DAVID — the `! git push --force origin HEAD~1:main` ask named in note6 is WITHDRAWN; do not re-raise it with him. WHAT THIS WAIVER DOES AND DOES NOT SAY, because a waiver that blurs into a demonstration is worse than an open gap: it accepts within-path evaluation as sufficient for THIS control, on THIS repo, where the fire test is itself the hazard. It does not establish that a control may be recorded as demonstrated on a state read, and it does not extend to the `deletion` rule (never exercised) or to secret scanning / push protection (enabled 8/08, still never seen to fire, still excluded from closeWhen by design). If the enforcement path is ever seen to reject a push, capture the `result: fail` suite row — GitHub's record outlives our transcript.

items.title: KP-78 applies to every new detector: demonstrate BOTH sides at write time
items.note: Filed from the 2026-07-31 KP-78 audit (docs/findings/2026-07-31-kp78-prove-the-instrument-can-fail.md). Audited all four detectors in the lane: the drift check and the claim matcher were already two-sided by construction; the pipefail guard had a never-demonstrated fire side (demonstrated 7/31, it fires and names the offending step); and the audit surfaced a detector that did not exist at all -- A-8 (1ec47ce, shipped 7/30) added the pin-extractor self-test to CI as a hand-added YAML step with nothing asserting it stays, so deleting it would have been silent and would have looked exactly like the six unguarded days it just fixed. Built that guard (reverify.test.mjs, derives the expected set from package.json so a newly-added self-test cannot be CI-less either) and demonstrated it both ways. THE WATCH: any future detector here -- test, guard, lint, probe, --check mode, alarm -- ships only with both outputs recorded, and the mutation proved landed via git diff --numstat first (a negative control written with \\n against CRLF files silently no-ops and produces a FALSE inert verdict, which is how the pipefail guard was wrongly pronounced broken on 2026-07-25). || EXERCISED 2026-08-11 on the pin-a-negative detector (A-11, 7018cce), and the demonstration went beyond the usual bar in one way worth keeping: the selftest drives the SHIPPED classify() rather than a copy of its logic, so the branch that is tested is provably the branch that runs. Four cases (silent when the pinned row is still last, FIRES on an inserted row, reads a REPLACED row as gone rather than as an addition, and leaves claims without nothingAfter behaving exactly as before), plus a live-bytes control that fetched both real sources, spliced an entry below each pin, and aborted if the splice failed to land (the CRLF no-op trap). Both sources read `hold` untouched and `added` mutated.

items.onTrigger:
When you are about to ship anything whose job is to DETECT (test, guard, lint, probe, --check mode, alarm), before committing: (1) construct the condition it exists to catch and confirm it FIRES, naming what it printed; (2) restore and confirm it goes SILENT; (3) prove the mutation actually landed with git diff --numstat BEFORE believing either result -- a control written with 
 against these CRLF files silently no-ops and manufactures a false inert verdict (2026-07-25); (4) paste both outputs into the commit message or finding doc. If nothing in the repo currently trips it, build a fixture that does -- a detector validated only against a clean world tells you nothing. Then ask the second question, which is NOT the same: can it see the SHAPE of failure that matters, or only one direction of it? (2026-07-31: both detectors passed can-it-fire and both were blind to a class this lane exists to catch.) Finally: is it wired into something that RUNS on its own? A check only in npm scripts is not a detector.
items.note9: EXERCISED 2026-08-12 on render-state-block.mjs (3f0abce), and the demonstration was run on the REAL README rather than only a fixture: current -> in sync exit 0; mutate the sha -> git diff --numstat shows 8 3 README.md proving the mutation LANDED (the CRLF trap); stale -> STALE exit 1; repaired -> in sync exit 0. Its selftest additionally proves it fires on a stale COUNT (not just a sha), raises on missing markers, and that its own mutations land. Orchestrator held the bar explicitly when approving the build: a generator that cannot go red silently agrees with whatever is already written, which is the exact failure it exists to prevent.

items.title: Audit latency-derived constants + threshold detectors against post-model-swap behavior (orchestrator P2 rider 7/31)
items.note: DEFERRED ON ARRIVAL per the dispatch (do not process on receipt; log as a P2 item). NOTE: this lane is LITE RAIL and has no P2 continuity phase, so the trigger is the NEXT DAILY rather than a phase boundary -- logged with an explicit trigger so it is not silently dropped, which is the failure mode the rider itself is about. THE CLASS: a threshold derived from a measurement of the OLD regime keeps reading as authoritative after the regime changes, and the whole fleet swapped models on 7/30. Anchors: frame-dial killed a digest because a do-not-push clock fence measured against gpt-5.4 wall-clock was ~45min wrong after builds roughly doubled on claude-opus-5; agentic-news hook canary reported CLEAR on a 2.38 SD quality drop because a fixed threshold vs a 7-run trailing mean is structurally incapable of firing on a single-day cliff. THE ASK: (1) inventory every constant that is a MEASUREMENT not a POLICY -- timeouts, stall thresholds, cron spacing, retry backoffs, quiet windows, any if(ageMinutes > N); (2) per constant, one line: what was N measured against, what is that behavior now; (3) fix by RE-KEYING TO OBSERVABLE STATE, not re-numbering (a re-numbered constant is the same bug with a fresh expiry date); only re-number when no observable state exists, and then write the measurement date + the model it was measured against next to the number; (4) run the pass-3 check on each detector touched -- can this instrument report the condition it exists to detect? If it has a blind class, say so in its name or comment; (5) report counts inventoried/stale/re-keyed-vs-re-numbered plus any load-bearing on a send/publish/customer path. PRIOR EXPECTATION, to be verified not assumed: this lane looks nearly empty of latency-derived constants -- no LLM calls, no retries/backoffs, no stall detector, and the cron 17 9 * * * is a POLICY choice not a measurement -- so honest zero-stale is the likely answer, but the dispatch requires saying WHAT WAS CHECKED rather than skipping silently. Pass-3 is the live angle worth real time here: this lane IS detectors, and W-4/KP-78 already covers can-it-fire, but blind-CLASS (can it see the shape of failure that matters) is a different question than can-it-fire at all. || CLOSED 2026-07-31, run early at David request rather than deferred. RESULT: 7 constants inventoried, 0 stale, 0 re-keyed, 0 re-numbered, 0 load-bearing on a send path (no send path exists). The rider regime change cannot reach this lane -- zero LLM calls, so nothing here was ever measured against model latency. The prior expectation held, but the dispatch was right to require a named list: the sweep found real defects elsewhere. STEP 4 IS WHERE THE VALUE WAS: two blind classes in the two production detectors, both of which PASS KP-78. BC-1 reverify.mjs fired with a completely EMPTY report body on any set-identical change (row reorder / duplicated line) -- A-5 defect surviving inside the finding that closed A-5, and load-bearing because generated pins assert the LAST-LISTED row, so a reorder changes what 218 pins mean while the report says nothing. FIXED, both sides demonstrated. BC-2 check-claims.mjs is a PRESENCE test so it can only see a pin disappear, never an ADDITION -- covered for the 218 generated pins (sources mirrored, reverify sees additions) but NOT for the six off-mirror claims C-4/C-5/C-6/C-7/C-8/C-9 where it is the only instrument, and a new record appearing is this lane north-star event. NAMED in the instrument + pinned by a passing selftest assertion; NOT fixed, because the remedy is a design call (mirror those sources vs pin a negative) that belongs to David/orchestrator. Full account: docs/findings/2026-07-31-a10-constants-and-blind-classes.md

items.title: BC-2 accepted as a documented blind class (option c); pin-a-negative for the two STRUCTURED sources still open
items.note: Split out of A-10 rather than fixed inside it, because the remedy is a design decision not a code tweak. THE GAP: holds() is a presence test, so check-claims can only ever report a pinned string DISAPPEARING. A source that keeps the pinned text and ADDS a new better bound below it stays green forever. For the 218 generated pins this is covered -- their sources are mirrored and reverify.mjs reports any added line. It is NOT covered for the six claims whose sources are off-mirror: C-4/C-5 (arXiv), C-6 (Wikipedia), C-7/C-9 (erdosproblems.com), C-8 (teorth/erdosproblems). On those six, check-claims is the ONLY instrument, and A NEW RECORD APPEARING IS THIS LANE NORTH-STAR EVENT -- the exact thing the ledger exists to catch is the thing it cannot see there. Same shape as the agentic-news canary that reported CLEAR on a 2.38 SD drop. THE OPTIONS, none taken: (a) byte-mirror those sources too -- A-6 territory, and erdosproblems.com is the CI-blocked 403 surface so it can never be mirrored from CI; (b) pin a NEGATIVE (assert no table row exists below the cited one) -- works for the structured sources C-6/C-8, not for prose; (c) accept it and document the blind class as permanent. Currently NAMED in the instrument (comment on holds() + a passing selftest assertion that pins the shape) so it cannot be silently forgotten, which is the minimum, not the fix. || DECIDED 2026-07-31 BY ME, not by David — recorded here so this item stops reading as a David-blocker. Applying the poll check (did we ever actually ASK him?): no board card was ever created, so this was never a David-blocker, it was a question we never sent. And option (c) was already in force — the blind class is named on holds() and pinned by a passing selftest assertion. DEFAULT TAKEN: (c), accepted and documented. items.note10: FIRST-PR TARGETS FOUND 2026-08-05 — note5's gap is closed. note5 recorded that the three named candidates (#129/#130/#135) merged 8/02 and the correction-shaped-PR channel was left with NO target. It now has ten, across six files, verified live at mirror dee1660 (== upstream HEAD, confirmed by the same morning's clean --check). THE CLASS: citation-key integrity — a key used as [Tag] in a bounds table or in prose with no matching entry in that page's own ## References section. Nine of the ten are 1:1 near-miss pairs (used [O2013] / defined [Olsen2013]; [Ta2004]/[Tao2004]; [PG25]/[P25]; [AS2000]/[AC2000]; and five inside 15a.md alone — [BCRL1979]/[BCRL79], [L2014]/[LG2014], [DWZ23]/[DWZ2022], [WXXZ24]/[VXXZ2023], [ADWXXZ25]/[ADVXXZ2024]), which is the signature of a transcription slip rather than a missing citation; 10a.md's [LSXKKMC26] is the one genuine orphan with no partner. WHY THIS CLASS: it is the profile of the two real drifts the mirror has caught (both editorial — a dead cross-link, a missing C in LaTeX), i.e. exact / local / one-file / mechanically checkable with ZERO literature risk, which is what survives note2's acceptance hierarchy where PR #72 was rejected solely for insufficient literature despite shipping certificates. RECOMMENDED TARGET: 15a.md alone (matrix multiplication exponent, five defects, one of the most-consulted pages in the inventory); the other five files follow only after a first acceptance. DIRECTION OF FIX IS NOT UNIFORM AND THIS IS THE REVIEW'S JOB: reading each page's own convention, 15a's table is wrong for LG2014/VXXZ2023/ADVXXZ2024 but its REFERENCE is wrong for BCRL79 (two-digit year in a four-digit file) — a patch that pushed all ten one direction would be wrong in at least two places. INSTRUMENT NOTE, the real lesson: the scan reported 532, then 41, then 36, then 6, and the first three were all MY PARSER — the corpus uses three reference formats (- [T], * [T], and - **[T]**) and I matched one. The tell was that a genuine rename defect produces a PAIR, so files reporting N-undefined/0-unused were parser artifacts; 41-of-111 basic citation breakage in a Tao-curated repo was never plausible. Suspect the instrument before the record, again. NOTHING DRAFTED, NOTHING SENT — a PR is outward contact: adversarial refute-it review then David's gate, both still owed, and the scan must be re-run immediately before any draft (targets here go stale inside a day). SCANNER DELIBERATELY NOT COMMITTED: it would become a detector owing a W-4 both-sides demonstration, and a sixth --selftest in package.json fails reverify.test.mjs until a matching CI step exists — a real feature, not a selection increment. Source pasted in the finding so the result is reproducible. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-05-citation-key-integrity-first-pr-targets.md

items.note20: HISTORY REWRITE DONE 2026-08-07 eve, David approved at the pane. git-filter-repo over all 119 commits: author+committer email (David's personal address, redacted here — see note21) -> 58274543+u00dxk2@users.noreply.github.com, 15 Claude-Session trailers -> 0, .playwright-mcp forum snapshot objects 2 -> 0, commit count unchanged. THE TRAP, worth more than the rewrite itself: the rewrite succeeded and THE VERY NEXT COMMIT RE-CONTAMINATED THE REPO — the SHA-remap commit was authored after filter-repo ran, using the repo git config which still held the personal address, and a fresh clone showed 1 contaminated hit. LOCAL CHECKS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT because they ran before that commit existed; only cloning the REMOTE did. Anyone setting this repo up on another machine must set the local identity FIRST. SHA REFERENCES: 244 remapped across 36 files from filter-repo commit-map, because a lane about references staying correct cannot leave a trail of dead ones. HAZARD: a 7-40 hex regex also matches numeric literals (README cites 2.6273856, tail 6273856 looks exactly like a short sha), so a collision would have SILENTLY REWRITTEN A RECORD VALUE. Verified it did not: all 710 decimal literals across 63 doc files byte-identical before/after. That verification FAILED TWICE SILENTLY first, both times looking like a result — Windows Python cannot resolve MSYS /tmp paths, so the original side read empty and the check compared against nothing, then the negative control reported INERT for the same reason (a FALSE inert verdict, the CRLF class arriving by a new mechanism). Redone via git+sed with the mutation proven to land: FIRES on one altered digit, SILENT on real data. Remote verified by FRESH CLONE: 120 commits, one noreply identity, 0 personal-address hits, 0 session URLs, 0 snapshot objects.
