items.title: C_87's record row cites a witness whose arithmetic yields the PREVIOUS record — verified, unreported, needs review + David's gate
items.note: Found during the 2026-08-14 drift cycle, in the constant upstream added that same morning (e70b4a4, an upstream sha; it does not exist in this repo). constants/87a.md's record row says rd <= 3^4*5^4*7^4*13^2*29^4*53^2*109^2 <= 857.5662. That product is 484887097019201067725625, a 24-digit integer, so the inequality as typeset is false and the root notation is missing. Supplying the 8th root the sentence itself invites (an 8-th root class-field tower, 2-class group of rank 8) gives 913.492694, which to six significant figures is 913.493 -- the value on the [Mar2006] row directly above it. No integer degree yields 857.5662 (the required degree is 8.0748), and single-factor transcription slips do not explain the gap (the needed product is 2.926e23 against the stated 4.849e23, a ratio of 1.657, which is not a prime power). WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the row is internally inconsistent, by exact integer arithmetic on the page's own text, with the factorization re-extracted mechanically from the mirror rather than re-typed. WHAT IS NOT: what [HMR2019] actually proves. arXiv:1901.04354 is the right paper (positive control: its abstract independently names the refined Golod-Shafarevich criterion, the mechanism the row cites) but states no numeric value, the same wall three abstracts put up on 2026-07-24. So the defect is in the WITNESS, not necessarily in the bound, and two readings survive: the factorization belongs to the [Mar2006] row, or it is the right construction with a different error. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-14-the-witness-attached-to-c87s-record-row-proves-the-previous-record.md. NOTE THE ALARM DID NOT CATCH THIS AND WAS NOT MEANT TO -- the mirror is byte-faithful including the defect; this came from reading a newly added page by hand, which has no detector behind it. *** GATE 1 CLEARED 2026-08-15: adversarial refute-it review run as an independent CROSS-MODEL pass (Codex, told to refute and to default to refuted under uncertainty, recomputing from the mirrored file rather than from our prose). Doc: docs/decisions/2026-08-15-A16-adversarial-review.md. VERDICT SURVIVES on all six angles, with ONE amendment and ONE residual risk. Independently recomputed and matching ours exactly: product 484887097019201067725625, eighth root 913.4926943720098688908, required degree ln(X)/ln(857.5662) = 8.074831 which is not an integer, neighbouring integer roots 913.4926943720 and 428.2899143899. THE REVIEW WENT FURTHER THAN WE DID on the transcription-slip angle: 275 one-edit candidates (dropped prime powers, exponents off by one, transposed digits) swept against integer degrees 1-64, none rounding or truncating to 857.5662 or 857.567; nearest misses 796.278, 823.480, 854.740; degrees above 64 excluded by bound (the largest candidate root there is below 2.524) rather than by sampling. Our hand-checked version of that angle now rests on a systematic sweep. AMENDMENT APPLIED: angle 6 rated the CONCLUSION overclaimed if headlined as 'proves the previous record' -- the arithmetic establishes internal inconsistency plus an eighth root equal to the row above, which is not a claim about Martin's construction. The body already refused to choose and the reviewer found no line inside it that overclaims; the gap is that a reader quoting only the TITLE inherits the stronger claim. The finding now carries a 'What we would say upstream' paragraph fixing the limited sentence in advance rather than composing it at send time. RESIDUAL RISK NAMED AND CLOSED: the reviewer's one worry was that upstream might already have corrected the page. npm run check at 2026-08-15T14:59Z reports no drift, 113 files matching upstream e70b4a4, so 87a.md is byte-identical to the live upstream file and the defect is uncorrected. RE-RUN THAT CHECK IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY SEND -- reporting an error the maintainer has already fixed is worse than not reporting at all. CARRIED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT ADOPTED: the reviewer states the arXiv full text assigns this factorization to Martin's construction and derives the new record by a different route, which if true resolves the two open readings in favour of 'attached to the wrong row'. Not adopted, because we have not read the paper body from this pane and on 2026-08-12 this lane came one step from publishing a false claim about a mathematician's paper on the strength of a fetch that had silently fallen back to an abstract page. A full-text claim needs a positive control naming the token that proves the document was the right one. Nothing is lost by holding it -- the finding stands without it. GATE 2 (David's explicit approval) NOT ASKED and not urgent: per the 2026-08-15 dispatch, nothing goes outward on this lane's own initiative.

items.note_primarySource: THE REVIEW READ THE PAPER WE HAD DELIBERATELY REFUSED TO READ, AND I VERIFIED IT MYSELF BEFORE ADOPTING ANY OF IT, because on 2026-08-12 this lane came one step from publishing a false claim about a mathematician paper on a fetch that had silently fallen back to an abstract page. TWO CONTROLS, both passed. (1) Arithmetic: 770.6432 * 13^(1/24) = 857.566203 against the page 857.5662 — a base value and a 24th-root-of-13 factor are not confabulated onto the page own number by chance. (2) Fetch: the ABSTRACT page (39 KB) contains none of 857.5662 / 913.49 / 770.6432, while the FULL TEXT (1.18 MB) contains all three plus the control tokens "Cutting towers" and "root discriminant" — which is precisely the distinguisher the 8/12 incident lacked. Read from this pane, not taken on trust.
items.note_whatThePaperSays: ESTABLISHED, no longer a choice between two readings. HMR section 3.3.1, verbatim: "Its discriminant is 3^4 . 5^4 . 7^4 . 13^2 . 29^4 . 53^2 . 109^2 and the root discriminant is less than 913.4927" — that factorization is a DISCRIMINANT of MARTIN degree-8 field, and its 8th root rounds to the 913.493 on the row ABOVE. HMR section 3.3.3 is where 857.5662 comes from and it is a DIFFERENT, degree-12 totally real field: rd_K < 770.6432, then rd . 13^(1/12 . (1-1/2)) < 857.5662, "a new record with savings by a factor of 13^(1/24)". The page attaches one construction discriminant to the other record.

items.noteInstrument: SAMPLER STOOD UP 2026-08-09, which is what this watch's onTrigger asked for and nobody had built: the traffic API retains 14 days, so the 90-day visitor count cannot be reconstructed later — it has to be accumulated. `scripts/traffic-snapshot.mjs` (npm run traffic) merges the daily views/clones window into continuity/traffic.json and prints days-since-flip plus the running totals. It renders NO verdict; the fair-read judgment stays with whoever adjudicates this watch, same reason a generated pin asserts listing position and never 'the record'. Auth is delegated to the `gh` CLI, so no traffic credential enters this now-public repo and the sampler deliberately does NOT run in CI; only its merge is guarded there (10th self-test), because a merge that returned just the incoming window would silently destroy every day older than 14 — the one bug that would eat the record we are building. Both sides demonstrated at write time per W-4/KP-78: with the truncating merge in place the self-test exits 1 naming the dropped history, with it restored exit 0. FIRST SAMPLE (taken 2026-08-09; a dated historical anchor, NOT a current reading — for the live figure run npm run traffic, which derives it from continuity/traffic.json), and it needs reading carefully rather than celebrating: 14 days recorded, 1 unique viewer-day since the flip, 25 unique cloner-days. THE CLONE FIGURE IS NOT ARRIVALS — 74 clones / 25 uniques all landed on 8/08, the day we ourselves cloned the remote repeatedly to verify the history rewrite, plus CI checkouts and whatever crawls a repo the minute it goes public. Views are the honest metric and they read 1. MEASUREMENT LIMIT FOUND, and it changes how this watch must be read: GitHub dedupes uniques only WITHIN a 14-day window, so a 90-day figure can only be a SUM of per-day uniques, which counts a returning visitor once per day. That sum is an UPPER BOUND on distinct people — which is the useful direction here: a sum under 100 conclusively settles that the threshold is NOT met, while a sum over 100 does not settle that it is. The closeWhen's '100 unique visitors' is therefore not directly measurable and must be read as 'upper bound at least 100, then look harder'.
items.note2: WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT / make me revert or replace it: an issue arriving that is NOT about the ledger's correctness (support questions, feature requests, spam) at a rate that makes the channel noise rather than signal; or a real correction arriving by some OTHER route (a PR, an upstream comment, an email) while the issue tracker stays empty — which would say the invitation is in the wrong place, not that nobody wanted to speak. The failure mode this watch exists to prevent is the walking-denver one named on 2026-08-05: reading a quiet contact link as 'users have nothing to say' when the truth is 'nobody could reach it yet'.

Reaching 100 distinct people by 2026-11-06 needs roughly 1.3 new people every day for 78 more days, about four times the current upper-bound rate. THE VIEWER COUNT IS THE ONLY FIGURE HERE THAT IS NOT MOSTLY OURS: the sampler deliberately does not deduct our own CI, which checks out daily and on every push and PR, so the clone figure is unattributed by design and must never be quoted as an audience. W-6 was re-pointed 2026-08-20 to the first unsolicited outside contact (n=1), so these figures are CONTEXT for that read and never a gate on it. POSITIVE CONTROL: the API forgets days older than 14, so 'days recorded' must EXCEED 14 — it can only do so because this file accumulated them; 14 or fewer means the accumulated history was lost and the gap is permanent.

items.title: MIRROR BLIND CLASS: README.md is not mirrored, and it is where upstream states which records it stands behind
items.note: Found inside the 2026-08-02 fourth-drift cycle (A-2 note6). We mirror constants/** + manifest.json (111 files); upstream README.md is NOT in the mirror. Commit dee1660 -- 'Mark C_21 and C_71 unverified records with asterisks in README' -- restored the peer-reviewed OT2013 value as the headline anchor for C_71 and marked the Numaro n=18 record (merged minutes earlier, PR #130) as unverified because it is on Zenodo but not yet peer-reviewed. Our drift alarm reported three constants files and was SILENT on the semantically largest change of the day. WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING, not academic: generated pins assert listing position inside the per-constant tables, while README is where upstream declares which of those rows it will STAND BEHIND. A record demoted from headline to asterisked is a real event -- arguably the most decision-relevant kind for anyone citing these numbers -- and we cannot see it. Same shape as BC-2 (A-11): the instrument is blind to the class the lane most exists to catch. SEPARATE FROM A-11, which is about check-claims' presence-test on OFF-mirror sources; this one is about the SCOPE of the mirror itself.
items.closeWhen: Either UPSTREAM's README.md (teorth/optimizationproblems' generated 421KB index — NOT this repo's own README.md) joins the mirrored surface with the drift alarm demonstrated firing on an asterisk/headline change and silent on an unrelated edit (W-4), OR a deliberate decision is recorded that the verified/unverified distinction is out of scope for this ledger, with the reason.
items.onTrigger: Before adopting: check how often README churns. It is a GENERATED table (the 8/01 research noted it is the repo's rendered index, 421KB), so a whole-file byte mirror may be as permanently-red as teorth/erdosproblems' problems.yaml was -- which is exactly why A-6 chose entry-level pins over a mirror there. The likely right shape is the A-6 shape: pin the specific README cells for constants we already track, not the file. Decide that before writing code.

verifyBy.method: demonstrate both sides per W-4 -- an asterisk/headline change on a tracked constant must fire, an unrelated README edit must not

items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-10 by the first branch of its own closeWhen: upstream README.md joined the mirrored surface, with the drift alarm demonstrated BOTH ways. Greenlit off the capacity ask (David's fire-don't-wait blanket) as the lane's #1 candidate. WHAT SHIPPED: file maps are now keyed by REPO-RELATIVE path (constants/1a.md, README.md) instead of bare filename, so a report names files as upstream does -- the old code prefixed 'constants/' by concatenation and would have printed 'constants/README.md', a lie about where the file lives inside an artifact whose whole value is being literally true. Nothing moved on disk: the 111 constants files stayed put, README sits beside them at the mirror root, and git diff --numstat after the re-snapshot showed ZERO content lines changed in any constants file (manifest + two scripts + one new file). Post-snapshot ratchet ran: extract-pins regenerated BYTE-IDENTICAL (220 generated + 9 hand), independently confirming no bounds-table row moved. Mirror 111 -> 112 files @ dee1660; ledger unchanged at 229 claims / 227 hold / 0 broken / 2 unverified. BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED, wired into reverify.test.mjs so it is guarded on every CI run: FIRES -- append an asterisk to a real README table row in upstream's own convention, check exits 1 reporting CHANGED README.md with the row verbatim; SILENT (restored) -- put it back and the same run exits 0; SILENT (unrelated edit) -- tamper a constants file and the verdict list is EXACTLY 'CHANGED constants/<file>', README not dragged in (without this, a mirror reporting every file on every run would pass the FIRES assertion while carrying no information); REMOVED -- delete the mirrored README and it reports REMOVED rather than passing silently. NEGATIVE CONTROL PERFORMED with the mutation proven to land first (files are CRLF): ROOT_FILES=[] gives 'AssertionError: an asterisked README row should exit 1, got 0' -- the alarm goes silent on exactly the event class it was built for; restoring returns PASS. THE ITEM OVERSTATED ITS OWN COST BY ~17x AND THAT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: closeWhen described a 'generated 421KB index'; the file is 24KB. The 421KB figure belongs to a DIFFERENT repo's README (teorth/erdosproblems, from A-6 scoping) and was copied across at write time. That wrong number is a plausible reason the item sat eight days -- 421KB of near-daily churn reads like a permanently-red alarm waiting to happen, which this lane refuses to ship; 24KB of curated table does not. The estimate, not the value, kept it parked. The check that would have caught it costs one curl: an item's description of its own cost is a claim like any other, and this repo does not accept unexecuted claims from anyone, including itself. ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG FIRST TIME AND THE ALARM WAS RIGHT: the unrelated-edit check originally asserted the string 'README.md' was absent from the report and failed immediately, because the report HEADER names the whole watched surface. Body was correct throughout. Fixed by asserting on verdict lines rather than raw text, which is also stricter -- it now pins the exact SET of files named. SCOPE HONESTY: this watches upstream's DECLARATION about its records, not the mathematics; a byte-mirror fires on any README edit including a typo fix, accepted deliberately because the file is small and the alternative (pinning only table spans) would reintroduce a blind class to avoid a minor annoyance. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-w5-the-readme-is-where-upstream-says-what-it-stands-behind.md.

items.title: Hosted brief drifts from docs/lane-brief.md — detector shipped, page still stale
items.note: The David-facing brief at https://skylarkcreations.com/t/lanes/bounds-ledger is ported by the ORCHESTRATOR, not by this repo, so it can silently fall behind its source. It did: stale since 26 JULY. Two hand-checks (7/30, 7/31) each reported only ONE missing block because each searched for the block the PRIMER named -- a hand-check that inherits its search term from a doc can only ever confirm that doc. scripts/check-brief.mjs derives the expected set from the source and inherits nothing; it found TWO missing (26 July + 28 July). Runs daily as a SEPARATE always-exits-0 CI job that surfaces via a deduped GitHub issue -- currently issue #6 -- rather than via an exit code nobody reads. Deliberately NOT in the drift job: it would go red and STAY red until the re-port lands, and a permanently-red alarm carries as much information as a permanently-green one (this lane founding defect). G-1 green streak measures the LEDGER, not the porter.
items.closeWhen: The hosted page carries all dated blocks — check-brief.mjs exits 0 against production WHEN RUN WITH THE MACHINE CREDENTIAL (CC_PROMPTS_PIN in env → x-cc-pin header; an anonymous probe cannot see the page at all since the 2026-08-02 gating and its exit code is meaningless) — and issue #6 closed, AND check-brief graduates into the reverify drift job proper on the run after it first reads green.
items.note3: RE-SCOPED 2026-08-02 ON THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ANSWER. Asked (note2) whether /t/lanes/* is meant to be gated; answer: INTENTIONAL — the 8/01 human wall covers David-facing /t/* including lanes — with the direction 'fix A-12's closeWhen to probe with the machine credential path (x-cc-pin header) instead of anonymous; the check, not the gate, is what changes.' DONE: check-brief.mjs now sends x-cc-pin from process.env.CC_PROMPTS_PIN when present (never logged — only its presence is ever reported), and when the pin is ABSENT the UNVERIFIABLE verdict now says so explicitly rather than leaving the reader to guess why the page looks empty. Verified live: anonymous → 18529 bytes of sign-in page, exit 3; with x-cc-pin → HTTP 200, 47958 bytes, the brief's H1 present. THE RE-SCOPED PROBE IMMEDIATELY ANSWERED THE OTHER OPEN QUESTION — are the blocks actually ported? NO: the credentialed read reports 3 OF 4 MISSING (26 July, 28 July, 1 August; the 'Sent — 24 July 2026' block IS present), which matches the 8/01 reading exactly. So the staleness is REAL and unchanged since 26 July — this morning's '4 of 4' was purely the wall artifact. CONSEQUENCE: the escalation suspended in note2 is RE-ARMED, now on true evidence. If the page is still 3-blocks-behind after 2026-08-07, escalate to David naming 26 July / 28 July / 1 August. The suspension was correct while the cause was unknown and is no longer needed.
items.onTrigger: Nothing to do while it stays red -- this repo CANNOT fix it, the port is the orchestrators. Do NOT re-post an identical bus note each day; issue #6 is the standing alarm. ESCALATION RE-ARMED 2026-08-02 (see note3): it was suspended for a few hours this morning while the cause was unknown, then the credentialed probe confirmed the staleness is REAL and unchanged since 26 July. If still 3-blocks-behind after 2026-08-07, escalate to David naming 26 July / 28 July / 1 August. ALWAYS read the page with CC_PROMPTS_PIN set -- an anonymous run reports UNVERIFIABLE and proves nothing either way.
items.note2: THE 8/02 READ WAS NOT STALENESS -- IT WAS A LOGIN WALL, AND THE CHECKER BLAMED THE PORTER. `npm run check` reported 4-of-4 blocks missing (up from 3, which reads exactly like the port falling further behind) and printed 'the port is the orchestrator's'. False: skylarkcreations.com/t/lanes/bounds-ledger now 307s to /t/signin?next=... and the sign-in page returns HTTP 200, so res.ok was true and the checker compared our dated blocks against the markup of a login form it had never distinguished from the brief. Cause is skylark-site 53c87f83 'feat(auth): Google sign-in (Supabase) human wall for CC surfaces'; /t/lanes/bank-see and /t/lanes/forecast-lab 307 identically, so it is site-wide and intentional. FIXED SAME SESSION: check-brief.mjs now proves the response IS the brief (tests for the source's own H1, derived not hardcoded) before assessing staleness; absent title => new exit 3 'BRIEF UNVERIFIABLE' naming the redirect target and stating explicitly that this is not evidence the re-port is behind. Verdict logic split into a pure assess() and covered by a new --selftest (in-sync / stale / wall / wall-behind-redirect + a guard that the wall verdict never says BRIEF STALE or blames the port), wired into npm test AND CI. Both sides demonstrated live per W-4: fires on production (exit 3, names /t/signin?next=%2Ft%2Flanes%2Fbounds-ledger); stays silent on the IDENTICAL captured sign-in HTML with only the brief's H1 prepended, which still reports BRIEF STALE exit 1 -- the load-bearing control, since a gate that swallowed the stale verdict would pass 'can it fire' while blinding the alarm it lives inside. Mutation proved landed via git diff --numstat first. Free second result: A-8's 7/31 CI-coverage ratchet fired for the first time against a real new self-test, naming it by name. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-02-the-brief-check-blamed-the-porter-for-a-login-wall.md. WHAT IS NOW UNKNOWN, and is the orchestrator's to answer: (1) is /t/lanes/* meant to be gated? if yes this item's closeWhen ('check-brief.mjs exits 0 against production') is UNREACHABLE as written and the item needs re-scoping, not escalating; (2) independently, are the four dated blocks actually ported? unanswerable from here since 8/01 -- only an authenticated reader can say.

verifyBy.method: run node scripts/check-brief.mjs against production and read the exit code; do not trust the issue state alone

items.note4: CLOSED 2026-08-03 ON EVIDENCE. Orchestrator ported the three missing blocks (26 Jul, 28 Jul, 1 Aug) from docs/lane-brief.md @ 85b2af4 — their commit 8d18e4d0, deploy verified live 15:20Z. Confirmed from this side by a CREDENTIALED probe (CC_PROMPTS_PIN set): "brief: in sync — all 4 dated block(s) present", exit 0. First green read since check-brief.mjs shipped 7/31. Issue #6 closed with the probe output pasted in. The 8/07 David-escalation is moot and is NOT to be re-armed. CAUGHT ON THE WAY OUT — the detector fired a trap in our own CLAUDE.md: the 7/31 pre-commitment "joins CI the run after the page first reads green" fired for the first time TODAY, and following it would have wired a check into CI that CI cannot run (no pin on a runner = exit 3 UNVERIFIABLE since the 8/02 sign-in wall), whose only fix is putting the pin in repo secrets — forbidden with a public flip pending. Clause retired the same day it first became actionable. This is the A-11 class exactly: a threshold derived from the old regime silently keeps reading as authoritative after the regime changes. Worth remembering that the trap was only visible because the alarm finally went green; a permanently-red alarm would have hidden it indefinitely.
items.note5: BLIND SPOT IN THE DETECTOR, found 2026-08-04 by changing the source under it. The voice pass (c7cff94) rewrote 52 em dashes and dropped a status glyph in docs/lane-brief.md, including inside two block HEADINGS ('## ✅ Sent — 24 July 2026' -> '## Sent - 24 July 2026'). Re-ran check-brief.mjs with the pin expecting the heading rewrite to break matching: still 'in sync — all 4 dated block(s) present', exit 0. It matches on the block DATE, not the heading text, so the rewrite was invisible to it — but so is the fact that the hosted page now carries the OLD prose until the orchestrator re-ports. The detector asserts block PRESENCE, never content fidelity. That is the same distinction as generated pins asserting listing position rather than 'the record', and it is the right scope for a checker whose whole job is to survive a page it does not control — worth stating out loud rather than discovering later as a surprise. NOT re-opening A-12: no dated block is missing, and a fidelity check on a page ported by someone else would go red on every edit until they re-port, which is the permanently-red-alarm failure this item exists because of. Consequence for a reader: after ANY lane-brief edit, the hosted page is stale in wording (not in coverage) until a re-port lands; say so rather than implying the pages match.

items.title: GOAL: contribute a verified bound improvement to the stewarded inventory (steward → steward + contributor; David-ruled 2026-08-06)
items.note: DAVID'S RULING, 2026-08-06, in-session after reading OpenAI's Ten Advances paper: that this was the kind of work he wanted this lane doing — then, on the four-step plan (gap table → pick 2-3 under-studied targets → LLM-proposes / local-verifier-scores search loop → exact reverify + literature check + adversarial review + David-gated PR): to do all four steps. SCOPE HONESTY, recorded at write time: we play the CONSTRUCTION game (an explicit object plus a finite certificate a script can check), never the theorem game (asymptotic proofs need mathematicians or Lean, which we do not have). The certificate IS the contribution — a claim ships only with a verifier the maintainer can run. GUARD: the late-2025 'solved 10 Erdos problems' embarrassment (a model rediscovering known results) is the named failure mode; the literature/priority check is a mandatory step, not hygiene. STEP 1 DONE same day: scripts/gap-table.mjs (selftest wired into npm test + CI) — 111 constants, 65 with a numeric gap, 6 parse-suspect (instrument flags, listed in docs/gap-table.json), 40 symbolic. TARGETS PICKED from reading the files, not the ranks alone: PRIMARY 27b (Earth-Moon problem, max chromatic number of biplanar graphs, bounds 9..12, lower bound unmoved since Sulanke 1980, Gethner conjectures 11; an improvement is a graph + a two-planar edge partition + a DRAT unsatisfiability certificate for (k-1)-coloring — every link machine-checkable); SECONDARY 69a (Sendov radius — lower-bound examples are explicit polynomials, checkable with interval arithmetic); STRETCH 39a (Hadwiger H_3, upper 14 Prymak 2023 — computer-assisted covering method, but the discretization reduction is proof-shaped so a win needs a mathematician-grade gate, riskier); REJECTED 73a after reading (its lower bound is the conjectured optimum — nothing to improve; the gap-table rank alone would have wasted a campaign on it, which is why target-picking reads files). BUDGET, David-asked, answered same session: per-target campaign hard-capped; numbers in the 2026-08-06 daily/bus post.
items.closeWhen: One bound improvement with a machine-checkable certificate is merged into the stewarded inventory (or formally acknowledged by its maintainers). A sent PR does not close this — same rule as G-1: merge or maintainer reply only. Interim milestone worth a note, not a close: our verifier reproduces the CURRENT record on a target (proves the harness can score the known answer before we trust it on a new one).
items.note2: INTERIM MILESTONE HIT 2026-08-06, same day as the ruling: the 27b verifier REPRODUCES THE KNOWN RECORD. David greenlit the first campaign in-pane (to go ahead and attempt one, and not to economise on model selection) and ruled Fable drives the proposal step — his instinct endorsed with one refinement recorded here: proposals AND strategy/diagnosis calls get the top model; the VERIFIER gets no model at all, its authority is being dumb checkable code the maintainer can run. Shipped: search/27b/verifier.mjs (exact DMP planarity + exact branch-and-bound chromatic number + certificate check, Node stdlib only), selftest proving both answers (4 nonplanar fire incl. Petersen and K3,3 which exercise the real embedding not the edge count; 4 planar silent; 5 exact chi values; 1 good certificate passes, 3 defect classes fail), wired into npm test + CI. Then the known-record reproduction: a random-restart greedy (deterministic PRNG, seed recorded) found a biplanar split of Sulanke's graph on restart 924 - 27/23 edges, both layers planar under DMP, chi exactly 9 - and the full certificate verifies: search/27b/sulanke-certificate.json. The harness can score the known answer; searching for a 10-chromatic biplanar graph may now begin. SEARCH POSTURE: Fable proposes construction families in-session (subscription, ~zero marginal cost) with the verifier as the only judge; API-billed overnight runs come later if volume demands, and need an API key decision from David first. CEILING RECORDED AT WRITE TIME: the in-house chromatic solver is exponential worst-case and fine at n<=40; a real candidate for upstream gets a DIMACS export + industrial SAT solver + DRAT proof as the shipping certificate, not our solver's word.
items.note3: ROUND ONE RAN 2026-08-07: 11 proposed constructions, 0 certified, 11 eliminated (edge-bound 5, k9-free 2, chromatic 4). Instrument: search/27b/propose-round.mjs, 8th self-test, wired into npm test + CI and proven both ways (each of 4 gates fires and stays silent; split search returns both outcomes; Sulanke re-certifies at target 9; and the CI wiring itself was negative-controlled — removing the workflow step made reverify.test exit 1 naming the unguarded selftest, restoring it returned exit 0 / 8 self-tests). FINDING (docs/findings/2026-08-07-g2-27b-round-one-the-one-edge-vise.md): two unrelated families land EXACTLY one short. The join family successor C5+K7 is over the 6n-12 budget by exactly ONE edge and has omega=9; buying that edge back from inside the clique meets budget exactly and drops omega to 8 but gives chi=9, buying it back from the join keeps omega=9 and dies on the clique gate. Independently, circulants sized to fit the budget top out at C17(1..5) with chi=9. Both directions arrive at nine. The vise: thickness 2 caps average degree below 12 so a 10-chromatic biplanar graph sits near the Brooks boundary where structure is pushed toward near-complete, while thickness 2 simultaneously forbids K9. ROUND TWO DIRECTION, falling straight out of the data (every death was too-dense-to-be-biplanar or not-chromatic-enough, none subtle): INVERT THE SEARCH — stop proposing high-chromatic graphs and hoping they are biplanar; glue two planar triangulations on a shared vertex set so biplanarity is free by construction, and maximise chi, the one gate we compute exactly and cheaply. PROVENANCE: the k9-free gate is CITED (theta(K9)=3, Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962), not executed — 2^36 splits is not brute-forceable and greedy failure proves nothing; labelled CITED in code, console and JSON. Its failure direction is safe: a wrong citation can only make us SKIP a family, never SHIP a false certificate. METHOD CATCH: the first run built two differently-labelled candidates as the SAME graph (positional edge-drop hit cross edges in a join, so the clique-edge candidate was never built); caught only by noticing two rows that should differ did not, NOT by the self-test, which tests the gates and not the candidate list pointed at them (A-13 F-4 shape). Fixed with removeEdge(g,u,v) which throws on a named edge that is not present; the correction changed the result and exposed the chi=9 near-miss the finding rests on. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates, and the chi=9 outputs merely re-derive the 1980 bound.
items.note4: ROUND TWO RAN 2026-08-07 (same day as round one): the INVERTED search — build biplanar graphs BY CONSTRUCTION (double-greedy two maximal planar layers out of K_n using the exact DMP test, union is thickness<=2 by construction) and measure chi. Instrument search/27b/round2-grow.mjs, 9th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. RESULT: hard ceiling at chi=8 across n=9..13, 300 seeds each — the inverted search tops out ONE COLOUR BELOW the record it was meant to beat, and degrades as n grows (n=9: 286/300 seeds reach 8; n=13: only 54/300, leftover grows 1->15). THE SENTENCE WORTH KEEPING: at n=11 the best round-two graph has EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=8, while Sulanke has n=11, EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=9 — same vertex count, same edge count, one colour apart, both verified by the same code in the same run. DENSITY IS NOT WHAT THE RECORD IS MADE OF; the objective behind the inverted search is measurably wrong, and this is the cleanest refutation of it. What separates them is STRUCTURE: Sulanke is a designed object (6-clique joined to a 5-cycle) and double-greedy explores the generic part of the space where that never arises by chance. SIDE RESULT, carefully bounded: at n=9 the grower produced K9 minus exactly one edge with both layers planar per the verifier — an EXECUTED demonstration that K9-minus-an-edge is biplanar (chi=8). That is CONSISTENT WITH the theta(K9)=3 citation the round-one k9-free gate leans on, but is NOT a proof of it and must never be recorded as one: exhibiting a split for K9-e says nothing about non-existence of a split for K9. The citation stays cited. ROUND THREE DIRECTION (both rounds now agree from opposite directions that the record is a STRUCTURED object — round one showed structured constructions fail by razor-thin margins, round two shows unstructured ones do not get close): seed the growth with structure. Next instrument should accept a SEED SUBGRAPH held fixed in the layers and double-greedy only the remaining edges; watch the leftover column, which at n>=12 is already large enough to be where the missing colour goes. METHOD CATCH: cross-checking the n=11 comparison by importing round2-grow.mjs silently re-ran the whole search and printed a second full result table into the middle of the check — harmless only because the numbers agreed. Both round scripts exported functions AND ran main at import; both now guard on being the entry point, proven both ways (import prints nothing and still exposes growBiplanar/runGates; direct invocation still runs). NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 8, the record lower bound of 9 stands untouched and round two did not even reach it.
items.note5: ROUND THREE RAN 2026-08-10: seed the search with the design, as round two's finding directed. Instrument search/27b/round3-seeded.mjs, 11th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. TWO HALVES, AND THE CHEAP ONE WAS DECISIVE. PART A — THE FAMILY IS CLOSED BY EDGE COUNT ALONE: Sulanke's graph is K6 join C5 and that family has chi = r+3, so chi>=10 needs r>=7; every biplanar graph obeys m <= 6n-12 (two planar layers of 3n-6). Scanning K_r join C_s for r=4..9, odd s=3..11 (30 members): 15 reach chi>=10, and exactly ONE of those fits the budget. Near misses are as thin as round one's — K7 join C5 is over by exactly ONE edge (n=12, m=61, budget 60), K8 join C3 also by exactly one (n=11, m=55, budget 54); every other chi>=10 member misses by 5 to 38. THE SOLE SURVIVOR IS K7 join C3, WHICH IS K10 — verified by execution, not inspection: the construction returns n=10, m=45, and C(10,2)=45, so the graph is complete; its chi was COMPUTED as 10, not taken from the r+3 formula. K10 has thickness 3 (Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962; the theta(K_n) formula's only exceptions are n=9 and n=10), so it is not biplanar and the family is closed. WHERE THIS RESTS ON A CITATION, STATED PLAINLY: the budget half is ours and runs; the theta(K10)=3 step is CITED, not executed — our verifier can exhibit a split when one exists but cannot prove none does, and non-existence is exactly what that step needs. Same citation round one leaned on for K9, same status. PART B — THE SEED CARRIES ALL THE COLOUR AND THE GREEDY CARRIES NONE: holding Sulanke's verified layers fixed and double-greedying only the edges the seed does not own, over n=11..14 at 40 seeds each (160 growths, every graph re-checked by verifyCertificate), best chi is 9 at EVERY n and on EVERY seed — 40/40, never below, never above. Read against round two (which reached 8 on 209/300 seeds at n=10 and only 54/300 by n=13), this is sharp in both directions: the structure survives generic growth, and generic growth adds nothing on top of it. It was still possible after round two that unseeded search underperformed merely because it never stumbled onto the structure; handed the structure outright, it still adds no colour. Leftover behaves as round two predicted: 5 -> 9 -> 14 -> 21 as n grows, i.e. the price of biplanarity rises faster than extra vertices can pay for it. WHAT THIS CLOSES: the clique-join-odd-cycle family as a route to chi=10, and the extend-the-record-graph-generically idea — both live hypotheses that morning, neither needing another search. ROUND FOUR DIRECTION, falling out of the budget scan: every construction tried so far is a JOIN, and a join buys three colours for r*s edges while the 6n-12 budget grows by only 6 per vertex — the next family must buy colour more cheaply per edge than a complete join does. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 9 — equal to the record and only because we handed the search the record graph — and the record lower bound stands untouched. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-g2-27b-round-three-the-family-is-closed.md.
items.note9: DEMOTED TO TIER-1 by David 2026-08-20: "keep improving a bound ourselves one level down." Not deprioritised into nothing — it stays a real goal with the search harness intact and the gap table refreshed the same day. The reason it is not Tier-0 is that its timing is not ours to control: it depends on finding a problem where we can actually do better, which could be next month or next year. See G-3.
items.readCommand: node -e "const fs=require('fs');import('./search/27b/verifier.mjs').then(v=>{const c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('search/27b/sulanke-certificate.json','utf8'));const pc=v.verifyCertificate(c);console.log('positive control - verifier still scores the KNOWN 1980 record:',JSON.stringify(pc));if(!pc.ok)throw new Error('verifier cannot score the known record - the instrument is broken, not the search');for(const f of ['round1-results.json','round2-results.json','round3-results.json']){const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('search/27b/'+f,'utf8'));const rows=j.results||j.rows||[];const vals=rows.map(r=>typeof r.bestChi==='number'?r.bestChi:(typeof r.chi==='number'?r.chi:null)).filter(x=>x!==null);const best=vals.length?Math.max(...vals):null;console.log(f,'rows='+rows.length,vals.length?('best chi='+best+' over '+vals.length+' scored row(s) - beats the record only if >9'):'0 rows carry a chromatic value (keys checked: bestChi, chi) - eliminated before the chromatic gate; verdicts: '+rows.map(r=>r.verdict||'?').join('/'))}})"
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-22 run readCommand and answer ONE question: has any round produced a certificate the verifier ACCEPTS that beats the 1980 record (chromatic number strictly greater than 9)? If NO — and no is the expected answer — do not re-ask whether to keep going. Ask instead WHICH BOTTLENECK is binding, because the two answers imply opposite next moves: (a) the HARNESS, if rounds are still eliminating families by arithmetic before any candidate reaches the verifier, in which case the work is a better generator; or (b) the SEARCH SPACE, if candidates reach the verifier and are honestly rejected, in which case the work is a different family or a different target entirely. State which, with the round rows as evidence. STATE AT DATING, 2026-08-22, so a later reader can see movement rather than re-deriving it: round 1 = 11 rows, ALL verdict DEAD but 4 of them scored, best chi 9; round 2 = 5 rows, all scored, best chi 8; round 3 = 4 rows, all scored, best chi 9. Best achieved anywhere EQUALS the 1980 record and beats nothing. The verifier scored the known 1980 record at chromatic number 9 on that date, which is the positive control that makes those figures mean something.
items.readCommandNote: Added 2026-08-22 with the date, under the rule adopted today that a readCommand is written the moment a row GETS an expectedSignalBy — the date is what makes a row a gate, so that is the moment to name the command. RUN BEFORE BEING WRITTEN DOWN (read from a file and executed, never retyped), exit 0. IT LEADS WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL AND THROWS IF IT FAILS: the verifier must still score Sulanke's known graph at 9, because a zero from a dead verifier is indistinguishable from a search that found nothing. FALSE ZERO CAUGHT IN THIS COMMAND BEFORE IT SHIPPED, recorded because it is the exact defect this lane polices: the first draft summed on r.chi, a field that does not exist in these files — the real key is bestChi — so it printed "best chi=0" for rounds 2 and 3 and would have read as "the search found nothing" when round 3 had in fact reached 9. The shipped version names rows with no bestChi field as an ELIMINATION ROUND with its verdicts, rather than reporting them as zero. CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, 2026-08-22, by the mandated sibling sweep — and the correction matters more than the original fix. Sweeping for other reads of a chromatic field found `propose-round.mjs` setting `out.chi`, a DIFFERENT key from the `bestChi` used by rounds 2 and 3. The just-fixed command tested only `bestChi`, so it reported round 1 as carrying no chromatic value at all when 4 of its 11 rows were in fact scored at up to 9 — they died at the CHROMATIC gate, not before reaching it. So the first fix for a false zero shipped a second false zero of the same shape, in the same command, and only the sibling sweep caught it. The command now tests both keys and, when genuinely none is present, says WHICH KEYS IT CHECKED rather than implying absence. Lesson worth keeping: a guessed field name is not one defect, it is a class, and fixing the instance you noticed does not fix the class.
items.dateRationale: DATED 2026-08-22 by the lane, NOT by David, and flagged in the P4 post so it can be overruled. WHY IT NEEDED ONE: G-2 became the Tier-1 goal when G-1 closed this morning, and it carried no structured signal date — which is precisely the defect G-1's own signalPrestaged recorded on 2026-08-17 (a gate with no date is invisible to every date-based check, and a detector with no input can never fire). G-1 got a date that day and G-2 did not. The continuity endpoint independently flagged this row stale-actionable at 12 days on the same morning. 2026-09-22 matches G-3's cadence so the two goals read together.

items.title: GOAL (Tier-0 from G-1 close): someone outside Skylark uses the ledger and acts on it
items.note: DAVID-RULED 2026-08-20, his words on card f460cdd1 resolving 230d5f46: "Yes - make the new top goal whether someone outside uses the ledger, and keep improving a bound ourselves one level down." This is his direction verbatim; everything below marked OPERATIONALIZATION is mine and is challengeable.
items.note2: WHY IT IS THE RIGHT NEXT QUESTION. G-1 proved the machine works ONCE — the alarm ran armed for 30 days and a maintainer acted on a correction we found. That establishes capability, not demand. The binding constraint after capability is whether anyone wants it, and we could not have asked that a week ago because there was nothing an outsider could use. Now there is: the README names twelve constants and links each to the rows we watch (ce25d76), and a page answering the question for all 111 is built and held for review (PR #27).
items.note3: OPERATIONALIZATION — the close condition is MINE, not his. Close when TWO distinct people who are not us take an action that depends on this ledger: filing an issue or correction, citing it, using the spot-check surface and telling us, or a maintainer acting on something we surfaced. TWO, not one, deliberately: G-1 already produced exactly one acknowledgement, so a threshold of one would close on a fact that is already true and would prove nothing new. If David wants one, or three, that is a one-line change and this note is where to make it.
items.note4: STATED WEAKNESS, not buried. This may read ZERO for months and that is not a failure of the goal. Twelve days after the repo went public it had roughly four unique viewer-days, and the sampler says that OVERCOUNTS distinct people. A Tier-0 that reads zero is uncomfortable and honest; the alternative — a metric that always moves — is the self-rating this lane already refused to build. Do NOT substitute an activity count for it.
items.note5: LEADING INDICATORS, readable now, none of them a substitute for the goal: W-6 (first unsolicited outside contact, re-pointed 2026-08-20 to a qualitative n=1); the viewer count from npm run traffic — NEVER the clone count, which is mostly our own CI; and whether the public surface actually exists and is findable, which currently means whether PR #27 clears the review lane.
items.note6: CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW — SHADOW ROW, owed and unrun, recorded 2026-08-22 rather than quietly skipped. The per-row report-link ship touched scripts/render-site.mjs, which is in-class as a file (it prints numbers a mathematician believes). I shipped without holding, on the reasoning that the diff touches NO printed claim — no bound, date, pin or count rendering changed, only an added link column plus its test. Carried up and RULED by the orchestrator the same day: no overrule, because the review lane is in SHADOW fleet-wide (32 of 32 in-class commits carry no review row), and ship-then-log is the correct shadow behaviour. This row is the honest log: a review was owed by the file-level rule, was not run, and the dated reason is recorded here instead of the row being backfilled as though the gate had been enforced.
items.closeWhen: Two distinct people who are not us have taken an action that depends on this ledger, each recorded with the date and the evidence. A single instance is a note, not a close — G-1 already produced one.
items.signalDateNote: One month, and it is an INSTRUMENT read, not an outcome read. Nobody should expect the goal to have moved by then.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-22 do NOT ask "has an outsider used it yet" — a zero there is expected and uninformative this early. Ask instead whether we COULD detect it if it happened: is the report-an-error channel reachable, does the public surface exist and render, would an issue or a citation actually reach us, and is npm run traffic still accumulating (the API forgets days older than 14, so a gap is permanent). If any detection path is dead, that is the finding and it is actionable now. The OUTCOME read is 2026-11-06, alongside W-6.
items.note7: LINKED 2026-08-22 during close-out, after the continuity check flagged 7 commits from the 2026-08-21 session in no item. Mapped by what each commit TOUCHED rather than by its subject line: 2443b55 built the page (index.html, render-site.mjs, the workflow and .nojekyll), 10e1db3 turned Pages on and updated the README and flow map, f421ea6 put a real catch on the README first screen, 883e108 recorded David's succession ruling (also linked on G-2). The remaining three went to the rows whose work they actually were — b63391b to A-27, and cdb6746 plus 1fb5c85 to A-16, whose upstream correction they sent and drafted. Nothing was filed under meta.untrackedCommits: every one had an unambiguous owner once the file stats were read, and guessing from subject lines would have put a false claim in the ledger.
items.note8: HOW TO REPORT THIS GOAL ZERO, and it will be zero for a while. A fleet rule adopted 2026-08-20 (canonical in skylark-site operating principles, not restated here): a clean zero with no considered-and-declined beside it is a QUESTION, not an ANSWER — a zero you never deliberated is an absence of a record, not evidence of judgment. G-3 is the lane most exposed to this, because its honest reading is expected to be zero for months and a bare "0" every week would look identical whether the instruments were live or dead. So every G-3 zero states WHICH KIND it is: measured (the detection paths were checked and nobody acted) or unexamined (nobody looked). The 2026-09-22 onTrigger already forces the first kind by asking whether we COULD detect an outside use rather than whether one happened.
items.note9: SAME RULE APPLIES TO THE LANE OTHER ZEROS, and they recur weekly: npm run catches reporting 0 movements, and W-6 arrivals. A zero from a dead probe is indistinguishable from a measured zero unless the report says which — that is KP-35 generalized, already in CLAUDE.md, and the fleet rule is the same shape arriving from the other direction.
items.readCommand: npm run traffic && node scripts/render-site.mjs --check && gh issue list --repo u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --state open --limit 5 && gh issue list --repo u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --search "Row looks wrong:" --state all --limit 5 && gh issue list --repo u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --search "Constant not tracked:" --state all --limit 5 && node -e "fetch('https://u00dxk2.github.io/bounds-ledger/').then(r=>r.ok?r.text():Promise.reject(new Error('page HTTP '+r.status))).then(t=>{if(!t.includes('Is the number you cited still current?'))throw new Error('not the ledger page - later checks would be meaningless');if(!t.includes('/bounds-ledger/issues'))throw new Error('report-an-error link ABSENT from served page');if(!t.includes('id=\"emptyask\"'))throw new Error('not-tracked report route ABSENT from served page');console.log('served page OK; both report routes present')})"
items.readCommandNote: Added 2026-08-22 (b3, orchestrator-approved). ONE command-shaped string chaining the detection paths G-3.onTrigger names in prose: is npm run traffic still accumulating (the API forgets days older than 14, so a gap is permanent); does the public surface still match committed state; would an issue reach us; does the SERVED page still carry the report-an-error link. RUN BEFORE BEING WRITTEN HERE, in the exact chained form stored in this field, exit 0 on 2026-08-22 — the 2026-08-18 rule that a command in a doc is verified by running it, not by reading it. It asserts liveness of the detection paths and NOTHING about arrivals: a green chain means we could detect an outsider, never that one came. FIFTH LEG ADDED 2026-08-22 on orchestrator ask: a `gh issue list --search "Row looks wrong:"` read, so the gate reads MECHANICALLY the observable that today's ship created (every row now opens a prefilled report carrying that title prefix) instead of a future session remembering to look for it. Positive control run the same day, because a zero from a dead probe is indistinguishable from a measured zero: the identical search for "Drift:" returned 3 rows, so the search CAN return non-zero and today's 0 is measured. The whole five-leg chain was run in the exact stored form (read from the file and executed, not retyped) and exited 0.
items.note10: DETECTION CEILING — written down 2026-08-23, orchestrator-ruled rather than sent to David, because it records a trade we already live under rather than proposing a change. G-3's read date asks not 'did an outsider arrive' but 'could we DETECT one if they did'. The honest answer: the public page is ARCHITECTURALLY INCAPABLE of reporting usage, and that is not an oversight — render-site.mjs's selftest actively enforces that the page references no third-party asset and fetches nothing at runtime, so adding analytics means deleting a guard we deliberately wrote. Both user-visible affordances emit nothing: the per-row report link (1995839) and the ordering control (2f9ff5d). The clone figure is mostly our own CI, which checks out the repo on a daily schedule, on every push and on every pull request. So the reachable outside-arrival signals are exactly FOUR: a filed issue, a pull request, an email, and a viewer count running at roughly 4 per 14 days. G-3 IS THEREFORE MEASURED BY CONTACT EVENTS ONLY, AND THAT IS A CHOSEN TRADE, NOT A GAP — a self-contained page is part of what makes this ledger trustworthy, and trading that for telemetry we would not act on is a bad exchange. The other direction (adding analytics) is a product-thesis call that WOULD need David; it is not proposed. Written before the read date so 2026-09-22 is spent on the question, not on rediscovering why it cannot be answered.
items.noteSixthPath: SIXTH DETECTION PATH ADDED 2026-08-23, and the gap is the lesson. The empty-state ship (9208ff3) created a NEW outside-arrival observable — an issue titled 'Constant not tracked: <term>', filed by a visitor whose search missed. It is the only path that captures someone who wanted a constant we do not carry. The readCommand did not check it, because a read command written before a path exists cannot know about it. RULE: shipping a new detection path is not done until the goal's own readCommand reads it, or the path is live and invisible to the very check that asks whether we could detect an outsider. The served-page leg also gained a POSITIVE CONTROL on the page H1 first — the chain previously asserted a link was present without first proving it had the ledger page, and an absence assertion against the wrong document proves nothing.
items.note11: THE CLOSE CONDITION LOOKS MET, AND IT WAS MET ON 2026-08-23 WITHOUT ANYONE NOTICING. Found 2026-08-26 in P5 while writing a readCommand for W-8, which is the uncomfortable part: nothing we run was looking. EVIDENCE, each with date and row-level provenance rather than a summary. (1) CHESSING234 (Taksh), a person who is not us, opened PR teorth/optimizationproblems#151 and committed 7848802 on 2026-08-23T15:14:02Z, titled 'Attach the right witness to the 857.567 record in 87a'. Its message ENDS with the words 'Reported in issue 150.' — an explicit citation of the issue this ledger filed on 2026-08-20, so causation is stated by the actor rather than inferred by us from timing. The issue timeline records 'cross-referenced by Chessing234 2026-08-23T16:50:14Z' naming 151. (2) TEORTH (Terence Tao) closed our issue #150 as state_reason=completed at 2026-08-23T17:15:36Z, and committed b1a28ac at 17:18:50Z. WHAT THIS MEANS AGAINST closeWhen: two distinct people who are not us took actions that depend on this ledger, each dated and evidenced. THE COUNTING QUESTION IS NOT MINE TO SETTLE and is why this is a note rather than a close: teorth is arguably ALREADY the one person G-1 produced (he merged PR #141 on 2026-08-05), so whether he counts again or whether Chessing234 is only the second of a required two is a judgment about a bar I wrote myself. note3 says that bar is mine and challengeable; a Tier-0 goal should not close on its author re-reading his own threshold favourably. Surfaced to David as a decision with a board card on 2026-08-26. NOTE WHAT IS ALSO TRUE AND UNFLATTERING: note4 predicted this would read zero for months, the fleet was told to expect zero, and the actual answer had been sitting in a closed upstream issue for three days. Our own mirror even ingested the fix — 87a.md changed in the 5c4aeee snapshot and the 2026-08-24 rotation classified it as a text edit — so the ledger SAW the bytes move and no instrument connected them to our own report. That gap is the real finding and it belongs to W-9.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-26 ON DAVID'S RULING, board card 8e8f547d resolving needs-decision 4e9f90a4. HIS WORDS VERBATIM: "Yes - mark it done, and make the next goal whether it happens again without us filing the report. But also let's find more things to have an impact on? Where else can we have an impact like this?" THE EVIDENCE THE CLOSE RESTS ON, dated and row-level (full account in note11): on 2026-08-23T15:14:02Z Chessing234 (Taksh) committed 7848802 to teorth/optimizationproblems, 'Attach the right witness to the 857.567 record in 87a', ending 'Reported in issue 150.' — the issue this ledger filed on 2026-08-20. He cross-referenced it from PR #151 at 16:50:14Z; Terence Tao closed our issue state_reason=completed at 17:15:36Z and committed b1a28ac at 17:18:50Z. Causation is stated by the actor in his own commit message rather than inferred from timing, which is the strongest form of this evidence we have ever had. DAVID SETTLED THE COUNTING QUESTION BY NOT ENGAGING WITH IT: three readings were put to him (Tao counting twice via his 2026-08-05 merge of PR #141, Chessing234 as the second of two, or the bar being too low because it fired within a week of being written) and he answered 'mark it done'. Recorded that way rather than as 'the two-person bar was met', because those are different statements and only the first is his. SUCCEEDED BY G-4, which is his framing and not ours.
items.note12: WHAT THE CLOSE DOES NOT CLAIM, written at close so a later reader does not inflate it. The goal asked whether someone outside Skylark uses the ledger and acts on it. It does NOT establish that the ledger is DISCOVERABLE — the impact path ran through an issue a human here wrote to a maintainer, not through anyone finding the public page. Traffic on the day of the close: 3 unique viewers in the trailing 14 days. G-4 exists precisely because that gap is the interesting part of what remains.

items.resolution: DROPPED 2026-08-12, NOT SENT, and the closing reason is a refutation rather than a deprioritisation. David opened the drafting gate ('Draft it and show me the PR, codex adversarial review it, then after I approve you can send it'); the review killed it before it reached him for the send approval. THE REFUTATION: the asymmetry is not an oversight in a uniform practice, it is THE MAINTAINER'S OWN DELIBERATE EDIT. Git history on README.md, read from the API: 49c07ee (Chessing234, 2026-08-10, 'Sync 3b lower bound in README with constant page' = PR #142 by an outside contributor) ADDED the 3b improvement line unmarked; then 400a9bb (teorth, 2026-08-11T17:17:35Z) 'Mark C_3b unverified record with asterisk in README' -- a commit by Terence Tao whose ENTIRE STATED PURPOSE was marking C_3b unverified -- put the asterisk on the table row and not on the improvement line three lines above. His legend scopes the asterisk to 'the table below' and his commit is consistent with his own legend. Sending would have told the maintainer his own dedicated edit of the previous day was incomplete, as our SECOND-ever contact, one day after he merged our first (PR #141). TWO FURTHER DEFECTS, either requiring a rewrite: (1) WRONG FORM -- the draft copied 3a (asterisk alone), but verified independently, 5 improvement lines use '(unverified)' AND the asterisk (22, 31, 84a, 84b, 1a) and only 2 use the asterisk alone, both being 3a's 'limit value' lines; we copied the minority pattern and called it the repo's convention. (2) constants/3b.md marks the row NEITHER way, so the status lives only in the README table and '3b alone is the exception' was too clean a story. ON THE REVIEWER: Codex found defect (1) and cited commit 400a9bb, which is what led to the history above; its own shell was dead (CreateProcessAsUserW failed -1073283067 -- the MSIX/Store-pwsh issue the orchestrator flagged as RED that morning), so it reviewed the facts through GitHub API tooling and NEVER READ THE PR BODY. It failed closed and said so explicitly; the body was reviewed locally instead. A review that reports the angle it could not cover is worth more than one that quietly skips it. THE LESSON THAT OUTLIVES THE ITEM: we enumerated the STATE of 111 rows and 19 improvement lines across two sessions and never once asked WHO MADE IT THAT WAY AND WHEN. `git log` on the exact line was the check that mattered and it costs one command. BEFORE PROPOSING A CORRECTION TO A MAINTAINED SURFACE, READ THE HISTORY OF THE THING YOU ARE CORRECTING -- an enumeration answers 'what is inconsistent', never 'is this inconsistency intentional', and only the second licenses contacting a human. Draft + full refutation retained at docs/decisions/2026-08-12-A14-pr-draft.md.
items.title: DROPPED 2026-08-12 after adversarial review: the 3b asterisk asymmetry is the maintainer's own deliberate edit, not an oversight — proposed correction NOT sent, and should not be revived
items.note: Found during the 2026-08-11 evening drift cycle (upstream dee1660 -> 400a9bb), which is also W-5's first fire on a real change. Upstream README states its own convention: bounds whose available verification is at minimal levels are marked with an asterisk in the summary table. The 3b row now reads '1.77898 (1.77898884*)' -- marked. The recent-improvements line announcing the SAME bound (13-point entropy certificate by Mosaic Intelligence, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20794135) carries neither the asterisk nor the '(unverified)' tag. ENUMERATED, not eyeballed: across all 17 improvement lines against all 111 table rows, 6 of 6 lines tagged '(unverified)' have asterisked rows, 9 untagged lines have unasterisked rows, 3a x2 drop the tag but keep the asterisk on the value -- and 3b alone has an asterisked row with neither mark. ADVERSARIAL PASS APPLIED TO OUR OWN CLAIM: the stated legend scopes the asterisk to 'the table below', so the improvement line is not strictly governed by it and the omission is defensible as a changelog entry carrying no status; the claim therefore rests on departure from upstream's own uniform PRACTICE (6 of 6), not on breach of a stated rule, and the finding says so in those words. We do NOT claim the bound is unverified -- only that the two surfaces are out of step and upstream should pick one. A join artifact was caught en route that would have manufactured a second false exception: the [22] improvement line points at a table row labelled [22a], so a naive id-join falsely reports it unmarked; join on label AND slug. Same shape as the correction that became PR #141: one line, checkable, non-mathematical. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-11-the-readme-leg-fires-in-anger.md.
items.closeWhen: David rules send or drop. If send: the adversarial review is already in the finding; a PR against teorth/optimizationproblems README.md follows, and an ACCEPTED one is a dated external ack for G-1/W-3. If drop: close with the reason recorded.

items.title: Two validated branches held for the cross-family review lane — merge alarm-title-honesty BEFORE guard-catch-count-v2
items.note: Both branches are finished, tested and pushed. Neither is merged, and the ORDER matters.  (1) alarm-title-honesty (4153c00) -- the A-5 recurrence fix: UNREACHABLE was titled Drift:, asserting records moved over an HTTP 429. Full account in A-5 note4 and docs/findings/2026-08-17-the-alarm-called-a-rate-limit-a-record-movement.md. HELD because the alarm issue TITLE is the most-read line this repository produces, which puts it squarely in the trusted-print class the cross-family review gate exists for. First use of that lane in this lane returned a boundary error in the exact figure a decision rule consumes that a self-review had missed, so this is not ceremony. Do NOT self-approve it and do NOT run the Codex review yourself -- post the bus request and let the orchestrator run it centrally.  (2) guard-catch-count-v2 (f0fbd41) -- the catch-count guard, which derives the drift-cycle count from mirror history and asserts it against the README own sentence. Reviewed 2026-08-16 (FINDINGS 2, both fixed), and as of 2026-08-17 RUNNER-VALIDATED, which was the whole reason the 8/16 close-out held it: the one environment it had never executed in was a Linux CI runner. It behaves correctly there -- "catch table: UNKNOWN -- shallow clone" plus pass, and the selftest reports history checks SKIPPED.  GETTING IT VALIDATED SURFACED TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING. (a) reverify.yml declares push: branches:[main], so a FEATURE BRANCH GETS ZERO CI RUNS NO MATTER HOW OFTEN IT IS PUSHED -- gh run list --branch guard-catch-count returned an empty list for a branch pushed the day before. workflow_dispatch --ref is the only route. Anyone holding a branch for a runner verdict needs to know that or the hold never ends. (b) main had MOVED under the branch: 58345b8 fixed the state-block CRLF comparison on 8/16 and the branch had independently fixed THE SAME LINES differently, so git merge-tree reported a content conflict. Validating the pre-merge sha therefore answered a question about code that could never have landed. Rebased onto main, conflict resolved in favour of main shipped wording, re-validated locally with both answers and on a runner again. LESSON: before validating a held branch, check it can still merge -- a runner verdict on an unmergeable sha is a verdict about nothing.  MERGE ORDER, and the reason: alarm-title-honesty FIRST. Every push to main triggers reverify.yml, so merging the guard first pushes a network run to main while main alarm is still the dishonest one -- a transport flake would file another false Drift: issue. Land the honest title, then the guard.  ALSO PENDING: delete the superseded remote branch guard-catch-count (dd336d8) once its replacement merges. A force-push to rewrite it in place was declined by the permission classifier, so the rebased state was published as a new ref rather than worked around.  DISPATCH NOTE for whoever merges: RETRACTED CAUSE -- this line previously read "two dispatches in ten minutes tripped raw.githubusercontent secondary rate limiting on 8/17". That attribution is WRONG and was retracted on 2026-08-17: GitHub was in a critical outage from 13:40:03Z, 52 minutes before the first dispatch; a local ~450-fetch run was fully green 48 minutes into it; and the errors included 502 and 503, which request volume does not produce. The PRACTICE guidance below survives the retraction, which is why the line is kept at all (~220 fetches per run, on top of the daily scheduled run). Do not dispatch this workflow repeatedly. items.title: Two non-blocking nits from the PR #21 review lane — count-referent imprecision, and a SKIPPED path that exits 0
items.note: Both raised by the cross-family review lane on 2026-08-18 as explicitly non-blocking; #21 was merged as reviewed rather than re-spun. N-1 (.github/workflows/reverify.yml, around lines 187 and 191): the title says "could not reach N cited source(s)" but the count is of UNREACHABLE CLAIM LINES. Six claims pinning the SAME file that 429s would title "could not reach 6 cited source(s)" when one source was unreachable. Honest in KIND -- it never asserts drift -- but imprecise in count-referent, which is pointed given the PR own theme. Suggested wording: "could not verify N claim(s) (cited source unreachable)", or dedupe by source. N-2 (scripts/reverify.test.mjs, around line 191): on a bash-less machine the alarm leg prints SKIPPED and npm test still exits 0. It is loud -- console.warn plus named in the PASS line -- and CI, the binding environment, always has bash. But house convention elsewhere is that could-not-run gets a distinct exit (rail gates use 2), and THIS REPO OWN 2026-08-17 LESSON is that a guard which cannot run must not report success. N-3 was an observation with no action: join_list sed would also space a comma occurring INSIDE a filename or claim id; none exist today, recorded so a future comma-bearing id does not surprise anyone.
items.note2: BOTH TOUCH TRUSTED-PRINT INSTRUMENTS -- the alarm title and the test that guards it -- so a fix goes through the cross-family review lane rather than being self-approved, the same reasoning that held #21. items.note7_gateResolved2026_09_01: GATE RESOLVED 2026-09-01. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS SETTLED AND THE REGISTERED BRANCH IS SHIP. note4 left the count at 2-against-N_min=3 with one unresolved row sitting exactly on the boundary -- issue #25, filed 2026-08-18T15:57:50Z with a transport-shaped title while NO failed run appeared on 2026-08-18 -- and said in terms that resolving issue 25's originating run IS the decision. It is now resolved, with literal output: gh api repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger/actions/runs/32157521934/attempts/1 --jq .conclusion prints failure, updated 2026-08-18T15:57:53Z, three seconds after issue #25 was filed and on head_sha 95c12f1. Positive control that the endpoint reports real per-attempt conclusions, run on the same run id: attempts/2 prints success. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, and this is the reusable half: gh run list reports only the LATEST attempt, so a run that FAILED and was then re-run to green vanishes from --status failure entirely. Any failure count taken from gh run list systematically UNDERCOUNTS by exactly the re-run population -- which is the population a retry item is about. The registered counting procedure said count from the run logs, and that instrument could not see its own most relevant case. COUNT FOR THE WINDOW since 2026-08-18, transport only: issue #25 (08-18, run 32157521934 attempt 1, 502 on constants/9a.md), issue #28 (08-22), issue #30 (08-25). Issue #29 (08-24) is a real six-file Drift and is correctly excluded; issue #16 (08-17) predates the window and was the GitHub-wide outage. THREE against N_min = 3, so branch 0 does not apply and the registered branch fires: ship a retry with backoff that LOGS every retry it performs. THE LOGGING IS NOT OPTIONAL -- note3 is explicit that a silent retry would have hidden both 2026-08-18 observations, so the flake rate must stay visible rather than being smoothed away. A NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING: before reading onTrigger I had assembled an evidenced case for DECLINE from 61 consecutive green runs and zero transport failures in the last seven days. That is the same error note6 records from 2026-08-27 in the opposite direction -- a same-day judgment overriding this row's own pre-registered discriminator. A pre-registered gate outranks the day's reasoning, including reasoning that feels well-evidenced, and the gate produced the opposite answer to mine.
items.prestage2026_08_31: PRE-STAGED at P4 the day before its 2026-09-01 gate. READ RUN 2026-08-31, both legs: grep -n -i -E retry|backoff|429|502 over scripts/reverify.mjs returns NO MATCHES (exit 1), and the positive control grep -c -i fetch on the same path returns 10, so the probe can match in that file and the empty result is a real absence rather than a wrong path. NOTHING HAS SHIPPED, so the question is still open exactly as posed and the gate is a genuine decision, not a status read. WHAT TOMORROW DECIDES, framed now: a retry layer would make an UNREACHABLE less likely, and the standing invariant is that UNREACHABLE stays RED because unverified must never launder into a pass. Those do not conflict -- retrying is about how hard we try to READ, not about what a failed read reports -- but a retry that swallows a persistent 429 into an eventual success WOULD convert an unverified into a green, which is the thing the invariant forbids. So the shippable form is bounded retry plus unchanged red on final failure, with the KP-78 both-answers test the closeWhen already demands. The alternative is to decline it and record that the daily scheduled run already absorbs transient failure by re-running tomorrow.
items.title: Should the fetch layer retry with backoff on 429/502? — separate from the unreachable-stays-red invariant
items.note: Raised in A-5 note4 and endorsed as separate and real by the review lane on 2026-08-18. The distinction that makes it safe: retry-with-backoff EXTENDS REACH rather than softening a verdict, so it does not conflict with the invariant that an unreachable source keeps the run RED. It is emphatically NOT the forbidden fix -- making a 429 non-fatal -- and this item exists partly so that nobody later mistakes it for one. Today supplied fresh evidence: the push run on 95c12f1 died on a single "fetch constants/9a.md: 502" out of roughly 450 fetches, and a plain re-run passed, which is exactly the shape a bounded retry would absorb.
items.note2: REVIEWER GUIDANCE, adopted: file it as its own tracked item with its own PR and its own test; do NOT ride it on another branch. It touches the network paths of two trusted instruments (reverify.mjs and check-claims.mjs), so it is in-class for the cross-family review lane. Design constraint to carry into that PR: a retry must never convert an unreachable source into a pass. It may only turn a TRANSIENT failure into a completed read, and must still report UNREACHABLE and go red once retries are exhausted. The test therefore needs BOTH answers: a transient failure that succeeds on retry, and a persistent failure that still ends red.
items.closeWhen: Either a reviewed retry-with-backoff ships with a test demonstrating both answers, or the idea is declined with a recorded reason.

items.note8_reviewLanded2026_09_01:
REVIEW LANDED 2026-09-01 AND THIS ROW DID NOT KNOW IT — filed 2026-09-04 at P2. The gap: reDated2026_09_01 says "What is NOT done is the cross-family review that note2 requires ... that is the review lane's timing, not ours". That was true when written and false about four hours later. The review posted at 2026-09-01T23:59:54Z (bus msgId 6ee1a050-e2fc-4bf0-9eea-05aea33d6181), and nothing updated this row afterwards. CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is filed rather than noted in a report: this row's own 09-08 instruction is "if the branch has not been reviewed, surface the LATENCY to the orchestrator as a question rather than merging unreviewed". A cold agent reading the row on 09-08 would raise a latency question about a review that finished a week earlier, while the actual blocker sat unnamed in the ledger. The row would have sent its own reader to chase the wrong thing.

THE VERDICT, quoted from 6ee1a050: "DO-NOT-SHIP as-is — one blocking finding, four should-fix, three nits. NOT merged." A Claude-family reviewer (Opus) read branch a20-fetch-retry-backoff at 8a4c2b8 against main at 81ffb9c in throwaway worktrees. Full review: skylark-site docs/rollups/2026-09-01-bounds-ledger-a20-cross-family-review.md (18.6 KB) — read it whole before touching the branch.

THE RETRY ITSELF PASSED, by mutation not argument, and this is the half that is DONE: removing the retry failed the recovery assertion; faking a 200 on exhaustion failed the persistence assertion (UNREACHABLE flipped to BROKEN, the A-5 shape). Both answers load-bearing. Bounded per call (3 attempts, delays pinned), 4xx and parse errors not retried, no new dependency, no secret path touched, merge-tree clean. So note2/note3/note7 are met; only the ambient ship bar is not.

F1 — BLOCKING (scripts/reverify.mjs:192, scripts/check-claims.mjs:160). The new main-module guard `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url` fails SILENTLY GREEN when the checkout path traverses a symlink or junction, because Node realpaths the ESM entry and not argv[1]. Measured both polarities through a junction: on the branch, reverify.mjs with no args exits 0 with 0 bytes and check-claims.mjs --selftest exits 0 with 0 bytes; on main the same invocations print usage / exit 2 and the selftest PASSes. `npm test` from the junction reported PASS with one of nineteen self-tests never executed. Not reachable on Actions or at C:\dev\skylark\bounds-ledger today; reachable under a subst/junction, /tmp on macOS, some bind mounts. It is blocking on THIS LANE'S OWN RULE — ship no detector without both answers — and A-19 N-2 shipped an exit-2 COULD NOT RUN for exactly this class six days earlier in the same file. Fix shape given in the review: realpathSync the entry; else-branch prints COULD NOT RUN and exits 2; one test through a symlinked path.

F2 — should-fix, same commit (reverify.mjs:44-76). The retry's SILENT half is unguarded: widening RETRYABLE_STATUSES to include 403/404, with the mutation proven landed, left `npm test` green — a 404 returns on attempt 1 with zero retry lines. F3: 429 retried at 500 ms with Retry-After ignored and no jitter. F4: failed fetches are not negatively cached, so a sick transport multiplies per claim. F5: a recovered retry is invisible to the surface note7 just proved cannot count re-runs — emit a run-end `retries: N over M url(s)` tally. F6-F8 are nits.

WHAT IS OWED, and it replaces the "surface the latency" branch: fix F1 (+F2 in the same commit), then merge under this lane's close protocol. The 09-08 date is now a SHIP-OR-SAY-WHY date on a known, specified fix, not a review-latency check. Two reads current as of 2026-09-03 and unchanged: the branch is unmerged (`git branch --contains 8a4c2b8` names only a20-fetch-retry-backoff and its remote) and still merges cleanly (`git merge-tree --write-tree main a20-fetch-retry-backoff` exit 0).

WHY THIS WAS NOT CAUGHT UNTIL 09-04: the review was posted to the bus and read there, and yesterday's report cites it correctly. What no instrument asks is whether a verdict that arrived on the bus reached the ROW it was a verdict about. That is the same shape as 2026-09-04's P1 finding that the day's most important fact lived in a bus message and not in the artifact of record — bus-to-ledger, rather than bus-to-report.

items.title: The fleet stale-actionable filter cannot see this lane parked dates — proposed upward, not ours to ship
items.note: Found 2026-08-19 by checking the kickoff stale-actionable figure of 5 instead of acting on it. the fleet endpoint helper skylark-site/src/lib/continuity-endpoints.ts (hasFutureDateInCloseWhen, line 523 — that path is skylark-site as it sees itself and does not resolve at our HEAD) scans only closeWhen and item.notes. This lane writes prose into note/note2..note9 (singular, numbered) so item.notes is UNDEFINED on all 14 open items, and parks items in expectedSignalBy which the filter never reads. Measured: all five flagged items return futureDatesInCloseWhen=[] while W-3 carries expectedSignalBy 2026-09-24 and W-6 carries 2026-11-06. filteredCount:0 is therefore structural, not an observation — no item in this lane can ever be excluded as parked.
items.note2: Why it is not cosmetic: the kickoff threshold is >3 = a real P4 forced-decision pass, so an uncorrectable figure sits directly upstream of owed work, and every pass re-derives the same answer (keep waiting). That is the founding defect — an alarm that cannot report the negative teaches the next reader to ignore it.
items.note3: PROPOSED FIX and the half to refuse: add the TYPED expectedSignalBy field to the scanned text, one clause. Do NOT also widen the scan across the note* prose family — those fields are narrative (W-3.signalNote alone names two dates), so any stray future date would park a genuinely neglected item, converting a false positive into a false negative, which is the more dangerous direction. Smaller and strictly more correct than the larger change.
items.note4: SCOPE: that helper belongs to skylark-site and is a trusted-print instrument feeding a threshold, so it is in the cross-family review gate class. Proposed upward in the 2026-08-19 P1 retro; NOT shipped from this lane. This row exists because W-7 rule says a recommendation routed elsewhere gets its tracker row in the same commit as the report proposing it.
