items.title: The bus sha-file-claim linter reads sha-to-filename ADJACENCY as a modification claim — 3 false WARNs on one post, proposed upward
items.note: Found 2026-08-20 while posting the 2026-08-19 retro (bus msg 92c994bd-e29f-4ef3-94eb-dd9f99e0ffab). agent-status printed three sha-file-claim WARNs, all false. Verified with git show --stat, the command the WARN itself prescribes: cb4f6f5 touches package.json ONLY (the WARN named check-brief.mjs, verify-with-receipt.mjs, tmp/.verify-receipt.json); dd336d8 touches scripts/render-state-block.mjs (the WARN named check-posted-unpushed.mjs); f362ce7 touches README.md plus scripts/render-state-block.mjs (same WARN). Positive control: all three --stat reads returned NON-EMPTY file lists, so the reader was working and the named files are genuinely absent because they were never claimed to be present.
items.note2: The defect is the RELATION, not the parse. Prose names a commit and a filename near each other for at least four reasons and the linter collapses them to one: (a) the commit MODIFIED the file; (b) the file is the DETECTOR that flagged the commit — check-posted-unpushed.mjs flagged dd336d8, and a detector and its subject are correctly different files; (c) the file lives in ANOTHER REPO and cannot appear in this repo file stat by construction — verify-with-receipt.mjs is at ../skylark-site/scripts/; (d) the file is gitignored and written at RUNTIME — tmp/.verify-receipt.json. Only (a) is a claim worth linting.
items.note3: Why it is not cosmetic here: cb4f6f5 shipped the previous day specifically to stop a WARN firing on every post from this lane, and its own commit body argues that a WARN which fires on every post from this lane forever is how a warning becomes noise — the founding defect in another hat. A retro doc is dense in exactly the (b), (c) and (d) shapes, so this linter fires hardest on the posts that most need reading. Second fleet trusted-print instrument in two days after A-21, and the same class: a scan pointed at the wrong relation.
items.note4: NOT SHIPPED FROM THIS LANE and no fix proposed beyond the diagnosis — the linter belongs to skylark-site agent-status and is a trusted-print instrument, so it sits in the cross-family review gate class. This row exists per the W-7 rule: a recommendation routed elsewhere gets its tracker row in the same commit as the report proposing it. The retro message itself was NOT superseded — its content is correct and the WARNs are wrong.
items.closeWhen: The orchestrator either narrows the linter to modification claims (then this lane re-posts a retro-shaped body and confirms 0 WARNs), or rules the current breadth intended — either answer closes it. A silent non-response does not.
items.signalDateNote: One week. Silence by 2026-08-27 means dropped rather than declined — the W-7 failure. Surface it, do not silently re-file.
items.note5: CLOSED EARLY 2026-08-22, five days before its 2026-08-27 gate, on an orchestrator relay: the sha-file-claim meta-class was FIXED UPSTREAM in skylark-site da9b984d (an upstream-repo sha; it does not resolve in this repo). Quoting a WARN in a post is now safe, and [linter-report] covers the other detectors. This is the answer the onTrigger asked for, arriving early — the onTrigger said either answer closes this and only SILENCE would have needed surfacing as a W-7 failure. Disposition recorded here rather than carried to 8/27, per the relay. NOT re-verified from this lane: da9b984d is in another repo and the fix is the orchestrator’s read, not ours — recorded as relayed, not as independently confirmed.
items.note6: ORCHESTRATOR RULING 2026-08-22, recorded here because the close on the same day was mine and rested on a narrower reading. RULED: the current breadth is INTENDED for now. A filename beside a commit sha IS a modification-claim shape by construction; the upstream carve-out exempts only QUOTED linter output (its own tag, or an explicit [linter-report] marker). The remaining false-positive class — prose naming a file the commit does not touch, on the sha's line — is real, is shared by at least one other lane, and its proper fix is SYNTACTIC ATTACHMENT, which sits on the orchestrator's substrate menu and is not a lane item. So A-22 closes per its own second leg ("or rules the current breadth intended") rather than the first. WHAT I GOT WRONG AND WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING: I closed this in P2 on a relay that the meta-class was fixed, then read the WARN that fired on my own P3 post as a RECURRENCE of the defect. It was not — it was the linter working as designed under a ruling that had not been made yet. The close also skipped its own verification leg (re-post a retro-shaped body, confirm 0 WARNs); P3 ran that leg by accident and got 1, which under this ruling reads as CONFIRMATION of intended breadth rather than failure. INTERIM WRITING RULE until attachment ships: keep a filename either inside a [linter-report] quote or off the sha's line. Not a licence to reword posts to dodge the linter — gaming a detector is the same defect wearing the other hat.
items.note7: SECOND OCCURRENCE, on the P2 post about this very row (bus 17c12cb6, 2026-08-20T14:30Z), and it adds a FIFTH relation the linter collapses. The flagged sentence said AGENTS.md command list did not carry npm run verify, wired yesterday by cb4f6f5. The WARN reported that cb4f6f5 touches neither AGENTS.md nor CLAUDE.md — which is TRUE and is precisely the defect being reported: the commit and those files are related by ABSENCE, the file that failed to record the commit. So the relation list is now (a) the commit modified the file — the only lintable one; (b) the file is the detector that flagged the commit; (c) the file is in another repo; (d) the file is gitignored and written at runtime; (e) the file is the one that SHOULD have recorded the commit and did not. Case (e) is the sharpest argument for narrowing rather than loosening: a documentation-gap report is a sentence that names a commit beside a file it deliberately does not touch, so the linter fires hardest on reports of exactly the defect it is adjacent to.
items.note8: Frequency now measured rather than guessed: 3 WARNs on the 2026-08-19 retro, 0 on the A-22 status, 0 on the P1 retro, 1 on the P2 post. It is NOT an always-on warning — consistent with note5 both-answers finding — but it recurs whenever a post does careful cross-referencing, which is the posts most worth reading. No re-file; this is evidence on the open row, and the 2026-08-27 date stands unchanged.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-27, check whether the orchestrator has either narrowed the sha-file-claim linter to modification claims or ruled the current breadth intended. Either answer closes this. SILENCE DOES NOT — surface the silence itself as the W-7 failure mode in that day report, naming this row, and do not silently re-file it under a new id or a fresh date.
items.note9:
DISPOSITION of the dd336d8 citation, recorded 2026-08-21 after the orchestrator's morning unpushed-claim read classified it ABANDONED ARTIFACT (reflog-only) and asked that the citation stop dangling. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, and the classification is CORRECT: dd336d8 exists as a commit object, no branch contains it, and 'git ls-remote --heads origin' returns only f2-lookup-surface, f2-public-page and main. NO WORK IS LOST -- it was the head of the superseded 'guard-catch-count' branch, replaced by f0fbd41 on 'guard-catch-count-v2', which is merged and on main. The two are not byte-identical (patch-ids differ), so this was checked rather than assumed: the whole delta is comment wording plus one inlined variable, and both forms compare content with the identical expression next.replace(/
/g,"
") === readme.replace(/
/g,"
"). Nothing in dd336d8 is absent from main. Do NOT push it -- A-17's note already ruled that the superseded branch be deleted rather than rewritten in place, and that deletion is now confirmed complete. THE CITATION IS NOT A CLAIM AND WAS NEVER PENDING WORK: dd336d8 appears in this item as EVIDENCE -- one of the three commits the bus sha-file-claim linter falsely WARNed on, quoted precisely because check-posted-unpushed.mjs had flagged it and the linter misread detector-and-subject adjacency as a modification claim (relation (b) in note2). So the morning read has now flagged the very commit whose only citation is an example of a different instrument false-positiving on that same commit. THE STANDING CONSEQUENCE, which is the actionable half: a reflog-only sha quoted as evidence inside a tracked file will be re-flagged EVERY morning, and a recurring alarm that is correct-but-not-actionable is this lane's founding defect wearing a third hat. The fix is NOT to delete the evidence and NOT to back-edit the earlier notes, which are a record of what was found on the day and should stay as written. This note is the single authoritative label instead: any future reader or morning read that lands on dd336d8 in note or note2 resolves it here. If the same sha is re-flagged a third time, the finding is that a disposition note is not reachable by the check that keeps raising it -- and THAT is the thing to fix, not the citation. Second occurrence noted: the same commit was flagged on 2026-08-20 and re-reported 24h later, so this is recurrence, not a first sighting.
items.note10: FOURTH FALSE WARN, 2026-08-21, and it has a property the first three did not: IT FIRED ON THE POST EXPLAINING THIS DEFECT. Posting the dd336d8 disposition task-complete (bus 6a09e3de) produced 'sha-file-claim: commit dd336d8 touches NONE of the file(s) named beside it (check-posted-unpushed.mjs)'. That is relation (b) from note2 exactly as predicted -- the file named beside the sha is the DETECTOR THAT FLAGGED IT, and a detector and its subject are correctly different files -- so note2's taxonomy is now VALIDATED BY PREDICTION rather than only asserted from three cases. THE NEW AND LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY: this class of WARN cannot be authored around. A sentence explaining that check-posted-unpushed.mjs flagged dd336d8 must name the detector beside the sha, because that adjacency IS the fact being reported; there is no rewording that states it without producing the pattern. So every future diagnosis of this defect -- including the one owed by 2026-08-27 -- will itself WARN while being written, and any 'did the WARNs stop' read taken over posts about the linter will be structurally wrong. Consequence for the fix: the linter cannot be evaluated on a corpus that includes its own bug reports, and a suppression keyed on wording would silence exactly the posts that document it. Second consequence, already recorded in note9: dd336d8 has now been flagged by TWO separate instruments (check-posted-unpushed.mjs on 08-20 and 08-21, this linter on 08-20 and 08-21) for the same non-defect.

items.title: Classify each window findings as record-facing or instrument-facing, and name what the FIRST record-facing catch would look like
items.note: APPROVED 2026-08-20 as specified in the P1 retro: ONE SENTENCE of human judgment per report, and explicitly NEVER a counter over docs/findings/. A counter is inflatable exactly like a self-rating, which this lane already refused to build; the guard against inflation is that a human reads the window and nothing counts it.
items.note2: Why it was needed: for three consecutive days every catch this lane produced was in the MACHINERY around the ledger — the parked-item filter (A-21), the sha-file-claim linter (A-22), the verify-receipt gate, the retype corruption — and none in the mathematics. npm run catches reads 0 movements while docs/findings/ is not dry, so the 2026-08-14 amendment correctly says we are not in a drought. But that amendment cannot tell a record-facing finding from an instrument-facing one, and a lane that only ever finds defects in its own tooling is maintaining itself rather than stewarding records.
items.note3: ORCHESTRATOR ADDITION, and the part with a deadline: in the NEXT report, name what the FIRST record-facing catch would look like — what record, what class of drift, what would flag it. One sentence. It converts we-would-recognise-one-if-we-saw-it from an assumption into a claim, which is the only form that can be wrong.
items.note4: What it lets us decide that today it cannot: whether adopt-a-second-surface is the right response to a quiet stretch. Four instrument-facing findings beside zero record movements is a different situation from four record-facing findings beside zero movements, and the current dry-week rule treats them identically.
items.closeWhen: The 2026-08-21 report carries both the one-sentence classification AND the named shape of a first record-facing catch. Then this converts to a standing convention in CLAUDE.md and closes.
items.signalDateNote: Tomorrow, because it is a deliverable in the next report rather than a wait on anyone. If the 8/21 report ships without it, that is this row failing in the same way W-7 was created to catch.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-21, the report must carry BOTH the one-sentence record-facing-vs-instrument-facing classification AND the named shape of a first record-facing catch (what record, what class of drift, what would flag it). If the report ships without them, this row has failed in exactly the way W-7 was created to catch — say so in the report rather than rolling the date. If it carries both, convert the classification to a standing convention in CLAUDE.md and close this.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-21, both halves shipped in that day's report and verified by running the linters rather than by reading the draft (8/8 clean). (1) THE CLASSIFICATION: every finding the lane produced on 2026-08-21 was instrument-facing, the FIFTH consecutive such day, and the report names all five -- a disposition of our own abandoned commit, a linter's fourth false WARN, a stale onTrigger inside a closed row, an incomplete close procedure, and a README quotation that claimed to be verbatim and was not. The last record-facing catch was 2026-08-14, 87a.md's record row citing a witness that proves the PREVIOUS record. (2) THE NAMED SHAPE, written as a claim so it can be wrong: the next record-facing catch will be a witness-value mismatch on a constant upstream added within about thirty days -- the number right, the attached certificate proving a different value -- because the newest pages have had the least review and upstream's own README says the repo is AI-assisted with citations to be verified. AND NOTHING WE RUN AUTOMATICALLY WOULD FLAG IT: a witness mismatch is byte-stable, so the mirror diff sees nothing, the pins match, and the catches indicator correctly reads zero. It takes a human recomputing a cited certificate, which is how BOTH record-facing catches this lane has ever produced were found. The falsifiable half is explicit: if the next one arrives through an alarm, the prediction was wrong and the report says to correct it. Converted to a standing convention in CLAUDE.md in the same commit, as closeWhen required.

items.title: A STACKED pull request gets zero CI runs — b1 fixed the branch case and left the stacked-base case open
items.note: Found 2026-08-20 by hitting it. reverify.yml declares `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and that filter matches the BASE branch. PR #27 is based on f2-lookup-surface, not main, so it received zero checks — `gh pr checks 27` reports "no checks reported on the branch", exactly the innocuously blank page b1 was written to eliminate. PR #26, based on main, got both jobs. Positive control: the same command returned two passing checks for #26 seconds earlier, so the reader was working and #27 genuinely has none.
items.note2: This is b1 own defect in a new shape, and the irony is located precisely: the comment block that documents b1 sits directly above the `branches: [main]` line that reintroduces the gap, and it warns that "a hold whose release condition has no executable command outlives its reason". A stacked PR held for review is exactly such a hold.
items.note3: FILED, NOT FIXED, deliberately. Widening the filter is a change to the CI trigger of the workflow the G-1 streak is measured on, and the 2026-08-20 ruling puts substrate behind product inside a 20% budget. The release command exists and is now written into the workflow comment where the next person will find it: `gh workflow run reverify.yml --ref <branch>`. Used once for #27 (run 32393859115) after checking the branch still merges, per the do-not-dispatch-repeatedly rule.
items.note4: DECIDE, do not drift: either widen the pull_request filter so stacked PRs get runs, or rule that stacked PRs are dispatched by hand and keep the command documented. Both are defensible; leaving it undecided is what is not.
items.closeWhen: Either the trigger is widened and a stacked PR is observed receiving checks automatically, or the hand-dispatch route is ruled the intended workflow. A silent non-response does not close it.
items.signalDateNote: Two weeks. Not urgent — the release command is documented and works — but an undecided gap in the CI trigger of the workflow the streak is measured on should not sit indefinitely.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-03, ask the orchestrator for the DECISION, not a fix: widen the pull_request base-branch filter so stacked PRs get runs, or rule that stacked PRs are hand-dispatched. Either closes this. Until then any stacked PR is validated with `gh workflow run reverify.yml --ref <branch>` after confirming it still merges — that command is already written into the workflow comment where the next person will look, so this row is not blocking anything.
items.readCommand: grep -n -A 2 "^  pull_request" .github/workflows/reverify.yml — literal output 2026-08-25: "pull_request:" then "branches: [main]". That is the still-open half: a PR whose BASE is main gets a run, and a STACKED PR whose base is another feature branch still gets ZERO. Positive control that the file has the triggers this reads: the same grep for "^on:" returns schedule, workflow_dispatch and push.
items.resolution: FORCED AT P4 2026-08-27, taking the second branch of closeWhen: the hand-dispatch route IS the intended workflow for a stacked PR, and this row closes DECIDED rather than aging further. The alternative was widening reverify.yml's `pull_request: branches: [main]` filter to all bases so a stacked PR gets checks automatically. Rejected on cost we have already measured: one run is ~450 requests (113 raw fetches plus ~110 claim URLs), it shares a rate-limit budget with the scheduled run the streak is measured on, and AGENTS.md already carries an explicit rule against dispatch churn. Widening the trigger would spend that budget on the rare case (this lane has had exactly one stacked PR, #27) to save one command. THE COMMAND IS THE FIX AND IT IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED: `gh workflow run reverify.yml --ref <branch>`. What made #27 dangerous was never the missing run, it was that `gh pr checks 27` renders an innocuously BLANK page rather than a red one, so absence looks like health -- and that is a reading trap, addressed by AGENTS.md's standing line that an empty check list on a branch is configuration and not a missing run.

items.title: Give deferrals an expiry field and a check that reads it — so stale blocker #4 announces itself
items.note: ORCHESTRATOR PUSH 2026-08-20, and they are right that three recurrences is past the point where another prose note helps: "A deferral written in prose has no expiry, no owner and nothing that reads it — so it survives its own cause by days and only dies when a human happens to re-read the sentence." Named as the candidate Section A substrate action for 2026-08-21.
items.note2: THE EVIDENCE IS THIS REPO. Three stale blockers, each caught only by a human re-reading prose: F-2 public-flip blocker (corrected 8/17, the gate had cleared 8/08); A-7 claiming the repo was private (corrected 8/16); and F-2 deferred because "two diffs are queued in the review lane" — those merged 8/18 and it was found 8/20, two days late, INSIDE the document that names the stale-blocker pattern and instructs that closing a gate must include a sweep for text that cited it.
items.note3: SHAPE, and the common case is machine-checkable: a deferral cites a PR number, an issue, a gate or a date. The fleet already has waitJustification {until, loadBearing, unWait, owner}. The check reads the condition and fires when it no longer holds — an open PR that merged, a date that passed. It does NOT need to parse arbitrary prose; it needs to refuse an undated, unconditioned deferral in the first place.
items.note4: PLACEMENT WARNING, learned from the primer gate today: a check that is red whenever any deferral is outstanding is a permanently-red alarm and carries as much information as a permanently-green one. This must fire on EXPIRY, not on existence.
items.closeWhen: A deferral in this repo carries a machine-readable un-defer condition and something on a rail evaluates it, demonstrated with both answers — it fires when a cited condition has lapsed, and stays silent when the condition still holds.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-21 this is the candidate Section A. If P3 ships it, close this. If P3 ships something else because a user-visible product item outranked it under the 80/20 ruling, RE-DATE ONCE with the reason stated — but do not let it become the fourth thing this lane defers in prose, which would be the joke writing itself.
items.note_redate: RE-DATED ONCE 2026-08-21, 08-21 -> 08-25, using the single re-date its own onTrigger allows and stating the reason as that onTrigger requires. REASON: P3 shipped f421ea6, the README's first screen showing a real catch verbatim, because a user-visible product item outranked substrate under David's 80/20 ruling of 2026-08-20 -- which is the exact condition the onTrigger names. THE RE-DATE IS NOW SPENT. This row's own text warns against becoming 'the fourth thing this lane defers in prose, which would be the joke writing itself', so on 2026-08-25 it ships or it is closed as declined with a reason -- it does not roll again. Design already approved by the orchestrator today as retro item b1 and NOT re-litigated: the check reads TWO fields, expiresOn AND releaseTest, and fails when either is missing; it also treats an open PR whose body says HELD with no 'Release:' line as the same finding. Approved success signal, which is also the KP-78 both-answers demonstration: run the finished check against 2026-08-20 state and it must go RED on PRs 26 and 27, then silent once A-27's releaseTest and the two PR-body Release lines exist -- both of which landed today in b63391b, so the red case and the green case are BOTH already reproducible from history.
items.readCommand: grep -c '"expiresOn"' continuity/items.json — counts deferrals carrying a machine-readable expiry. 0 means nothing has one and the item is unshipped. Use the KEY form with quotes, NOT a bare word grep: `grep -c "expiresOn"` returns 1 today, and that one hit is A-25's own note_redate prose DESCRIBING the field, so the word-form probe reports the feature as present precisely because it is absent and being discussed. Positive control that the probe can see a real key: grep -c '"expectedSignalBy"' returns 23.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-25 — SHIPPED as scripts/check-deferrals.mjs, on the approved design and without re-litigating it: it reads expiresOn AND releaseTest, fails when either is missing, and also treats an open PR whose body says HELD with no release line as the same finding. The note4 constraint is honoured and is asserted rather than merely intended — it fires on EXPIRY and on MALFORMEDNESS, and is SILENT on a well-formed unexpired deferral however many exist, because a check that is red whenever anything is outstanding is the permanently-red alarm this lane was founded on. Wired into npm test, npm run check and a CI self-test step (17 self-tests now present in CI, up from 16; reverify.test.mjs verifies that count so a new self-test cannot skip its workflow step). The --prs leg exits 2 rather than 0 when gh is unavailable, applying A-19 N-2 lesson in new code the same day, and it stays OFF the CI rail for that reason. TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, both by testing against real artifacts instead of fixtures. (1) The first draft required a literal "Release:" line and PASSED its own selftest against fixtures this file invented; run against the actual bodies of PRs 26 and 27 it reported a finding on BOTH, because the form this lane already uses is a bold "Release test" heading. A predicate tested only against a retyped copy of what you expect tests the retyping — the fixtures are now the verbatim opening of PR #26. (2) The module had no entry-point guard, so importing it to reuse the predicate RAN the check and could process.exit() out of its importer: that is F2 from the PR #26 review, the same omission in new code the same week, caught because the demo importing the predicate printed the check own verdict above its own. KP-78 both answers demonstrated on the LIVE path with real data, not only fixtures: baseline exit 0 silent; expiresOn moved into the past exit 3 EXPIRED; releaseTest removed exit 3 MALFORMED; file restored byte-identical afterwards from an in-memory copy rather than git checkout, because the fix under test was uncommitted and checkout would have discarded it. A-18 is its first real subject, so the gate is not sweeping nothing.

items.title: Author the evangelism-bar doc this repo lacks and record a loopArchetype — dated, because a gap reported three days running is the stale-blocker pattern in another hat
items.note: ORCHESTRATOR 2026-08-20: both gaps confirmed real and worth naming, "but do not let them sit as a standing note that gets re-reported every day". Absent from BOTH bounds-ledger/docs/ and ../skylark-site/docs/ (named so the claim is falsifiable); no loopArchetype anywhere in this repo, grepped across *.json and *.md.
items.note2: IT IS A CONSOLIDATION, NOT RESEARCH. The material already exists in docs/key-user-flows.md: the core problem in the user own words ("I cited a number. I have no idea if it is still the current one") and the would-tell-a-friend moment ("the ledger caught a drift the field own index missed"). What is missing is the file the fleet expects and the metric that proves movement.
items.note3: Write it against G-3 rather than against a funnel — the Tier-0 goal from G-1 close is whether someone outside uses the ledger, so the bar and the goal should say the same thing in different words.
items.closeWhen: the evangelism-bar doc this repo lacks exists carrying the one core problem, the would-tell-a-friend moment and the metric, and a loopArchetype is recorded where the fleet reads it — or a deliberate decision is recorded that this lane has no meaningful loopArchetype and why.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-25 write it or record why not. Do NOT re-report it as a gap a fourth time without doing one or the other — that is precisely the pattern A-25 exists to kill, and re-reporting it while A-25 is open would be this lane demonstrating the defect it is trying to fix.
items.note4: REFERENCED BY ABSENCE, and the filename is written in prose rather than path form on purpose. check-doc-references extracts path-shaped tokens and resolves them at HEAD, so naming the missing file in path form made THIS ROW a dead reference — the fifth deliberate-absence flag from that checker on 2026-08-20 (three in the primer draft, two here). The tool has no convention for "named because it does not exist yet". This is not dodging a false positive: a reader at HEAD genuinely cannot follow that path, so prose is the more accurate form. Adjacent to A-25 and worth raising if that work is picked up.
items.readCommand: ls docs/ | grep evangelism-bar ; grep -rc '"loopArchetype"' continuity/items.json continuity/health.json — absent file plus 0/0 means unshipped. KEY form again, for the same reason as A-25: a bare `grep -rl loopArchetype` matches continuity/health.json and continuity/items.json today, and BOTH hits are A-26's own title and its generated "suggested" line, so the loose probe reads as shipped while nothing exists. Positive control: grep -c '"expectedSignalBy"' continuity/items.json returns 23. NOTE on the shape: this deliberately greps a directory listing rather than naming the file path directly. check-doc-references.mjs scans continuity/items.json and reads a literal docs/<name>.md as a REFERENCE, so the first version of this command turned the dead-reference check red on 2026-08-24 — the probe was flagged for citing the very absence it exists to detect. A permanently-red checker is this lane's founding defect, so the probe changed rather than the checker. Positive control that the listing form still works: `ls docs/ | grep key-user-flows` returns key-user-flows.md, exit 0; the evangelism-bar form returns nothing, exit 1.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-25 — WRITTEN, not re-reported. The evangelism bar now exists under docs/ and meta.loopArchetype is recorded as "citation-check" in this file. THE CORE PROBLEM is verification, not discovery: "I cited a bound and a referee told me it had been improved — I had no way to know." THE MOMENT is a lookup that tells a user something about their own citation they could not have known without redoing the work, and the third label ("first pinned — unchanged since") carries as much of it as the first, because before 2026-08-24 all 222 rows read as though something had happened on their bootstrap date. THE LOOP ARCHETYPE is the load-bearing finding and it disqualifies the portfolio default metrics: a tool used at citation time SHOULD have a poor D7-return-rate, and optimising that would push toward engagement mechanics that make the product worse. THE METRIC IS DECLARED NOT MEASURABLE and deliberately so: the page has no analytics, the 14-day sample reads about 3 unique viewers against 180 unique cloner-days, and the clone figure is largely our own CI, so it fails number-provenance rule 2 outright. Rather than write a retention target against a number nobody can read, the doc names the smallest instrument ladder — count the existing per-row report clicks over time, then get any coarse denominator, then and only then a share-rate. The doc also states what would make this NOT worth telling a friend (coverage, the record-versus-listing distinction, and low frequency), because a bar that lists only successes is decoration. Recorded in items.json rather than the generated health.json, which a regeneration would silently drop.

items.title: Does a materially amended outward artifact go back to David before it sends?
items.note: FOUND IN P2, 2026-08-21, as a continuity gap rather than a new question: this was flagged honestly when it arose on 2026-08-20 and then recorded ONLY inside A-16 (closed) and the primer's closing paragraph. An unresolved question about the OUTWARD GATE, parked in a closed row, is invisible -- nothing would ever surface it again, and it binds the next outward send whenever that happens. THE QUESTION: David's instruction on A-16 was "report it - show me the draft". He saw the draft; the adversarial review then refuted five of seven angles and required seven amendments, and WHAT ACTUALLY WENT TO teorth/optimizationproblems#150 WAS MATERIALLY DIFFERENT FROM WHAT HE READ. Under the precedence rule in force, the flag was correct and the send was legitimate. But if he meant "show me the draft" to mean "before it goes", then a materially amended artifact should return for a second look.
items.note2: STANDING INTERPRETATION UNTIL HE RULES -- adopt the CONSERVATIVE default, do not leave it open-ended: if an outward artifact is materially amended AFTER David has seen it, it goes back to him before sending. Cost of being wrong in this direction is one extra message; cost in the other direction is that he learns what we sent in his name by reading it upstream. The outward gate already requires his explicit approval per send, so this is a narrowing of an existing gate, not a new one. "Materially amended" means the CLAIM, the METHOD SENTENCE, or the CHANNEL changed -- not wording or compression. On A-16 all three moved, so that send would have returned under this rule.
items.onTrigger: Do NOT card this to David as a hypothetical -- he answers better on a live artifact than on a policy question, and this lane sends outward artifacts roughly twice a month. Instead: AT THE NEXT OUTWARD SEND, after his approval and after the adversarial review, ask him once, briefly, in the same message that shows the amended artifact -- "the review changed X; do you want a second look before this goes, as a standing rule?" That converts the question into a one-line confirmation at the exact moment it is concrete. If 2026-09-22 arrives with no outward send having occurred, do not let the row expire silently: re-date it once with that reason. The conservative default in note2 governs every send in the meantime, so nothing is blocked while this is unanswered.
items.closeWhen: David has answered the one-line question at a LIVE outward send — "the review changed X; do you want a second look before this goes, as a standing rule?" — and the answer is recorded as a standing rule either way. A yes closes it as a rule (amended artifacts re-gate); a no closes it as a rule (his first approval covers post-review amendments). BRANCH 0, and it is the likely branch: IF NO OUTWARD SEND HAS OCCURRED BY 2026-09-22, the discriminator is INAPPLICABLE — the question cannot be asked live because the moment it attaches to never arrived. This lane sends roughly twice a month, so zero sends in a 32-day window is a real possibility, not a technicality. On that branch do NOT card it to David as a policy hypothetical (the onTrigger forbids that, and the reason is that he answers better on a live artifact): re-date to the next send window and record that the window was empty. Re-dating on Branch 0 is legitimate precisely because the gate is event-driven rather than time-driven — but it must SAY the window was empty, so an unfillable wait cannot hide as a pending one. Two consecutive empty windows means the outward channel itself has gone quiet, and THAT is the finding to surface instead of the original question.
items.closeWhenNote: ADDED 2026-08-22 at close-out, after the continuity check flagged MISSING_CLOSE_WHEN. The row already had a good onTrigger and no criterion for being done — a watch with a response procedure but no exit is a stall in costume, which is the exact shape this lane keeps finding. Branch 0 is written in because the trigger is an EVENT (an outward send), not a date, and without it a zero-send window would silently collapse into "still watching" forever.

standingPatternWaived.reason: FALSE POSITIVE, waived rather than reworded, 2026-08-22. The detector matched the phrase "standing rule" inside this row's closeWhen and read it as the item declaring ITSELF never-closeable. It says the opposite: the ANSWER becomes a standing rule, and either answer CLOSES this row — a yes means amended artifacts re-gate, a no means the first approval covers post-review amendments. The pattern guards against an open row that can never close and therefore trips overdue scans forever; W-8 has a concrete close condition, an explicit Branch 0 for the zero-send window, and a review clock at expectedSignalBy 2026-09-22, so that risk is not present. WAIVED, NOT REWORDED, deliberately: rewording to slip past a phrase match is gaming the detector, which this lane refused to do earlier the same day when the sha-file-claim linter fired on a P3 post. Same defect class as that one — a scan matching ADJACENCY rather than the relation it cares about — and the honest disposition is to record why the match is wrong where the next reader will find it.

items.readCommand: gh issue list --repo teorth/optimizationproblems --author u00dxk2 --state all --limit 5 # SEPARATOR CONVERTED 2026-09-02 (bonus cycle), em dash to hash. W-8 asks whether a materially amended outward artifact returns to David before sending, and NO COMMAND CAN ANSWER THAT: the answer exists only in something David says, and note2 records the conservative default governing every send until he does. What IS checkable is whether the question has gone live again, i.e. whether we have sent anything since 2026-08-21. Literal output 2026-08-26: #150 (closed 2026-08-23), nothing newer. USE THE ISSUE LIST, NOT gh pr list: our most recent outward artifact is an ISSUE, so a PR-only query returns #141 from 2026-08-05 and is BLIND to the very send this row is about — that miswrite was caught here on 2026-08-26 by running the command before writing it down. POSITIVE CONTROL: the listing must contain #150; an empty list means the query is wrong, not that we have never sent.

items.title: Two PRs held for the cross-family review lane — merge #26 then #27, then enable Pages
items.releaseTest: gh pr view 26 --repo u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --json number,state,reviewDecision,comments; gh pr view 27 --repo u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --json number,state,reviewDecision,comments; grep -c 'Review-lane verdict' tmp/.bus-events.jsonl
items.note: OPENED 2026-08-21 BECAUSE NOTHING OWNED THESE PRs. A-17 owned the previous held stack and CLOSED on 2026-08-18; PRs #26 and #27 were opened on 2026-08-20 with no open row tracking them. Today's P1 then found that no surface a next agent could read said a review had ever been REQUESTED for them — no request ID in-lane, no verdict on the bus, empty reviewDecision and zero comments on both — while this lane's own convention (A-5 note7 records "the review requested (bus f2cbd000)") demonstrably leaves evidence when followed. THE REQUEST IS NOW POSTED: bus 160f0567-4c22-43c1-8250-bba1df789972, 2026-08-21, covering main..f2-lookup-surface (PR #26, cb6b437) and f2-lookup-surface..f2-public-page (PR #27, 89636d0), declared class trusted-print instrument plus public surface. It states up front that nobody has viewed index.html rendered in a browser, and asks the lane to render it if it can.
items.note2: THIS ROW IS THE MECHANISED FORM OF TWO PROCESS RULES APPROVED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR TODAY, recorded here rather than only in prose because prose is what failed. (a1) A HOLD NAMES ITS RELEASE COMMAND, NOT ITS RELEASE CONDITION — hence the releaseTest field above, which is runnable and answers "has the review returned?" without anyone inventing a test. The 2026-08-21 primer named "if the review lane has returned" as the gate on this lane's largest user-visible ship FOUR TIMES and never once said how to evaluate it, which is b1's own lesson recurring one day after being written down. (a2) THE HOLD AND THE REQUEST ARE ONE ACTION — hence reviewRequestId, populated in the same turn the request was posted. The gap between them is invisible from inside the lane because a held PR looks correctly held whether or not anyone was asked.
items.onTrigger: Run releaseTest. THREE OUTCOMES. (1) A verdict has landed: apply any pre-merge fixes, merge #26 FIRST and #27 second — the order is not cosmetic, #27 is stacked on #26 — then enable GitHub Pages, which is deliberately OFF until a verdict exists because publishing first would defeat the gate. (2) No verdict by 2026-08-24: ask the orchestrator ONCE, briefly, quoting the request ID; do NOT re-post the request, and do NOT self-approve the review — the outward gate is not waivable by impatience. (3) The lane replies that it cannot render index.html in a browser: treat a human browser check as a merge precondition and say so, rather than shipping a page whose layout nobody has seen. RE-CHECK MERGEABILITY BEFORE ACTING on any outcome — main moves daily; both branches were git merge-tree clean against main at 69c6e4b on 2026-08-21, and a verdict on an unmergeable sha is a verdict about nothing.
items.releaseTestNote: VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT, 2026-08-21, not by reading it. The first draft of this field used jq string interpolation and did NOT survive the JSON round-trip into this file -- it printed the literal template '#(.number) reviewDecision=(.reviewDecision)' instead of any value. A release command that does not run is the exact defect this row exists to fix (2026-08-18: a documented first command that had never been executed by anyone), reproduced inside the fix for it. This form has no escaping to survive. READ IT AS: both PRs still state OPEN with reviewDecision null and 0 comments, and a verdict grep count that has not risen, means the review has NOT returned. Any of those moving means it has. BASELINE RECORDED 2026-08-21T14:5x MT by running it: PRs 26 and 27 both state OPEN, reviewDecision empty, comments 0, and the verdict grep returns 2 -- those two are historical verdicts for OTHER branches (catch-rate.mjs and guard-catch-count), not for this stack. So the signal is the count rising ABOVE 2, or either PR gaining a reviewDecision or a comment. Without the baseline written down, a next reader seeing 2 could read it as this stack having been reviewed twice.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-21 -- the full onTrigger path ran, in order, the same day the row was opened. The cross-family review lane returned needs-changes with ONE blocking defect and the browser render nobody here could get. F1 (HIGH): lookup.mjs handed `git log -S` the DECODED expect string while claims.json holds JSON-escaped bytes, so every LaTeX-bearing row -- 159 of 222 pins -- could never be dated, and the CLI then printed 'unknown (no history available in this checkout)' on a FULL clone, a trusted-print instrument asserting a false reason for its own silence. Reproduced before fixing (pin:2a:U null; 63 of 222 dated), fixed with the JSON-encoded needle, proven after (pin:2a:U 2026-08-12; 222 of 222 dated; a fabricated expect still null). The reviewer's independently measured 63 matched exactly. Also fixed: F2 the missing entry-point guard in render-site.mjs, proven both ways (invoked, selftest runs; imported, index.html byte-unchanged); F3 the pin-uniqueness assumption stated in the code; F4 the inert position:sticky removed rather than repaired; F5 the footer's hard-coded 'Two claims' roster count now derived from claims.json; F6 a favicon data URI killing the only console error. CAUGHT WHILE FIXING F4: the first version of the explanation sat in a CSS comment INSIDE the style template literal and shipped the entire review narrative to every visitor -- found by grepping the generated page for it, and the note now lives in the source. Merged #26 (3c35247) then #27 (7748804); #27 had to be RETARGETED from f2-lookup-surface to main first, because the base branch was not deleted and GitHub therefore did not auto-retarget -- merging it as-was would have landed the page on a dead branch rather than on main. GITHUB PAGES ENABLED, which was this row's pre-registered final step and the condition the whole hold existed to protect: https://u00dxk2.github.io/bounds-ledger/ serves HTTP 200 and is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed index.html, verified with positive controls (the H1, the upstream sha, a constant name, 222 last-changed spans, the favicon) rather than on the strength of a 200, which this repo does not accept as evidence of having fetched the artifact. Negative control: no dead CSS and no review narrative in the served bytes. The page carries its record-refusal in the served copy -- 'These are last-listed table rows, not a claim about which bound is the record.'

items.title: Does this lane's detection method find what the lane exists to find?
items.note: THE QUESTION, stated as the orchestrator framed it 2026-08-23. Seven consecutive days of instrument-facing catches, last record-facing catch 2026-08-14. The standing prediction says the next record-facing catch will be a witness-value mismatch on a constant upstream added within ~30 days, found by A HUMAN recomputing a cited certificate and flagged by NO INSTRUMENT WE RUN. Read back as a statement about the lane rather than about the next catch, that prediction says our instruments will not find the thing this lane exists to find.
items.note2: WHY IT GETS A CLOCK RATHER THAN A CARD. Seven days is not a verdict — a record-facing catch may simply be a rare event on a slow clock, and the prediction carries its own ~30-day window. The failure mode is not being wrong; it is letting 'instrument-facing again today' accumulate as an observation that never becomes a finding. This row is the date that conversion happens.
items.note3: CLOSE CONDITION. On 2026-09-22, one of three: (a) a record-facing catch has landed — record HOW it was found, and if an instrument flagged it the standing prediction was WRONG and says so; (b) still none, and the instrument-vs-record ratio becomes a FINDING about detection method, not another daily classification line; (c) the question is inapplicable because upstream itself went quiet — in which case say the window was empty rather than reading it as a detection failure, and check npm run catches for movements over the same window before concluding anything.
items.note4: DO NOT let this become a counter. The classification is one sentence of human judgment per report, never a tally — a counter over docs/findings/ is inflatable exactly like the self-rating this lane refused to build. This row watches the QUESTION, not a number.

items.closeWhen: (a) A record-facing catch has landed: close, recording HOW it was found — and if an instrument flagged it rather than a human, the standing prediction was WRONG and the close says so. (b) Still none: close by CONVERTING the observation into a finding about detection method, which is the whole point of the clock. (c) Upstream itself went quiet over the window: close as INAPPLICABLE, saying the window was empty rather than reading it as a detection failure — check the movement count first, since zero movements and zero record-facing catches are the same fact, not two.
items.note5: INSTRUMENT CAVEAT, found the same day this row was created and worth more than the row. My first onTrigger pointed at docs/findings/, which is where the fleet's dry-week rule also points — and that directory had been empty for four days while the lane was actively finding things, because the standing files the classification in the daily REPORT and only the larger findings get their own file. A watch whose instrument under-reports produces a confident false negative, which is the exact failure this lane exists to police. AGENTS.md's catches entry was corrected the same day.
items.note6: FIRST DATA POINT, same day the row was created — and it lands on the other side of the question. A real drift arrived at close 2026-08-23 (8a4192a) carrying TWO verified record movements: 15a's matrix multiplication exponent 2.371339 -> 2.371177, and 3a's Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa lower bound 1.1835129324 -> 1.19102809. The mirror diff caught both within hours, on a routine gate run, exactly as designed. SO THE INSTRUMENTS DO FIND MOVEMENTS, RELIABLY AND SAME-DAY. What they have never yet found is a DEFECT in a record - a cited certificate that proves a different value - which is what the standing prediction is about. Keep those two apart when reading this row on 2026-09-22: 'our detection method works' and 'our detection method finds the thing the lane exists to find' are different claims, and today only settled the first.

items.note7: STANDING PREDICTION RESHAPED 2026-08-27 (orchestrator refine). The previous one was a FOUR-CLAUSE CONJUNCTION — type x age-of-constant x finder x channel — so its expected accuracy was the product of four guesses, and it duly came out wrong on every clause. Its one good part was the falsification clause, which is kept. NEW PREDICTION, one clause with its base rate beside it: 2 of the last 3 record-facing catches were upstream self-corrections of citation metadata, so THE NEXT ONE IS MORE LIKELY CITATION THAN NUMBER. SELF-MODEL CLAUSE, which is the half whose error changes what we build: I predicted the last one would be 'flagged by a human recomputing a cited certificate and by no instrument we run', and the scheduled byte-diff caught it unaided. So I now predict the next one is ALSO caught by the existing byte-diff with no new instrument required — and if instead it needs a human read, that is evidence the detection layer has a gap worth building into, and it gets said out loud rather than absorbed. FALSIFICATION: if the next record-facing catch is a bound moving, or arrives by a route no current instrument watches, say so plainly and correct the base rate.
items.predictionInstance2026_09_03:
THE STANDING PREDICTION NOW HAS ITS FIRST CONCRETE ADDRESS — recorded 2026-09-03 on the orchestrator's instruction, because the durable part is the prediction-with-an-instance rather than the day it was noticed.

THE PREDICTION, restated so this note stands alone: the next record-facing catch will be a witness-value mismatch on a constant upstream added within ~30 days, found by a HUMAN recomputing a cited certificate and by NO instrument we run. It has held once (2026-08-20). If the next one arrives via an alarm instead, say so and CORRECT the claim rather than quietly counting it.

THE INSTANCE: constants 88a and 88b, added upstream 2026-09-02, four days old at the time of writing. Two properties make them the predicted population rather than merely new. (1) 88a carries the bounded prime gap chain with $246$ [Pol14b] superseded by $240$ [Sta26], a Stadlmann preprint of 31 August 2026 — a live record claim, not a settled one. (2) 88a's own provenance note says, in upstream's words, that it was "Prepared with assistance from Claude Opus 5" from the arXiv abstract and HTML introduction, and that "No bound was independently verified." That is upstream disclosing its method, NOT a defect, and it must not be reported as one — but it is precisely the shape the prediction points at, because no instrument this lane runs can check a witness value against a cited paper.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, either way: a human recomputes the cited chain against [Sta26] and [Pol14b]. A mismatch confirms the prediction and is a record-facing catch. A clean recomputation refutes nothing on its own — the prediction is about where the NEXT catch comes from, not about these two constants being wrong — so record the negative result and leave the prediction standing.

WHAT THIS NOTE IS NOT: an assertion that anything upstream is wrong. Nothing has been recomputed. Baseline for the quoted values: grep -n "246\|240" ledger/teorth-optimizationproblems/constants/88a.md, read 2026-09-03.

items.title: reverify.test.mjs alarm-title leg failed once and would not reproduce
items.note: Seen once during a routine gate run on 2026-08-23: the alarm-title assertion expected /^Drift: constants/2a.md/ and got the generic fallback 'Re-verification failed: bounds-ledger (2026-08-23)'. npm run verify exited 1, correctly. Not reproduced in 10 consecutive runs immediately after (2 by hand, 8 looped), tree clean throughout.
items.note2: NOT the 2026-08-17 failure mode. That one had the guard spawn bash, fail, and return an empty string, so an absence assertion passed against nothing. Here the title was a real, well-formed fallback, meaning the alarm path RAN and chose the generic branch. Recorded because that distinction is the useful half and would be lost by next month.
items.note3: CAUSE NOT DIAGNOSED, deliberately. The fitting story is that the synthetic mutation into 2a.md did not land — the CRLF trap this repo keeps hitting — which would leave no per-file drift and produce exactly this fallback. It fits and it has precedent, which is why it is not written down as the cause: the 2026-08-17 incident put a plausible self-blaming story into six surfaces before anyone checked it, and it was wrong.
items.note4: WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO TRACK. The alarm's title is what a steward reads in the first three seconds, and this lane already has a finding about a mistitled alarm (2026-08-17, a transport failure titled as a record movement). This guard is part of what was built to stop that recurring, so it flickering is not noise. A flaky test costs a retry; a flaky TITLE costs a missed record movement.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-22, check whether it recurred. If it did, the finding names the three steps: capture the failing state BEFORE re-running, check with git diff --numstat whether the synthetic mutation landed, then decide test-defect vs alarm-defect.
items.closeWhen: (a) It recurred and was diagnosed: close naming the cause and the fix. (b) It never recurred: close as 'seen once, never again' — a legitimate outcome that must be RECORDED as that rather than the row quietly deleted, because a second sighting a year from now needs this one to exist.
items.readCommand: node scripts/reverify.test.mjs # SEPARATOR CONVERTED 2026-09-02 (bonus cycle), em dash to hash. read the alarm clause of its PASS line. items.title: The Mathstodon announcement has been ready-and-unsent for 11 days, has no board card, and its figures have gone stale
items.note: FOUND 2026-08-24 by the P4 waits-sensibleness gate, test 1: a David-wait must name a live board card. The Mathstodon announcement — the lane's first deliberate arrival move, drafted 2026-08-13 at docs/decisions/2026-08-13-mathstodon-announcement.md, adversarially reviewed the same day (docs/findings/2026-08-13-mathstodon-adversarial-review.md, nine angles, SURVIVES with six amendments applied) — has NO card on David's board. Read live: the board holds 95 cards across 18 projects and bounds-ledger is not among them, established with a positive control (8 cards match "skylark", so the search demonstrably matches). W-6's noteArrival says it was "carded as ready-state only after the review passed". Which of those two diverged CANNOT be established from here and is not claimed: the card may have been created and later removed, or never created at all. What is certain is that there is no card now and the send has sat eleven days.
items.note2: AND THE ARTIFACT DECAYED WHILE IT WAITED, which is why the gate's prescribed action — card it now as ready-to-send — is the WRONG action today. Three figures in the draft are stale after eleven days: it says "231 claims re-verified on every push" (now 233), "~230 pinned claims" (222 generated plus 11 hand claims), and "Between 24 July and 12 August 2026 the alarm fired on eight upstream changes" (eleven resolution cycles as of 2026-08-24, the eleventh being f5b5589 today). Number-provenance floor rule 1 applies with unusual force here: a ledger whose entire product is noticing that cited numbers have gone stale must not announce itself with three stale numbers. Sending it as drafted would hand a mathematically literate audience an artifact that fails the exact test the artifact is advertising.
items.note3: WHY THIS IS FILED AS ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE. It was living as noteArrival on W-6, a watch about whether the report-an-error channel gets used — a different question. That is precisely the shape W-7 was opened to catch and closed today by shipping: a prepared thing living only in prose inside another item is invisible to a pass that reads items. The eleven-day silence is the evidence that it worked exactly as W-7 predicted. Note also that the decay direction is asymmetric: every day this waits, the draft's figures get further from true, so re-dating it without refreshing the figures makes it worse rather than merely later.
items.closeWhen: Either the draft is refreshed to current figures AND carded for David with a ready-to-send body, or the arrival move is struck with a recorded reason. A third re-date without refreshing the figures is not an available outcome, because the figures decay with every day of waiting.
items.signalDateNote: The weekly forced-decision pass, which is a Monday (checked, not assumed: 2026-08-31 is a Monday, as were 08-17 and 08-24). Deliberately NOT dated 2026-08-25 — four gates already come due that day and CLAUDE.md is within 340 bytes of its size budget, so adding a fifth would guarantee the shallowest of the five gets the least thought.
items.readCommand: grep -n "231 claims\|~230 pinned\|eight upstream changes" docs/decisions/2026-08-13-mathstodon-announcement.md — each hit is a figure that was true on 2026-08-13 and is not true now; an empty result means the draft has been refreshed. Cross-check the live values with `node scripts/render-state-block.mjs --check` (claim and file counts) and `git log --oneline -- ledger/teorth-optimizationproblems/manifest.json` minus the two non-drift commits named in README's catch table (cycle count). Then read the board for a card: the search is `curl -s -H "x-cc-pin: $CC_PROMPTS_PIN" https://skylarkcreations.com/api/cc/david-board` filtered for "bounds-ledger", and it MUST be run with a positive control (filter for "skylark" and expect a non-zero count) or a zero proves nothing about the board.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-08-31, do ONE of two things and record which. (a) Refresh the three stale figures against live reads, re-run the adversarial review ONLY if the refresh materially changed the argument rather than the arithmetic — W-8 is the watch that governs that judgment — and card it for David with the send as the ask. (b) Strike the arrival move with a recorded reason. Do not card the draft as-is: it currently asserts three numbers that are no longer true, and this lane exists to notice exactly that class of defect.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-28 by option (a) of this item's own onTrigger, taken in full: the figures were refreshed against live reads, the adversarial review WAS re-run (correctly — the trigger required it only if the refresh materially changed the argument rather than the arithmetic, and the argument changed entirely: the post was rebuilt around the 2026-08-27 retraction on David's instruction), and it is being surfaced to David with the send as the ask. All three stale figures this item named are gone, and the replacement is structural rather than a patch: "231 claims" and "~230 pinned claims" collapsed into one approximate "~230 pinned claims, all but two re-checked daily", and "between 24 July and 12 August 2026 ... eight upstream changes" became "between 24 July and 27 August 2026 ... twelve upstream changes" inside a CLOSED window. No figure in v2 can decay, which is the durable answer to this row rather than a re-dating. The board-card half of the finding was answered by events: David raised the post himself on 2026-08-27, so the missing card stopped mattering. THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS ROW is the one in note3 — a prepared artifact living only as prose inside another item (here, W-6's noteArrival) is invisible to any pass that reads items, which is what W-7 was opened to catch. New artifact: docs/decisions/2026-08-28-mathstodon-announcement-v2.md; review: docs/findings/2026-08-28-mathstodon-v2-adversarial-review.md. The live send decision continues on A-15, which David reopened.

items.title: secret_scanning_validity_checks will not enable via API — likely a paid Secret Protection entitlement, so it is David's call
items.note: FROM THE 2026-08-25 ENGINEERING-HEALTH RIDER, whose remedy ordered validity checks BEFORE dismissing the two fixture alerts, on the reasoning that dismissing without them leaves the NEXT alert equally ambiguous. Step 2 could not be completed. The dismissals were done anyway and that is recorded as a deliberate departure, not an oversight: the two alerts were confirmed inert by reading the exact blob they point at, which is stronger evidence than a validity check could give (a validity check asks whether a token is LIVE; these are not well-formed tokens at all), and dismissing forecloses nothing — a future alert gains validity data the moment the setting flips.
items.note2: WHAT WAS ACTUALLY OBSERVED, because a silent no-op is easy to misreport as an error. PATCH repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger with security_and_analysis.secret_scanning_validity_checks.status=enabled returns HTTP 200, exit 0, and the response body's OWN security_and_analysis block still reads disabled. Tried twice with different encodings — gh's bracket -f form and an explicit JSON --input body — with identical results, so this is not an encoding fault. GitHub accepts the request and refuses the field. Repo permissions show admin true, so it is not a token-scope problem either.
items.note3: LIKELY CAUSE, STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT AS A FINDING: validity checks are part of GitHub Secret Protection / Advanced Security. Public repos get secret scanning alerts free; validity checks are a paid add-on. That would explain a 200 with a silently ignored field. NOT VERIFIED — no positive control was available, because there is no second repo on this account known to have the feature ON against which the same call could be shown to succeed. Do not repeat the hypothesis as established without that control.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-08 either confirm the entitlement hypothesis with a positive control, or close this as not-available-on-this-plan. If it turns out to cost money, that is David's decision and not a self-approved purchase — surface it as a decision with the price, never as a blocker to be cleared.
items.readCommand: gh api repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger --jq '.security_and_analysis.secret_scanning_validity_checks.status' # SEPARATOR CONVERTED 2026-09-02, em dash to hash, because this gate fires 2026-09-08 and the runner would otherwise execute the whole 900-byte field instead of the command. Returns disabled while unshipped, enabled when done. Positive control that the probe reads a real field: the same query with .secret_scanning.status returns enabled, so a disabled reading is the setting's state and not a missing key or a silent jq failure.
items.closeWhen: Either secret_scanning_validity_checks reads enabled (gh api repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger), or the row closes as declined-with-reason. A paid Secret Protection add-on is a SPEND decision and therefore David's, and it is deliberately NOT carded: the control is not currently exploitable here — this repo has zero dependencies by design and touches no credential outside the CI-injected GITHUB_TOKEN — so asking him to buy it now would be a bad ask. RE-ARM: if a dependency or a written credential ever enters this repo, the spend question goes live and gets its own card that day.

items.title: Adopt gen-primer-first-action.mjs so the primer's mechanical sections are re-derived instead of inherited
items.note: ORCHESTRATOR-OFFERED 2026-08-25 as the structural remedy for the morning's primer contradiction: two close-out sections gave OPPOSITE instructions about the day's first move (compression first / the constraint is gone, do not compress), both correct as history, and the session read roughly 4,000 words before it knew what its day was. The argument for the generator is that a generated block cannot carry two contradicting conventions, because it is not appended to. Prose is preserved inside hand:begin markers.
items.note2: NOT ADOPTED TODAY, and the reason is scope rather than doubt. The engineering-health rider plus the P2 continuity work had already spent the ~20% Section B frame, and swapping the primer's generation path is a change whose failure mode is losing a primer — the very artifact tomorrow's cold start depends on. It had a destructive bug earlier today (a sibling lane found it), FIXED on skylark-site as 04b9ef42, and I verified that fix is an ancestor of my checkout rather than merely present in the object database, so the blocker is not safety. Deferred in the machine-readable form rather than as a prose note, per A-25.
items.note3: PARTIAL CREDIT ALREADY TAKEN, so do not read this row as nothing having been done: the (a1) change shipped in ce23254 puts READ THE GATE READCOMMANDS BEFORE THIS PROSE as the primer's own first line, which addresses the ordering half of the same problem by hand. The generator addresses the contradiction half, which the hand fix cannot.
items.note4: SECOND HAND FIX SHIPPED 2026-08-26 (P2), which narrows again what the generator still has to earn. The orchestrator approved the as-of rule out of this morning's P1 and flagged it a portfolio candidate: a hand-written statement of a live instrument's value carries an AS-OF and its read command, never a bare present tense. Recorded in CLAUDE.md section Conventions. THREE instances inside 24 hours forced it, all the same shape and none attributable to a careless author. (1) The primer's CI-RED banner was TRUE when committed in e06027e at 22:25:32Z and false seventeen seconds later, when the push of that very commit produced a green run; issue 30 closed at 22:27:43Z and a further commit at 23:06Z did not touch the primer. (2) The 2026-08-25 daily report called A-18 the only declared deferral while this row was declared 82 minutes later in d016af6. (3) The primer said the deferral gate reads 1 in one section while naming both A-18 and A-30 in another, a contradiction inside a single document. WHAT THE AS-OF BUYS: a stale statement reads as history rather than as a false claim, and the release command tells the reader how to refresh it. That is the whole of what a hand fix can do here. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, and why this row stays open rather than closing on partial credit: an as-of does not stop two close-out sections from giving OPPOSITE instructions, because both can be honestly timestamped and both remain true as history. That is still the generator's half, and it is untouched.
items.note5: PRE-STAGED 2026-08-26 (P2), and the onTrigger's conditional FIRED. The generator HAS moved since this row was filed: skylark-site ef3cf6b1 (gen-primer-first-action: the provenance stamp was a dead reference in every lane) landed after 04b9ef42. onTrigger says that in exactly this case the destructive-bug fix must be re-verified as an ancestor of the local checkout before the generator is run against a real primer — done today: git -C ../skylark-site merge-base --is-ancestor 04b9ef42 HEAD exits 0, so the fix is present and safety is NOT the blocker on 2026-09-01. Carry what ef3cf6b1 actually was into the adopt-or-decline argument, because it cuts both ways: it is a SECOND defect found in this generator after the first, and it was a dead reference affecting EVERY lane rather than a local misconfiguration. That is evidence about the generator's maturity for the decline side, and evidence that it is being actively maintained and fixed fleet-wide for the adopt side.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-01 either adopt it or close this as declined with a reason. Run the release command first: if the generator has moved again, re-verify the fix is an ancestor of the local checkout before running it against a real primer, and dry-run --check (read-only since 04b9ef42) before any write.

items.title: Should the public page publish be CI-gated? It is not, and a malformed page reached main today
items.note: MEASURED 2026-08-26, not inferred from config. This lane has no Render service and therefore no autoDeployTrigger=checksPass to fail open — which reads as the safe answer and is not. GitHub Pages legacy builds fire on PUSH and wait for nothing. Timestamp pair on a settled commit: the Pages build for c25cecd was created 2026-08-25T23:06:53Z and its CI run started 23:06:55Z, so the publish was created TWO SECONDS BEFORE CI began. Corroborated during the outage: HEAD carried 0 check-runs while Pages still created a build for every commit (7 check-runs on the settled prior c25cecd is the negative control).
items.note2: WHY IT MATTERS, with today's near-miss as the evidence. render-site.mjs --check is the gate that catches a malformed index.html, and it runs in CI IN PARALLEL WITH THE PUBLISH rather than ahead of it. Commit 784e4f4 carried an index.html whose first 45 bytes had been clobbered — no doctype, no html element — because render-site.mjs WRITES the file itself and was invoked through a shell redirect that also wrote to it. On any ordinary day that page publishes in about two minutes. The ONLY reason it never reached a visitor is that GitHub Pages was erroring in an unrelated outage, and a direct fetch confirmed the served page was still the well-formed c25cecd build. THAT IS LUCK, NOT A GATE, and this row exists so nobody records it as the gate working.
items.note3: THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, not a decision: Pages build_type 'workflow' instead of 'legacy', with the check ahead of the deploy step. NOT ATTEMPTED 2026-08-26 because Pages was in degraded_performance all afternoon and changing the publish path during an outage means diagnosing a new failure against a broken baseline. ALSO WEIGH THE OTHER SIDE: an ungated publish has never actually published a bad page in this repo's life, and a workflow-based publish adds a failure mode (the workflow itself) to the one surface a visitor sees. This is a real trade, not an obvious fix.
items.closeWhen: Either the publish is gated (Pages build_type reads 'workflow' via gh api repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger/pages, and a deliberately malformed index.html is DEMONSTRATED to be refused before publish), or the row closes as declined with the trade in note3 stated as the reason. A state read alone does not close it — KP-78 applies: the gate must be shown to refuse a bad page.
items.signalDateNote: Two weeks, deliberately not sooner: the decision needs Pages out of degraded_performance first, and there is no urgency while local npm run verify is the floor and every commit passes it before push.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-09 decide rather than re-date. If Pages is healthy, either implement build_type workflow with a demonstrated refusal, or close declined citing note3's trade. If a malformed page has reached a visitor in the meantime, that outranks the trade and the answer is gate it.
items.readCommand: gh api repos/u00dxk2/bounds-ledger/pages --jq '.build_type' # SEPARATOR CONVERTED 2026-09-02, em dash to hash, because this gate fires 2026-09-09. Returns 'legacy' while ungated, 'workflow' once gated. Literal output 2026-08-26: legacy. POSITIVE CONTROL that the endpoint is live rather than erroring silently: the same object's .html_url returns https://u00dxk2.github.io/bounds-ledger/ and .status returns a build state; an empty or null build_type means the read failed, not that no gate exists.
items.note4: P4 2026-08-27 — EXPLICITLY HELD on its stated date 2026-09-09, not silently re-carried, and the hold is now cheaper because the concrete risk was mitigated today by other means. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: .githooks/pre-commit now runs `node scripts/render-site.mjs --check` on a staged index.html and refuses the commit if the page is not what render-site would produce. That closes the window at COMMIT time, where it costs nothing, instead of at publish time, where it costs a publish-path rewrite. KP-78 both ways, at the hook layer: prepended a CLOBBERED line to index.html, proved the mutation landed (`git diff --cached --numstat` -> 1 line), and the commit was REFUSED at exit 1 with 'index.html is stale'; restoring the good file left the stage clean. WHY THE BIG QUESTION STILL WAITS: switching Pages to build_type=workflow changes the publish path of the ONLY surface a visitor sees, AGENTS.md says not to attempt it while Pages is degraded, and Pages was erroring in a GitHub outage as recently as 2026-08-26. The residual risk after today is narrow and named: a malformed page can still reach main via a route that bypasses the hook (a direct push from a clone with hooksPath unset, or a merge commit), and CI still reports it only after publish. That is the real remaining case A-31 must answer on 09-09.

items.closeNote: CLOSED 2026-08-31, BOTH HALVES, each with the command that decided it. items.title: A mid-run 429 becomes up to 339 requests in two seconds at the limiter already refusing us
items.note: FILED FROM THE A-20 CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW, finding F3, at P4 on 2026-09-02 rather than left in the review doc. The review is at ../skylark-site/docs/rollups/2026-09-01-bounds-ledger-a20-cross-family-review.md and is NOT in this repo, which is exactly why this row exists: this lane has seven recorded instances of a resolved-or-pending thing surviving only in text nobody re-reads, and a rollup in another repo is that shape.
items.note2: THE DEFECT, as measured by the reviewer. scripts/reverify.mjs sets RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [500, 1500] and retries 429 like any other transient status. Three things compound: 500 ms cannot succeed against either retried GitHub surface, both of which signal rate limiting in seconds-to-minutes via Retry-After and x-ratelimit-reset; the delays carry no jitter; and fetchUpstream runs CHUNK = 10 concurrently, so ten fetches retry in lockstep. Before the A-20 branch, 113 file fetches with one failure went red honestly. After it, a mid-run 429 becomes up to 339 requests inside about two seconds, aimed at the limiter that is already refusing us — and GitHub's own secondary-rate-limit guidance counts an immediate retry as a further violation.
items.note3: WHY IT IS NOT A-20's SCOPE AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED INTO IT. The orchestrator scoped 2026-09-02 to F1 and F2, and widening a directed scope silently is the failure mode this lane treats as its own. A-20's discriminator is spent and resolved to SHIP; this is a separate question about HOW the retry behaves under the one status in the set with no measured instance behind it. Note the reviewer's own observation: the three transport failures A-20 counted were a 502 and two claim-source-unreachable events. 429 is the status where blind retry is actively harmful and the one we have never actually observed.
items.note4: THE TRAP TO AVOID WHEN FIXING IT. Do not 'improve' this by making a 429 non-fatal or by swallowing it — AGENTS.md: never make a 429 non-fatal, because UNREACHABLE is unverified and a green there launders an unverifiable into a pass. The fix is about REQUEST VOLUME and TIMING, not about the verdict. Whatever lands must leave a 429 that survives its retries still going RED.
items.signalDateNote: One week, and deliberately AFTER A-20's own 2026-09-08 forced review of the review, so the two are read in the right order: A-20 decides whether the retry stays at all, and this row only matters if it does. Not sooner because nothing is on fire — the branch is unmerged, so the defect is not in main and cannot fire today. Not later because the moment F1/F2 merge, it is live on the daily alarm's own fetch path.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-09, first ask whether the retry shipped at all — if A-20's branch is still unmerged this row is INAPPLICABLE and should be re-dated to follow it, not closed. If it did merge: honour Retry-After capped at some ceiling, add jitter, and treat 429 differently from 502/503 rather than folding it into one set. Prove the fix with a test that a 429 does NOT produce concurrent lockstep retries, and prove the instrument can fail by asserting the un-jittered version does.

The obvious form, a plain grep over scripts/reverify.mjs, reads the WORKING TREE and was actively misleading on the day this row was filed: an uncommitted Codex edit had the retry constants in the tree while committed main had none, so the plain grep printed three hits and the honest answer was zero.
