POSITIVE CONTROL, the same command against the branch that has it: git grep -c RETRY_DELAYS_MS a20-fetch-retry-backoff -- scripts/reverify.mjs prints a20-fetch-retry-backoff:scripts/reverify.mjs:3 at exit 0. So exit 1 here means absent-from-main, NOT a broken pattern or a wrong path — the control proves the pattern matches when the thing is there. When this command starts printing a count against HEAD, the retry has merged and this row is live.

items.title: A change to a file we have filed an upstream report against is a CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT, not a text edit — the classifier reported the lane's own top-goal event as noise
items.note: ORCHESTRATOR-DIRECTED 2026-08-26, and filed as a checkable item rather than a discipline note at their explicit instruction. THE GAP, stated as what actually happened: on 2026-08-23 an outside contributor fixed constants/87a.md citing our issue #150, and Terence Tao closed that issue as completed. Our mirror INGESTED the fix — 87a.md moved inside the 5c4aeee snapshot taken 2026-08-24 — and the page's change classifier labelled it 'text edited, bound unchanged', which is CORRECT as a description of the bytes and wrong as a description of the event. The instrument watched the exact thing G-3 (the Tier-0 goal that someone outside Skylark uses the ledger and acts on it) exists to detect, and reported it as routine. It was found by accident on 2026-08-26 while writing an unrelated readCommand.
items.note2: WHY THE CLASSIFIER IS NOT AT FAULT AND STILL MUST CHANGE. changeKind() compares the bound cell and answers 'did a number move'. That is a good question and it answered it correctly — no number moved, because the correction attached the right WITNESS to an unchanged record value. The defect is that nothing else asked the second question: is this file one WE reported against? The classifier had no way to know, because the filed-report list exists only in prose scattered across item resolutions.
items.note3: DESIGN, cheap leg first. LEG 1 (the one that would have caught this, and the cheaper): poll the STATE of every outward artifact we have filed. `gh issue list --repo teorth/optimizationproblems --author u00dxk2 --state all` returns our reports and their states; a report that has gone CLOSED since the last check is a candidate causal event and must be surfaced, not silently true. This catches an acknowledgement even when no file changes at all — a maintainer can close a report by disagreeing. LEG 2 (the orchestrator's framing): key a small map of upstream path -> filed issue number, and have the drift/change classifier label any movement in a mapped file CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT rather than value/text. Both legs are needed and they fail differently: leg 1 misses a fix that lands with the issue left open, leg 2 misses an acknowledgement that touches no file. DO NOT auto-close anything on either — the output is 'go look', never a verdict, because deciding that a change was CAUSED by our report is a judgment.
items.note4: PLACEMENT WARNING, same shape as A-25 note4. This must NOT become a permanently-red alarm: once #150 is closed it stays closed forever, so a check that fires on 'a filed report is closed' fires every day from now on. It must fire on the TRANSITION — state changed since the last recorded state — which means the recorded state lives in the repo and gets committed when the finding is dispositioned. A check that cannot go quiet again is the founding defect of this lane wearing a new hat.
items.closeWhen: Both legs ship with KP-78 demonstrated on each: leg 1 fires when a recorded-open report is found closed and is SILENT on a report whose state is unchanged; leg 2 labels a movement in a mapped file as a candidate causal event and leaves unmapped files reading value/text exactly as now. The 2026-08-23 event is the natural fixture for both — it is real, it is dated, and the classifier's wrong answer on it is reproducible from the snapshot history.
items.disposition2026_09_02: GATE FIRED AND IS PARTIALLY DISCHARGED — re-dated three days, and the honest account is that I did not ship what onTrigger asked for. onTrigger said ship LEG 1 at minimum. Leg 1, the transition poller, is NOT built. What DID ship (4c2fd97, live and verified on the published page) is a THIRD thing the row did not name: the reader-facing disclosure. Every public-page row we filed an upstream report against now links that report and its state, so on 87a the page shows 'text edited 2026-08-23 — bound unchanged' directly beside 'we reported this row · closed 2026-08-23'. That juxtaposition IS this row's finding, handed to a reader rather than to us. Also shipped: ledger/upstream-reports.json, which is exactly the recorded baseline leg 1 needs in order to fire on a TRANSITION rather than on the permanent fact that 150 is closed (note4). So leg 1 is now a small job against an artifact that exists, instead of a job that had to invent its own state store. DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: leg 2's CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT label, and not for cost — on a public page that label publishes a judgment about causation, which note3 forbids in terms. The disclosure form was chosen over it, permanently, and leg 2 should be read as internal-only if it is ever built. RE-DATED rather than closed because the row's own closeWhen requires BOTH legs with KP-78 on each, and one of them does not exist. Three days, not a week: the remaining work is small and the baseline is fresh.
items.signalDateNote: One week. Not sooner because David's ruling on G-3 may change what the check is FOR — if he raises the bar, this becomes the instrument that feeds the higher threshold rather than a post-hoc explanation of a close. Not later because the gap is live: another upstream report could be acted on tomorrow and we would find out the same way, by accident.

items.prestage2026_09_01: PRE-STAGED the day before its 2026-09-02 gate, so tomorrow reads a decision rather than starting a dig. READ RE-RUN TODAY, output above: still exactly one row, issue 150, closed 2026-08-23. NOTHING HAS CHANGED since the field was written on 08-26, so the gap this row describes is still open and still unsurfaced by any instrument. WHAT TOMORROW DECIDES, framed now: this asks whether a change to a file we have filed an upstream report against should be treated as a CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT — i.e. whether our own outward artifacts should be cross-referenced against the drift alarm, so that a mirror change to constants/87a.md is read beside the fact that we filed issue 150 against exactly that file. The shippable form is a cross-reference at drift time, not a new alarm. THE CAUTION THAT MUST RIDE WITH IT, and it is G-4's whole condition: an event whose causal path contains an artifact we authored and sent CANNOT satisfy G-4. So this cross-reference is a tool for reading drift honestly, and any hit it produces is explicitly NOT a G-4 arrival. Building it must not blur that line -- if anything, it makes the line easier to hold, because it names our own artifacts rather than leaving them unlabelled in the drift stream.

items.leg1Shipped2026_09_04:
LEG 1 SHIPPED 2026-09-04, a day before this row's gate, at the orchestrator's instruction to start it today rather than tomorrow morning. scripts/check-upstream-reports.mjs, npm run upstream.

WHAT IT DOES. Reads the baseline in ledger/upstream-reports.json, lists our filed issues live (gh issue list --repo teorth/optimizationproblems --author u00dxk2 --state all), and diffs by issue number. It reports three things and no verdict: a state TRANSITION since the recorded baseline (CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT, output is "go look"), a live report of ours with no baseline row (UNRECORDED, because a store that silently omits our own artifacts looks complete and is not), and a recorded row absent from the listing (NOT IN LISTING, framed as suspect-the-query rather than as a deletion, since the listing is filtered by author and repo).

NOTE4 IS THE DESIGN AND IT IS TESTED, NOT JUST OBSERVED. It fires on the TRANSITION, never on the standing fact that #150 is closed — that check would fire every day from now on, and an alarm that cannot go quiet is this lane's founding defect. KP-78, two mutations, both proven landed and both restored byte-identical: M1 made the transition invisible (`if (false && ...)`) and tripped "a state transition must fire — it is the only thing this checks"; M2 made it always fire (`if (true || ...)`) and tripped "an unchanged state must not fire — this alarm has to be able to go quiet". M2 is the one that matters here: an assertion set that only proved firing would have left the dangerous direction untested. Clean run exit 0.

LIVE READ AT SHIP: 1 recorded report, 1 live row, 0 transitions — issue 150 CLOSED 2026-08-23T17:15:35Z, identical to the baseline. Exit 0, silent. That is the correct answer today and it is also the positive control that the differ ran rather than failing early: it names the counts it compared.

WIRING. The selftest is network-free and joins the offline battery plus a matching reverify.yml step; reverify.test.mjs now reports 22 self-tests present in CI across 28 workflow steps, which is the guard confirming the wiring rather than my say-so. The LIVE run needs gh auth against someone else's repo and stays OUT of CI, alongside npm run traffic and npm run reports. An unreachable listing exits 2 as UNREACHABLE and says in terms that this is not evidence nothing moved; the catch prints a fixed string and echoes nothing from the failure.

LEG 2 IS NOT SHIPPED, and the one-line reason onTrigger asks for: its public form was permanently declined on 09-02 because a CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT label on a public page publishes a judgment about causation that note3 forbids in terms, and its internal-only form has no subject while leg 1 covers the same events more directly.

CLOSE DECISION DELIBERATELY LEFT TO TOMORROW'S GATE. closeWhen requires both legs with KP-78 on each, and leg 2 is declined rather than built, so closing today would need that judgment made a day early on a row that is not yet due. The work is done and recorded; 09-05 decides close-with-leg-2-declined versus re-date, against a row that no longer has to start with a dig.
items.disposition2026_09_05:
GATE FIRED, AND THE DAY ANSWERED IT DIFFERENTLY FROM THE WAY THE PRIMER FRAMED IT. The framing was close-with-leg-2-declined versus re-date. RE-DATED to 2026-09-12, and the reason is an event, not a cost estimate: this row's declined leg acquired its first real subject on the gate day itself.

WHAT HAPPENED. The 09:23Z scheduled run went red over 15 files, and constants/87a.md was one of them — a movement in the ONE upstream file we have filed a report against (issue 150). Leg 1, shipped 09-04 and working, was SILENT, and correctly so by its own design: it fires on a state TRANSITION, and 150 has been CLOSED since 2026-08-23, so nothing transitioned. What surfaced today's movement was a human reading the drift report line by line — which is precisely the accident that surfaced this row's founding event on 08-26.

A LIMITATION NEITHER note3 NOR note4 NAMED, and it is the decision-relevant fact. note3 says leg 1 "misses a fix that lands with the issue left open". The sharper and worse statement is that leg 1's window closes PERMANENTLY once an issue reaches a terminal state: the transition has already been consumed, so no future change to the file that issue concerned can ever produce a leg-1 signal again. 150 closed on 08-23. Leg 1 is therefore blind to today's 87a movement and to every one after it, forever. That is not a defect in leg 1 — a state poller cannot see a file — but it means leg 1 ALONE does not cover this row's own founding case going forward, which is what closing today would have implicitly asserted.

WHAT TODAY'S EVENT ACTUALLY WAS, verified rather than assumed: 87a gained a paragraph on the nearest visible improvement and why it is out of reach — the HMR2019 tame-inertia depth argument — building on the corrected record rather than responding to our report. So it is NOT plausibly caused by us. That is the strongest possible argument for note3's "go look, never a verdict" rule: leg 2 would have flagged this movement, a human would have looked, and the answer would have been no. A leg that produces a correct no is working, and a leg that never runs produces nothing.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is small and now has both a subject and a fixture. Leg 2, INTERNAL-ONLY — its public form stays permanently declined on the 09-02 grounds, unchanged: a CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT label on a public page publishes a judgment about causation that note3 forbids in terms. The internal form keys on the `path` field already present in every row of ledger/upstream-reports.json, so it invents no state store: at drift time, a changed file whose path is in that map prints CANDIDATE CAUSAL EVENT and the words "go look", to stdout, beside the value/text classification rather than instead of it. KP-78 has a real fixture for the first time: today's 87a movement is the firing case, and any of the other fourteen files in the same cycle is the silent case, both reproducible from the mirror history.

ONE WEEK, not three days. The work is small but it is a detector, and this repo ships no detector without both directions demonstrated on it.

items.denominatorPreCommit2026_08_31: PRE-COMMITTED BEFORE THE NEXT READ (orchestrator-approved 2026-08-31 under default-decision authority; the pre-commit ordering is the half that makes it honest). From today this goal reports as ARRIVALS OVER UNIQUE VIEWERS in the same window — the next report line reads 0 of 3 viewers, never a bare 0. Both figures already exist: npm run reports for arrivals, npm run traffic for unique viewers over the trailing 14 days. THE THRESHOLD, named before reading it: a zero carries information about the PRODUCT only at 30 or more unique viewers in the 14-day window. Below that it is a statement about audience size and must be reported as one. 30 is rule-of-three: with n=30 and zero arrivals the 95 percent upper bound on the arrival rate is about 1 in 10, which is the first point at which a zero rules anything out; at the current n=3 the bound is about 1 in 1, which rules out nothing. This does NOT re-point what G-4 measures — the goal text is untouched and a re-point is David call, per the same ruling. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE REPORT LINE: this is the direct input to A-34 ranked second-surface proposal due 2026-09-02, which cannot rank anything without being able to say whether a quiet month is a product signal or a traffic signal.
items.title: GOAL (Tier-0 from G-3 close): an outside party acts on a record this ledger watches WITHOUT us filing the report
items.note: DAVID-RULED 2026-08-26, his words on card 8e8f547d: "make the next goal whether it happens again without us filing the report". That is his direction verbatim; everything below marked OPERATIONALIZATION is mine and is challengeable, the same standing G-3.note3 carried.
items.note2: WHY IT IS THE RIGHT NEXT QUESTION, and it is a genuinely harder one. G-3 proved the ledger can produce a correction a stranger will act on. It did NOT prove the ledger is discoverable: the path ran through an issue a human here wrote to a maintainer, and the public page had 3 unique viewers over the trailing fortnight. Everything that made G-3 succeed was our outbound effort. G-4 removes exactly that ingredient and asks whether the artifact works on its own.
items.note3: OPERATIONALIZATION — MINE, not his. Close when an outside party takes an action on a record this ledger watches, where the causal path did NOT include an artifact we authored and sent. Qualifying shapes, all of them things we could actually observe: an issue arrives on OUR repo through a per-row 'looks wrong?' or 'Constant not tracked:' link (npm run reports counts these); someone cites the public page in a paper, a forum post or an upstream discussion; an upstream correction lands whose author references the ledger without us having filed anything. NOT qualifying: a maintainer acting on a report we wrote — that is G-3 again, and it will keep happening.
items.note4: STATED WEAKNESS, inherited and sharper than G-3's. This is bounded by DISCOVERABILITY, which is currently near zero and which this lane has deliberately chosen not to instrument: the public page is architecturally incapable of reporting usage (render-site.mjs's selftest actively enforces that it references no third-party asset and fetches nothing), so the only reachable arrival signals are a filed issue, a pull request, an email, and a viewer count running at roughly 3 per fortnight. G-3 took six days from public flip to a met condition BECAUSE we pushed; G-4 may take much longer precisely because it forbids pushing. A long zero here is expected and is NOT evidence the ledger is worthless — it is evidence about reach, which is a different question and may be the one worth acting on.
items.note5: THE TRAP TO AVOID, named now. The obvious way to make G-4 fire is to promote the page — post it somewhere, tell people. That is FORBIDDEN by two standing rules at once: David is never the distribution channel, and any outward contact needs an adversarial review plus his explicit gate. If the honest answer to G-4 is 'nobody can find it', the response is product-side share-worthiness or a surfaced decision, never a quiet campaign.
items.note6: DETECTION VALID FROM 2026-08-28, AND THE ZERO MUST BE READ AGAINST THAT DATE — not against the public-flip date. `report-rate.mjs` classifies an arrival ONLY by the prefilled `Row looks wrong:` title or the `Ledger mirror: upstream` body marker. Until `888a1e5` (2026-08-28, day 20 of the public window) index.html's highest-attention call to action pointed at the BARE GitHub issues list, so an issue filed from the loudest link on the page had `arrivalKind() === null` BY CONSTRUCTION and landed in `outsideOther` — it could never have been counted as an arrival, however genuine it was. So the days before 2026-08-28 are not evidence that nobody arrived; they are days on which an arrival was undetectable through the page's own primary route. Filed at P2 on 2026-08-29 out of that morning's P1 retro; orchestrator-approved the same hour as a WINDOW correction. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: G-4 still measures 'an outside party acts on a watched record without us filing the report' — the measure is untouched and this is not a David metric change. DO NOT retroactively reclassify the pre-2026-08-28 `outsideOther` rows into arrivals: that WOULD change the measure. If those rows are ever wanted, count them under their own named line with the caveat attached.
items.note7: SECOND DETECTION AXIS, ADDED 2026-08-30 AT P2: VIEWPORT. note6 corrected the TIME axis; this one corrects the DEVICE axis, and the 2026-09-26 read must state BOTH or it overstates what a zero means. A-38 (filed 2026-08-29, measured against the live published page) established that on a 390x844 viewport the `looks wrong?` link — the control that every counted arrival passes through — has its left edge at x=755, which is 365px past the right edge of the screen, behind a horizontal scroll with nothing cueing that it exists. So the honest denominator is not `29 clean-detection days`; it is `29 clean-detection days FOR DESKTOP READERS, and zero for phone readers, who have never been able to reach the control at all`. WE CANNOT SIZE THE GAP: GitHub's traffic API carries no device breakdown and the Pages site has no analytics, so the phone share of the trailing-14-day viewer count renders NOT-READY — never 0, and never `all of them`. CONSEQUENCE FOR 2026-09-26: read both axes together; a zero is not evidence of absent interest while this axis is open, because for a phone visitor no-detection and no-interest are indistinguishable. CONSEQUENCE ON 2026-08-30: A-38 is not a layout chore, it is a repair to this goal's ONLY detection path — the same class of work as the note6 window correction, which is why it is that day's Section A. As with note6, the MEASURE is untouched and nothing is reclassified.

items.readDateKnownUninterpretable2026_09_04:
THIS ROW'S 2026-09-26 READ IS KNOWN-UNINTERPRETABLE IN ADVANCE, recorded 2026-09-04 at close-out under the stuck-ask half so that the 09-26 reader does not discover it cold.

THE ARITHMETIC. The pre-committed threshold for a zero here to mean anything about the product is 30 unique viewers. `npm run traffic`, read 2026-09-04T18:43:30Z: 2 unique viewers in the trailing 14 days, 6 unique viewer-days since the public flip on 2026-08-08, day 27. At that rate the denominator reaches roughly 8-10 by 09-26, not 30. So on its own date this row will produce a zero that its own pre-registered rule says cannot discriminate "the product is not worth acting on" from "almost nobody has seen it" — and we know that 22 days early.

WHAT IS NOT BEING DONE HERE, deliberately. This is NOT a re-point and NOT a re-date. Re-pointing a Tier-0 goal is a working-model change, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that adopting a second surface — the obvious re-point — is David's call and never self-approved. The waits-sensibleness gate says a data-wait whose denominator cannot fill is re-pointed, converted or retired and never re-dated; all three of those are his, so the honest action available to the lane is to make the row carry its own defect rather than to quietly move its date.

WHERE IT IS ROUTED. The arithmetic was escalated into `A-34` on 2026-09-03 rather than handled here. `A-34` is David's, dated 2026-09-05, and asks where else this ledger can have the kind of impact `G-3` produced — the breadth-versus-depth question that this denominator is the strongest evidence for. If that ruling slips again, this row's 09-26 gate reads a zero everyone already knew was uninterpretable, which is the specific waste this note exists to prevent.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE READING. Any of: David re-points the goal or adopts a second surface (`A-34`); an arrival actually lands through the per-row "looks wrong?" links, which `npm run reports` counts and which needs n=1 rather than 30; or the viewer count moves by an order of magnitude, which nothing currently planned would cause. The instrument is honest either way — `npm run reports` reconciled 27 + 0 + 0 = 27 on 2026-09-04, so its zero is measured rather than dead.

items.title: David asked where else this ledger can have the kind of impact G-3 just produced — bring him a ranked proposal, not a brainstorm
items.note: DAVID ASKED 2026-08-26, in the same breath as closing G-3: "But also let's find more things to have an impact on? Where else can we have an impact like this?" This is the adopt-a-second-surface question arriving from HIM. CLAUDE.md has said for weeks that adopting a second surface is his call and never self-approved; he is now asking for the options, so what is owed is a ranked proposal with the reasoning, not a list of names.
items.note2: WHAT ACTUALLY PRODUCED THE IMPACT, because the proposal has to reproduce this mechanism rather than the vibe. We mirror a curated record surface BYTE-FOR-BYTE, which is what made a defect findable at all; a human read a row against its cited source and found the witness did not support the record; the correction was one line, checkable, and non-mathematical; and the surface had a maintainer who accepts corrections. All four were necessary. A surface missing any one of them cannot reproduce G-3 — in particular, a surface nobody cites produces no impact however wrong it is.
items.note3: CANDIDATE SHAPES, to be evaluated rather than adopted. (a) Curated 'dynamic survey' documents that are explicitly living records of best-known values and are heavily cited — this is the closest structural match to what we already steward. (b) Community-maintained metadata databases where entries carry values people quote; teorth/erdosproblems is already partially adopted this way as A-6 and is entry-level rather than a mirror. (c) Encyclopaedic articles on named constants, which we already pin two of (C-6, C-10) and which drift and accept corrections, but where correcting is a different social contract and a different outward-gate question. (d) Additional record tables hosted as repositories, which are the cheapest to mirror because the tooling already exists. EVALUATION CRITERIA, in order: is it CITED (no citations, no impact), does it DRIFT (a static document cannot produce a catch), is it MIRRORABLE without a permanently-red alarm, and does it have a correction path that is not a cold email.
items.note4: THE HONEST COST, which belongs in the proposal rather than being discovered afterwards. Each new surface is a mirror plus pins plus a place in the cadence, and this lane's own evangelism bar names COVERAGE as the single biggest threat to its value — but it also warns that a second surface adopted badly makes every existing alarm noisier. The A-6 experience is the evidence: teorth/erdosproblems is pushed near-daily, so a whole-file drift alarm there would be permanently red, and it had to be adopted as entry-level pins instead. Any candidate gets that question asked BEFORE adoption, not after.
items.closeWhen: A ranked written proposal reaches David — candidate surfaces scored against the four criteria, each with the cost of adopting it and the specific reason it could or could not reproduce the G-3 mechanism — and he rules. The row closes on HIS RULING, not on the proposal being written.
items.disposition2026_09_02: GATE FIRED. NO CARD MINTED, AND THAT IS THE ROW'S OWN INSTRUCTION BEING FOLLOWED, NOT A SLIP. onTrigger says: if the research is not done, say so plainly and give a date rather than sending a thinner version, because a ranked list with no citation-footprint evidence behind it is a brainstorm wearing a ranking. The research IS NOT DONE — nobody has established any candidate surface's citation footprint or its correction path, which note2 makes load-bearing: a surface nobody cites produces no impact however wrong it is. Sending David four candidate SHAPES with no evidence would answer his question with the exact artifact this field forbids. READ RUN TODAY, stamped on the row: 'No drift. 113 files match upstream 3a1491040076a3f67a52719e366f5e6b139e5c24' — still ONE mirrored surface, so nothing has been adopted and the question stands exactly as posed. THE PLAIN STATEMENT OWED, said here and in the P4 post rather than left implicit: David asked this on 2026-08-26 and it is now seven days old with no proposal. That is the second re-date. It must not become a third — a question he asked should not age, and at some point 'the research is not done' stops being a reason and becomes the finding. WHAT UNBLOCKS IT, concretely: the deep-research question pitched in today's P3 bonus-session post — what a working mathematician actually does, step by step, when checking whether a bound they are citing is still the best known, and where they look first. That answer IS the citation-footprint evidence this row needs, and it is a question David runs externally rather than one this lane can measure. If the bonus session does not fund it, the fallback is a hand read of citation counts for two candidate surfaces, which is thinner but is evidence rather than shapes. C3 RIDES WITH THIS ROW by the orchestrator's direction: the proposed threshold — 7 consecutive instrument-facing days AND npm run catches at 0 numeric movements raising a second-surface card — is the same decision wearing a trigger, and it lands as a David card, never as a self-adopted threshold.
items.signalDateNote: One week. He asked a direct question and the answer needs real research into each candidate's citation footprint and correction path, which is a day's work rather than an afternoon's. Not longer, because a question he asked should not age.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-05 the proposal goes to him as a board card with the ranking and the costs. If the research is not done, say so plainly and give a date rather than sending a thinner version — a ranked list with no citation-footprint evidence behind it is a brainstorm wearing a ranking, and he asked this question because he wants the reasoning.
items.readCommand: node scripts/reverify.mjs --check # SEPARATOR CONVERTED 2026-09-01 at pre-stage, em dash to hash. The grep leg was DROPPED from the executed command and its result recorded here instead: grep -c 'ledger/' continuity/items.json returns 21 on 2026-09-01, and the count is prose-inflated rather than structural, so it never discriminated one surface from two. The command that answers this row is the check, whose first line names the mirrored surface and its file count. Literal output 2026-09-01 14:30Z: No drift. 113 files match upstream commit 3a1491040076a3f67a52719e366f5e6b139e5c24 (an upstream teorth/optimizationproblems commit; it does not resolve in this repo -- git cat-file -t on its short form reports Not a valid object name, while the same command on a local commit returns commit) -- ONE surface. A second adopted surface shows up as a second mirror directory under ledger/ and a second line here. POSITIVE CONTROL that the check reads a real mirror rather than reporting an empty set: the file count must be non-zero and match the manifest; 113 today.
items.prestage2026_09_01: PRE-STAGED the day before its 2026-09-02 gate. READ RUN TODAY, output above: ONE mirrored surface, 113 files, no drift. Nothing has been adopted since 08-26, so the question is open exactly as posed. WHAT TOMORROW DECIDES: David asked where else this ledger can have the kind of impact G-3 produced, and this row owes him CANDIDATES, not a decision -- adopting a second surface is explicitly his call and never self-approved. Frame it that way or the row will be answered by the wrong person. TWO THINGS THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE CANDIDATE LIST, both learned today. First, the erdosproblems metadata DB (A-6) is already a SECOND surface in the claim sense -- C-8 pins an entry there -- so 'we watch one surface' is true of the MIRROR and false of the CLAIMS, and the candidate list should say which kind it means. Second, and this is the sharper one: the day's finding was that our pin tracks LISTING POSITION, and on Brun's constant a row appended below the pinned one read as a change while nothing was superseded. Any second surface inherits that property. A candidate should be assessed on whether its structure makes appends distinguishable from replacements, because on a surface where it does not, the alarm's output needs the same human reading ours turned out to need. ALSO NOTE the readCommand's grep leg was dropped today as non-discriminating: the number it returned (21) counts prose mentions and would have read the same at one surface or three.
items.dropped_grep_leg_note: The grep -c 'ledger/' leg named in the 2026-08-26 readCommand counted 21 on 2026-09-01. It was DROPPED from the executed command rather than kept, because it does not discriminate: the string appears in prose notes throughout continuity/items.json, so its count moves when anyone writes about the mirror and does not move when a surface is adopted. This is the 2026-08-23 premise-check defect -- the field exists, and it does not discriminate -- caught here before the gate ran on it rather than after.
items.note5: THE ANSWER MAY NOT BE A NEW SURFACE AT ALL, and this belongs at the top of the proposal because it changes what the question is. Look at HOW G-3's instance was actually found: not by the drift alarm. The alarm catches upstream CHANGING; it is structurally blind to upstream being WRONG AND STAYING WRONG, because a row that never moves never fires anything. 87a was caught on 2026-08-14 by a human reading the record row against the paper it cites and noticing the quoted witness — a degree-8 discriminant — could not support a degree-12 record. That is a DIFFERENT detection method from everything on our rail, and it is the one that produced the only outside impact this lane has ever had. WHAT FOLLOWS: we mirror 111 constants, each carrying citations, and almost none of them has had that check applied. The unexamined inventory we ALREADY HAVE may be a richer seam than any second surface, it needs no new mirror or cadence slot, and it is the thing W-9 (the watch asking whether this lane's detection method finds what the lane exists to find) has been circling for days. Breadth versus depth is the real choice to put to David, and presenting only a list of candidate surfaces would silently answer it for him.
items.note6: PRECONDITIONS, DISSECTED FROM THE ONE SUCCESS rather than guessed — orchestrator posed four on 2026-08-26 and asked to have them confirmed or destroyed. TWO CONFIRMED, ONE WRONG, ONE DEMOTED, ONE MISSING. (1) CONFIRMED — a public, machine-readable record a third party maintains. (2) WRONG AS STATED: 'being wrong is checkable by COMPUTATION'. The 87a defect was not computationally checkable and our automated diff never found it and never could have: the row did not CHANGE, it was wrong from the day it was written. What found it was a human reading the record row against the paper it cites and seeing that a degree-8 discriminant cannot support a degree-12 record. REPLACE WITH: each record carries a CITATION to a primary source, and record and citation can be compared by a reader. The defect class that produced impact is 'the record does not match what its own citation says', which is checkable by READING, not by diffing. (3) CONFIRMED, and it is the one precondition we have hard evidence for twice over — teorth merged PR #141 on 2026-08-05 and closed issue #150 state_reason=completed on 2026-08-23, and a third party (Chessing234) authored the actual fix. Two independent acceptances of an outside correction. (4) DEMOTED — 'a standing diff we can watch cheaply' is a precondition for the LANE being sustainable, not for the impact. Our diff had run for a month and produced instrument-facing findings only. Replace with: a corpus large enough that nobody has audited it row by row. The opportunity is unexamined inventory, not motion. (5) MISSING, and probably the strongest filter: THE CORPUS MUST BE CITED BY PEOPLE WHO WOULD BE EMBARRASSED TO CITE IT WRONG. 87a matters because someone may quote 857.5662 in a paper. A corpus nobody cites can be wrong indefinitely at no cost, so a correction there is accepted and changes nothing.
items.note7: WHAT THE CORRECTED SET IMPLIES, and it sharpens note5 rather than repeating it. If the operative precondition is 'record carries a citation, and the two can be compared by reading', then the 111 constants we ALREADY mirror satisfy all five preconditions trivially — we have already proven this corpus qualifies, because the one success came out of it. A new corpus has to be shown to satisfy them; this one is shown. That does not settle breadth versus depth, and the proposal must still put both to David, but it means the burden of proof is asymmetric and the proposal should say so: depth is the option whose preconditions are already evidenced.
items.note8: HOW THE ASYMMETRY GOES IN THE PROPOSAL — orchestrator refinement 2026-08-26, and it is a real sharpening of note7 rather than a restatement. note7 says the proposal should SAY the burden of proof is asymmetric. The refinement: state it as a PREMISE, not as a conclusion. David asked 'where ELSE', which is a breadth question, and if the five preconditions imply the highest-expected-impact next correction is inside the corpus we already hold, the proposal must say that plainly AT THE TOP and let him overrule it knowingly. A proposal that reaches depth as a conclusion after surveying breadth has already done the persuading in its structure — and BREADTH ALWAYS SOUNDS MORE AMBITIOUS THAN DEPTH, so a framing that buries the asymmetry is not neutral, it is a thumb on the scale toward the more impressive-sounding answer. Same failure shape as declaring my own goal met: letting a framing do work that belongs to the person whose decision it is.
items.note9: DECISION RULE, COMMITTED 2026-08-27 BEFORE THE COUNT IS READ (orchestrator-directed at P2, and the timing is the point — a threshold written after the third data point arrives is a threshold fitted to it). RULE: if the THIRD record-facing catch is again an upstream self-correction of CITATION METADATA — a date, a version, an attribution — rather than a bound moving, then the lane's self-description is rewritten and the 09-02 proposal is DEPTH on citation metadata, not BREADTH via a second surface. Standing at 2 of the last 3: 2026-08-14 (87a.md citing a witness that proves the previous record) and 2026-08-27 (the Lorist-Schwenninger attribution retracted). WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the dry-week rule's only prescribed answer to a quiet stretch is 'adopt a second surface', which is a breadth move. If what this ledger actually detects is citation decay rather than record movement, breadth is the wrong axis and we would be answering a real signal with the wrong instrument. The orchestrator carries this to David when the third lands, NOT before, and adopting a second surface stays David's call either way.
items.disposition2026_09_05:
NOT DONE, THIRD SLIP, DATED 2026-09-08. Saying it plainly as onTrigger requires: the citation-footprint research is not done, no thinner version was sent, and the reason is that the alarm fired first. The 09:23Z scheduled run went red over 15 upstream files carrying TWO record movements, and a drift cycle with records in it outranks a research task on the day it lands — that is the whole premise of the lane. The cycle took the morning: primary-source verification of both movements, the snapshot ratchet, a broken hand claim, the README catch table, and the issue close.

WHAT TODAY ADDED TO THIS ROW, and it is not nothing. The proposal was missing per-candidate evidence; it was ALSO missing an exhibit, and today produced one that no amount of research would have generated. Two mathematical records moved overnight — the bounded prime gap constant 240 to 186, and the Steiner ratio lower bound 0.8559 to 0.860 asterisked — and this ledger had both, verified against the Lean manifest and the Zenodo record, within six hours of the push. On top of that a curated table quietly moved a cited bound to its truncation, below the value the paper proves, and a hand claim caught it.

Nobody outside Skylark knows any of that. That sentence is the whole of A-34's question stated as an observation instead of a plan, and it is now datable, quotable and cheap for David to check. When the ranked proposal goes to him it should OPEN with 2026-09-05, because the strongest argument for widening this instrument's reach is a day on which the instrument worked perfectly and reached nobody.

THREE DAYS, NOT SEVEN. The research is a day's work and the row has now slipped three times; a week is what produced the third slip. 09-08 is a Tuesday and the work is a single sitting.

items.title: CLAUDE.md was 49,202 bytes against a 45,000 budget — compressed to 44,902 at P5, same day
items.note: ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, 2026-08-28T14:46:52Z, folded in as instructed rather than acted on immediately (the dispatch said DEFER to the /daily Section 0 / P2 read and self-compress at P5, and explicitly said not to preempt the kickoff row ahead of it). MEASURED WITH THE TOOL, NOT SELF-READ, exactly as the dispatch required: `node ../skylark-site/scripts/check-claude-md-sizes.mjs` prints 49202 for this lane against warn>45000, exit 1, and names bounds-ledger FIRST of 32 projects — we are the largest CLAUDE.md in the portfolio. The remedy named in the dispatch is `node ../skylark-site/scripts/compress-to-budget.mjs --file CLAUDE.md --target 45000`, trimming our OWN file and keeping the lane gotchas.
items.note2: WHY THE OBVIOUS releaseTest WAS REJECTED, because it is this repo's own known trap. The natural release command is the fleet script that produced the finding — but it exits 1 if ANY of the 32 lanes is over budget, and two others are (skylark-n8n-workflows 46371, walking-denver 46365). Its exit code therefore cannot go green on our action alone, so adopting it would have recorded a PASS CONDITION THAT CANNOT BE REACHED — the exact defect found on A-18 on 2026-08-25 and now carried in memory. The releaseTest below is scoped to this file instead. POSITIVE CONTROL that the scoped command measures the same property: `git cat-file -s HEAD:CLAUDE.md` returns 49202, byte-identical to the fleet tool's figure for this lane, and git stores blobs LF-normalized which is the unit the tool declares (utf8-bytes-lf). The two agree, so the cheap command is a faithful proxy and not a different measurement wearing the same number.
items.note3: ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, passed up rather than chased, because it is the orchestrator's tool and not ours. The output lists learn-the-dao at 47994 — above the stated warn threshold of 45000 — and does NOT flag it, reporting '3 of 32 over budget' while four rows exceed 45000. The likely explanation is a per-project budget in docs/size-budgets.md rather than a bug, and that file was not read from here, so this is a QUESTION and not a finding. Flagged because a threshold that reads as global while behaving per-project is the shape that makes a reader mistrust the number they are being asked to act on.
items.releaseTest: git cat-file -s HEAD:CLAUDE.md — prints the LF-normalized byte size of our committed CLAUDE.md. Under 45000 means the compression landed and this row CLOSES; 49202 or anything above 45000 means it has not. Cross-check with the fleet view via `node ../skylark-site/scripts/check-claude-md-sizes.mjs`, but do NOT use that script's exit code as the release condition — it reports on all 32 lanes and two others are also over budget, so it can stay red for reasons outside this repo.
items.onTrigger: At P5 today run `node ../skylark-site/scripts/compress-to-budget.mjs --file CLAUDE.md --target 45000`, then re-measure with the releaseTest above and paste the literal before/after byte counts into the commit rather than a paraphrase of the verdict. KEEP THE LANE GOTCHAS — the dispatch says so and they are the highest-value content in the file; the compression targets repetition and superseded history, never a trap that is still live. If P5 does not happen today this row EXPIRES and check-deferrals fires tomorrow, which is the intended behaviour and not a bug.
items.signalDateNote: Same P2 scan, same class, one row later. A-35 carried expiresOn (which check-deferrals reads) but no expectedSignalBy (which the item date sweep reads), so it was half-visible: one instrument could see it and the other could not. Dated to match expiresOn so both read the same day. THE TRANSFERABLE POINT, and it is why this is written down rather than just fixed: two date fields serving two different instruments is a place where an item can be simultaneously tracked and untracked, and nothing reports the disagreement.
items.readCommand: git cat-file -s HEAD:CLAUDE.md — prints the LF-normalized byte size of the committed CLAUDE.md, which is the exact quantity the trigger is about. Under 45000 means the P5 compression landed; 49202 (the value at filing) or anything above 45000 means it has not. POSITIVE CONTROL that this cheap command measures the same property as the fleet tool that raised the finding: on 2026-08-28 both returned 49202, and git stores blobs LF-normalized, which is the unit `check-claude-md-sizes.mjs` declares (utf8-bytes-lf). DO NOT substitute that fleet script as the read: it exits 1 if ANY of the 32 lanes is over budget and two others are, so its exit code can never go green on our action alone — a pass condition that cannot be reached.
items.note4: THE MISSING readCommand WAS THE SAME DEFECT AS THIS MORNING'S, ONE FIELD TO THE LEFT — orchestrator-caught 2026-08-28, and worth recording rather than quietly filling in. This row was filed carrying a `releaseTest` whose value is the exact command a reader needs, so it was FULLY COMPLIANT with `check-deferrals` and CRITICAL under `continuity-check`, which reads `readCommand`. The command existed; the field the second instrument reads was empty. That is the identical shape written up in the P2 task-complete hours earlier — A-35 carrying `expiresOn` but not `expectedSignalBy`, 'two date fields serving two instruments, and nothing reports the disagreement' — and I then reproduced it on the same row in a different pair of fields. THIRD INSTANCE TODAY of one thing being simultaneously tracked and untracked. Also worth noting plainly: P2 declared its gates clean and `continuity-check` was not in that battery, so the phase that diagnosed the class shipped a fresh instance of it behind a green board.
items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-28 at P5, on the day it was filed and the day it was due. LITERAL BEFORE/AFTER, pasted rather than paraphrased because this row's own onTrigger demanded exactly that: `git cat-file -s HEAD:CLAUDE.md` read **49202** at filing and the working tree now measures **44902** — `compress-to-budget --file CLAUDE.md --target 45000` reports "HEAD -> now: 49202 -> 44902 bytes (shrank -4300) ... target: 45000 (utf8-bytes-lf) — under by 98" and "keep-list: 32 entries · 0 missing". The fleet view confirms it independently: `check-claude-md-sizes.mjs` now lists this lane at 44902 and NO LONGER NAMES IT among the over-budget rows (2 of 32 remain: skylark-n8n-workflows, walking-denver).
items.note5: THE KEEP-LIST CAUGHT A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED, which is the whole reason to run a compression against one. Rewriting the classification bullet, I capitalised a protected string to "**Numeric or BYTE-ONLY**"; the tool reported `keep-list: 32 entries · 1 missing — "numeric or BYTE-ONLY"`. Repaired by rewording to "**Whether a counted catch was numeric or BYTE-ONLY**", restoring the string verbatim, and the final run reads 0 missing. A compression that only measured BYTES would have shipped that silently.
items.note6: WHAT WAS CUT AND WHAT WAS NOT. Every RULE survives; only incident narrative and duplication were trimmed, and all cut text is preserved in docs/claude-md-archive.md plus git history. The largest single win was the classification bullet, which stated one sentence TWICE and carried two stale day-counts ("five consecutive", "six consecutive") in a file whose own as-of rule says not to hold live values — it now says explicitly not to quote a day-count from CLAUDE.md at all. Two bullet PAIRS that were one lesson each were merged (erdosproblems-403 with test-from-the-exercising-environment; the two pipe/exit-code bullets). Three script paragraphs that restated AGENTS.md were reduced to the judgment AGENTS.md does not carry.
items.note7: AND THE COMPRESSION FOUND TWO STALE CLAIMS, which is the more valuable half. items.title: On a phone, G-4 detection path is 365px off-screen behind a horizontal scroll nothing cues
items.note: FOUND 2026-08-29 by the A-36 read, which is the point of having run it. Measured at 390x844 against the live published page with playwright-cli. The page body does NOT overflow (390 against a 390 viewport) so the layout is not broken -- the .scroll wrapper does its job. But the wrapper shows 348px of 1032px, and the looks-wrong? link on a row has its left edge at x=755: 365px past the right edge of the screen. The first column ends at x=274, so what a phone reader actually sees is the constant name and part of a bounds cell, with nothing indicating that source, looks wrong? and cite exist off to the right.
items.note2: WHY IT OUTRANKS AN ORDINARY LAYOUT NIT. The looks-wrong? link IS G-4 detection path -- the Tier-0 goal is that an outside party acts on a watched record without us filing the report, and npm run reports counts exactly the arrivals that come through those per-row links. A phone visitor who spots a wrong row therefore cannot reach the control that would make the goal fire, and at roughly 3 unique viewers per fortnight we would never see the loss in the numbers. This is the same blind spot A-36 note4 predicted, now measured instead of predicted.
items.note3: WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The controls ARE reachable: a horizontal swipe inside the table brings them into view. The defect is that nothing cues the gesture, not that the page is broken. This is a reachability measurement from a headless viewport and says nothing about tap ergonomics, real-device behaviour, or how the page feels in a hand.
items.note4: FIX CANDIDATES, none chosen -- this is a layout decision worth its own flow rotation rather than a rushed edit, and the measurements above mean that rotation starts from evidence instead of a dig. (a) below a breakpoint, move the row controls out of the last cell and under the constant name in the first cell; (b) make the last column sticky to the right edge so it rides along the horizontal scroll; (c) collapse the table to stacked cards below a breakpoint. Each trades differently against the desktop layout, which is currently correct and must not regress.
items.note5: CLOSED 2026-08-30 on candidate (c), stacked cards below 56rem, shipped in ee19ee9. The breakpoint is the table's OWN min-width, so the switch happens exactly where horizontal scroll would otherwise begin rather than at a number someone picked. Each bound cell gained a data-label surfaced by a CSS ::before, which is load-bearing and not decoration: stacking hides thead, and the column header is the only thing telling the upper bound from the lower one. CANDIDATE (a) WAS REJECTED BY THE PAGE'S OWN SELFTEST, which is the part worth keeping: render-site asserts one report link per row (flagLinks.length === rows.length), so moving the controls into the first cell for phones -- which means rendering them twice and hiding one copy by media query -- fails it. The right answer to a verifier rejecting a candidate is a different candidate, never a weakened assertion. Candidate (b), a sticky right column, is one CSS rule but would permanently occlude roughly 200px of a 390px viewport and behaves badly with the cite disclosure open.
items.note6: CLOSE EVIDENCE, read from the LIVE PUBLISHED PAGE after the Pages build for ee19ee9 reported status built at 2026-08-30T15:46:09Z -- not from local bytes, because closeWhen asks for the published numbers and identical-input is not the same claim as measured-output. AT 1440x900 AFTER, desktop re-verified unregressed on the same live page: thead visible with 4 headers, cell display table-cell, the row cells share one baseline, hiddenToRight 0, bodyScrollW 1440, and getComputedStyle(cell, '::before').content resolves to 'none' -- so the mobile labels provably do not leak onto desktop. items.title: The table's cite block emits a non-canonical URL for a constant that now has a canonical page
items.note: Filed 2026-09-03 as P3 rec 2, named rather than shipped at the end of a long session, and the orchestrator's ack directed it to be tomorrow's Section A. A row's `cite` control emits the in-table anchor form `<SITE>#c-<id>`, while that constant's own page emits `<SITE>c/<id>.html` AND declares that page `rel="canonical"`. So one site hands out two addresses for one object, and the one the table gives is not the one we tell search engines is authoritative. Measured 2026-09-03: 114 anchor-form cite URLs in index.html; positive control, c/88a.html carries 2 hits of its own canonical URL, so the page half is already correct and only the table half is wrong. This is small but it is NOT cosmetic on this lane: a ledger whose product is citation accuracy should not emit two addresses for one constant, which is why it was not shipped unreviewed at 16:00.
items.note2: SCOPE CAUTION for whoever ships it. Do NOT simply repoint the `cite` block and walk away: the in-table anchor is ALSO the permalink target that `<a class="id">` uses, and render-site's selftest asserts that permalink targets the row's OWN id in document order. Changing the cite text must leave the permalink alone. KP-78 applies -- demonstrate that the check fires on the anchor form and is silent on the canonical form, and prove the mutation landed before believing either verdict.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-04 ship it as Section A: the table's cite block emits the constant's canonical page URL, the permalink keeps targeting the in-page anchor, and the selftest gains an assertion that no cite block emits the anchor form. If it is not shipped that day, say why in one line rather than carrying it silently -- it is a one-line template change plus a test, so a slip means something displaced it.
items.closeWhen: index.html emits zero anchor-form cite URLs, every row's cite block carries that constant's c/<id>.html address, the row permalink still resolves to the in-page anchor, and a selftest assertion fails when the anchor form comes back.
items.readCommand: grep -c 'bounds-ledger/#c-' index.html # counts cite blocks still emitting the NON-canonical in-table anchor. 114 on 2026-09-03, which is every row; 0 is the closed state. POSITIVE CONTROL that the two forms are really different and the page half is already right: grep -c 'bounds-ledger/c/88a.html' c/88a.html returns 2. Do NOT read a 0 as done without that control -- a typo'd pattern also returns 0.
items.resolution:
CLOSED 2026-09-03 as Section A, a day BEFORE the 2026-09-04 the onTrigger named — this session ran a day early on spare capacity, so the row ships early rather than slipping. Dating note, because this lane keeps catching its own: the work was first labelled 09-04 after the primer's filename, and the render's own git-derived date (first pinned 2026-09-03) caught it before the push. The table's cite block now emits the constant's canonical `c/<id>.html`; the row permalink still targets the in-page anchor, which the onTrigger required and which render-site's permalink assertions (unchanged) still pin row-by-row in document order. Source ship: c125704. The page render lands in the commit carrying this close.

LITERAL READS, before and after, from the same probe the readCommand names. BEFORE (2026-09-03, and re-measured today at HEAD before the edit): 114 anchor-form cite URLs in index.html, positive control `grep -c 'bounds-ledger/c/88a.html' c/88a.html` returns 2 so the page half was already correct. AFTER: 0 anchor-form cite URLs, 115 canonical cite URLs, 115 relative row permalinks still `href="#c-`, and `id="c-1b"` present. The closeWhen asked for zero anchor-form cite URLs and got it; it also asked for a selftest assertion that fails when the anchor form comes back, and there are now three, proven.

THE SCOPE CAUTION IN note2 WAS RIGHT AND IS WHY THE PERMALINK SURVIVED. The change was made in `citation()` alone; the `<a class="id" href="#c-<id>">` template was not touched, and the two are asserted separately — the cite-block loop asserts the anchor form is ABSENT from every citation while a positive control asserts it is still PRESENT as the permalink, so a future edit cannot satisfy one by breaking the other.

KP-78, THREE CONTROLS, each proving the assertion it actually TRIPPED rather than the one intended (the 2026-09-02 lesson, applied deliberately here because the first control shadowed the second). (1) The anchor form restored in citation(): render-site --selftest exit 1 on "row 2a's citation must carry that constant's canonical page URL". (2) The same mutation with the per-row loop neutralised to `[].entries()`: exit 1 on the unit-level assertion instead, so both levels are proven live. (3) The same mutation against render-constant-pages --selftest: exit 1 on "the page's cite block must cite the page, not the table row" — the assertion that now catches a re-added local substitution. Restored, both suites exit 0. Every mutation was proven to land by grep before its verdict was read.

WHAT ELSE THE WORK FOUND, recorded here because it was found by executing this row and it is the larger half. `pageCitation()` in render-constant-pages.mjs — a local `.replace()` swapping the anchor for the page URL — is DELETED rather than left beside the fix: it was the mechanism that let one site publish two addresses, and after the change 114 of 115 constant pages were byte-identical to what it had been producing, which is the proof that it was a patch over a divergence rather than a feature. And checking whether the flow doc's already-ships line was stale surfaced a coverage hole nothing here could see: extract-pins skipped 1b.md, so the Erdos minimum overlap constant — the record this repo opened on — had no row on the page while the README promised "All 111 tracked constants". Fixed in the same commit, with a new coverage guard in render-state-block --check asserting the README's front-door sentences against the page's own row count. Full account: docs/key-user-flows.md Rotation 8.

CODEX: not dispatched. Both attempts returned the fleet's concurrent-subagent ceiling ("You can run 20 subagents at once. Do not retry."), so this pane could not spawn the delegate. Reviewed against the five questions by hand instead; that is self-review and is not recorded as a Codex round.

items.title: The brief leg became permanently unverifiable on 2026-09-04 — should it keep contributing to npm run check's exit code?
items.note: WHAT HAPPENED, measured 2026-09-04 at P1. npm run verify exited 3 at f5f54c0 on the check-brief leg alone; every other leg passed (no drift, 116 files @ 01a0bc8, 241 claims with 239 holding and the 2 manual ones UNVERIFIED by design, state block in sync, catch table 14/14, coverage counts 115/115, both render checks PASS, deferrals PASS). The documented cause for exit 3 is a missing CC_PROMPTS_PIN. The pin was PRESENT: a direct probe carrying x-cc-pin returned 307 to /t/signin?next=%2Ft%2Flanes%2Fbounds-ledger. The orchestrator supplied the actual cause the same morning — sign-in on /t/* went Google-session-only on 2026-09-04 (S-20260904-25) and the cc_pin cookie was retired that day, so an x-cc-pin header no longer signs a person in. The brief itself is fine and the David-facing link resolves in a browser; what is gone is any way for a SCRIPT to verify it.
items.note2: WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A PATCH. The leg now fails on every run, forever, with no repo-side change that can make it pass. A permanently-red alarm is this lane's FOUNDING DEFECT — the same shape as the five Drift: issues that sat open for six days and taught the reader to ignore the alarm, and as the always-red whole-file watch that A-6 refused to build. An alarm that cannot go quiet carries no information, and the next real failure of npm run verify will land on an agent who has learned that exit 3 is just the brief.
items.note3: THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THIS REPO AND IT IS THE LIKELY ANSWER: the manual: true claims. C-7 and C-9 are pinned to a source that blocks automated fetch, so they report UNVERIFIED, are never green, and — the load-bearing half — never touch counts or the exit code. The brief leg is now in exactly that position: a surface a script cannot read, whose unreadability says nothing about whether the artifact is correct. Treating it the same way keeps the honest UNVERIFIED report while letting the gate's exit code mean what it used to mean. WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, and it is the tempting shortcut: making the leg exit 0. That laundeers an unverifiable into a pass, which is the invariant this lane refuses in every other place (never make a 429 non-fatal; UNREACHABLE stays red). The distinction is that a manual claim is EXCLUDED from the exit code while still being REPORTED, not silently passed.
items.note4: COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO HOLD, because it is real: check-brief exists because the hosted brief drifted from its source and hand-checks under-reported — on 7/30 and 7/31 a hand-check found ONE missing block each time while the script derived TWO, stale since 26 July. Excluding it from the exit code means nothing fails when the brief goes stale again, and the brief is the ONE David-facing surface this lane has. So the exclusion is only safe if the UNVERIFIED line stays loud in the output and something still reads it. Do not close this row by quietly deleting the leg.
items.closeWhen: Either the leg is excluded from npm run check's exit code on the manual: true pattern — reported, never green, never counted — with KP-78 demonstrated both ways (a stale brief still prints its finding; an unreachable brief no longer reds the gate), or a route/credential that a script can actually use is available and the leg goes back to being a real check, or the leg is deliberately retired with the David-facing-surface risk in note4 written down as accepted.
items.signalDateNote: Four days, not same-day and not a week. Not same-day because nothing is mechanically blocked — the P1 task-complete posted normally against a receipt recording exitCode 3, so this is corrosion rather than an outage. Not a week because the corrosion is the whole problem: every day the leg stays permanently red is a day the next agent learns to read exit 3 as noise, and that habit is what the founding defect is made of.

items.title: Two user-facing readers still key off OUR pin history and read as claims about the RECORD — the date label and the sort key
items.note: FROM A ONE-PASS AUDIT the orchestrator asked for on 2026-09-04, after the same root cause surfaced twice independently. THE ROOT CAUSE, stated once: every instrument keyed to our pin history is blind to a constant's past when we arrived after it. Instance 1, found 2026-09-03: npm run catches reads 0 for a week containing a real bound improvement, because a catch is a generated pin whose expect CHANGED and an ADDED constant has no prior expect (movedPins in catch-rate.mjs requires the id in BOTH sides). Instance 2, found and FIXED 2026-09-04 in 356987f: the search haystack carried only pinned and previously-pinned values, so 0.380876 and 246 returned zero rows. The audit — grep -rn 'prevExpect|changeFor(' over scripts/ — found the primitive in lookup.mjs and exactly two remaining consumers, both of them USER-FACING and both unfixed.
items.note2: INSTANCE 3, the date label, and it is the one that does reassurance work. cell() renders whenLabel(changed, kind) from changeFor(), whose kind is 'first' when no prior pin exists. Live on the public page right now: constant 1b, the Erdos minimum overlap constant this repo opened on, reads 'first pinned 2026-09-03 — unchanged since' on BOTH bound rows. That is TRUE about our pinning and it is the sentence docs/evangelism-bar.md calls 'a believable nothing-to-see-here, which is worth more than silence'. At one day old it is not believable in that sense: upstream's own 1b.md table lists $0.380876$ at line 24 and $0.380868$ at line 26 as separate rows, so the record this label reassures about has visible history and we simply were not watching for it. The label is honest about US and reads as a statement about the RECORD, which is the exact confusion this lane exists to police. NOT proposing to remove it: the disclosure 'first pinned <date>' is the honest half and deleting it would be worse. The question is whether a pin younger than some window should say 'unchanged since' at all, or should read as 'tracked since <date> — no movement seen yet', which claims only what we can support.
items.note3: INSTANCE 4, the sort key, and it mis-ORDERS rather than mis-states. data-changed is newerOf(upperChanged, lowerChanged), which for an added constant is the day WE pinned it. So the 'Most recently updated first' ordering puts a newly MIRRORED constant at the top as though its record had just moved. 1b currently carries data-changed=2026-09-03 and sorts accordingly. A visitor using that ordering to find what moved recently is shown what we STARTED WATCHING recently. Same root, and it is the ordering control the page offers for exactly the question this lane answers.
items.note4: WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A PATCH TODAY. Both fixes are judgments about WORDING and RANKING on the public page, and this repo's hardest-guarded line is that a from-to pair is a movement claim whatever noun sits in the sentence (the note above cell(), and commit 8a4192a which refused exactly that inference). A label change here is a change to what the page ASSERTS, so it gets designed rather than tweaked at the end of a P4. It is also not urgent: nothing is false today, the disclosure is present in both cases, and the misread requires a visitor to skim rather than read.
items.closeWhen: Either both readers are changed with KP-78 on each — the date label distinguishes 'no movement seen while we watched' from 'unchanged', and the sort key either excludes first-pin dates or discloses that it includes them — or each is deliberately declined with the reason written down, which is a legitimate outcome for the sort key in particular.
items.signalDateNote: A week. Not sooner because nothing here is false and the page is not misleading anyone today at 2 viewers a fortnight; not later because this is the THIRD and FOURTH instance of one root cause found in two days, and the first two were both found by accident rather than by looking.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-11 decide both readers separately, because they fail differently: the label is a wording question about what we may assert, the sort key is a ranking question about what the control means. Do NOT bundle them into one fix. If the label changes, the replacement must still disclose the first-pin date — deleting the disclosure to avoid the reassurance would trade an over-read for a silence, which is worse.
items.readCommand: node -e "const t=require('fs').readFileSync('index.html','utf8');const i=t.indexOf('id=\"c-1b\"');const s=t.slice(i,i+900);console.log(s.match(/first pinned[^<]*/g), s.match(/data-changed=\"[^\"]*\"/)[0])" # prints the founding record's live date label and sort key. On 2026-09-04 it printed [ 'first pinned 2026-09-03 — unchanged since' ] and data-changed="2026-09-03", which IS the finding. POSITIVE CONTROL that the probe reads a real row rather than an empty slice: it must print a non-null match for both; a null on either means the id or the offset is wrong, not that the label is gone.

items.title: Upstream moved Haugland's minimum-overlap bound to its truncation — is that one wrong cell or the whole column's convention, and does either warrant an upstream report?
items.note: THE FACT, established 2026-09-05 and not in dispute. Upstream changed the H2016 row of constants/1b.md (the Erdos minimum overlap constant, in a table headed 'Known upper bounds') from 0.380927 to 0.380926. The cited paper, arXiv:1609.08000, proves 0.3809268534330870 — re-fetched via ar5iv on 2026-09-05, with 'minimum overlap' (7 occurrences) and 'Haugland' (4) in the SAME response as the positive control that the fetch was the paper. 0.380926 is therefore the truncation and sits strictly BELOW the proved value, so read as a bound at the precision shown it asserts something Haugland did not establish. 0.380927 is the round-to-nearest form and is bound-safe, because rounding an upper bound UP preserves validity. Our drift alarm caught the change and hand claim C-2 went BROKEN on it; C-2 is re-pinned and docs/findings/2026-07-23-haugland-final-digit.md carries the dated reversal.
items.note2: WHY THIS IS NOT YET A REPORT, and it is the whole of the work. The 2026-07-23 finding read Tao's table as using round-to-nearest for this row and called that the better citation form. What was NEVER established is whether the COLUMN's convention is 'a valid bound' or 'the leading digits of the value'. Four neighbouring rows — 0.380924 [GGSWT2025], 0.380876 [YKLBMWKCZGS2026], 0.380871 [T2026], 0.380868 [YLTLYSTYLLGDHZSWZSHMELCZX2026] — may be truncations of longer values too. If they are, the H2016 row is now CONSISTENT with its neighbours and the caveat belongs to the whole column; a one-cell correction would then be the wrong report and would make us look like we had read one row and generalised. If they are not, one cell is out of step with four and the report is small, specific and checkable. The difference is four primary-source lookups, and nothing outward should be drafted before they are done.
items.note3: GATE. Any upstream contact goes through the adversarial refute-it review AND David's explicit approval — the standing rule, no exception for a correction that looks obvious. Deliberately NOT surfaced to David as a board card on 2026-09-05: the question as it stands is undecidable by him, because the fact that decides between the two report shapes has not been looked up yet. A card asking him to rule on an unresearched fork is noise on his board. It goes to him WITH the four lookups done, or not at all.
items.note4: PROVENANCE OF THE CATCH, worth recording because it is the shape the lane claims to have. Nothing here was found by looking for it. The scheduled alarm went red at 09:23Z over 15 files; C-2 was pinned to this exact digit BECAUSE a finding in July had decided the digit was the interesting thing; and the pin broke. A cross-surface hand claim, written seven weeks earlier about a rounding convention, is what turned an editorial-looking one-character diff into a bound question.
items.onTrigger: On 2026-09-12 do the four lookups — the proved values behind 0.380924, 0.380876, 0.380871 and 0.380868 — and decide which of the two report shapes the evidence supports, or that neither does. Then EITHER draft the report and put it through the adversarial review before it goes anywhere near David, OR close this row recording that the column is uniformly truncated and the H2016 row is no longer out of step. Do NOT send anything on the strength of the H2016 row alone; that is the failure mode this row exists to prevent.
items.closeWhen: Either an upstream report on constants/1b.md has passed the adversarial review and reached David for the send decision, or the four neighbouring rows have been checked against their sources and the row closes with the finding that the column's convention is uniform and no report is warranted. Closing on the second branch REQUIRES the four values written down, not a summary judgement that they are probably truncations.
items.readCommand: curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/main/constants/1b.md — prints the live file. The H2016 row currently reads 0.380926; if it reads 0.380927 again upstream reverted and this row closes as moot. POSITIVE CONTROL that the fetch is the right document and not an error page: the response must also contain the string 'Erdos minimum overlap constant' heading text and the neighbouring value 0.380924, so an empty or redirected body cannot be misread as 'the row is gone'.
items.lookups2026_09_05:
FOUR LOOKUPS DONE 2026-09-05, and the fork this row registered was a FALSE DICHOTOMY. Neither branch is what the evidence says. Every one of the four neighbouring rows quotes its source's OWN figure, stated by that source at exactly six decimals — so upstream truncates nothing and the column's convention is "quote the source". Each was read from the source itself, never from another paper's summary of it, and each fetch names a token proving the artifact.

1. 0.380924 [GGSWT2025] — arXiv:2511.02864, AlphaEvolve. The paper's own sentence: "AlphaEvolve managed to improve the upper bound ever so slightly to" 0.380924. Stated at 6 dp; no longer form of its own value appears. Control: "AlphaEvolve" 1006 occurrences, "minimum overlap" 3, in the same fetch. NOTE: this paper also carries Haugland's full-precision 0.3809268534330870, three times.

2. 0.380876 [YKLBMWKCZGS2026] — TTT-Discover, "Learning to Discover at Test Time". 0.380876 appears 7 times; 6 dp. Control: "Minimum Overlap" 20 occurrences plus "minimum overlap" 7 in the same fetch. CORROBORATION WORTH KEEPING: this paper independently renders Haugland as 0.380927, nine times, and never as 0.380926 — an outside party using the round-up form as the citation form.

3. 0.380871 [T2026] — TogetherAI, github.com/togethercomputer/EinsteinArena-new-SOTA. Read the repo README's own results table, whose row is: Erdos' Minimum Overlap | minimize | **0.380871** | 0.380876 | -0.000005. Their value bolded as the new result, prior best beside it. 6 dp. Control: the row names the problem.

4. 0.380868 [YLTLYSTYLLGDHZSWZSHMELCZX2026] — SimpleTES, arXiv:2604.19341. UPSTREAM IS RIGHT HERE AND IT TOOK WORK TO ESTABLISH, so record it: the paper CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Its intro headlines 0.380856 ("SimpleTES found a construction achieving 0.380856"), and 0.380856 appears eleven times against five for 0.380868 — so a future reader grepping this paper will conclude our table is stale. It is not. The results section says "Our best result is 0.380868", and of the smaller figure the authors write: "an even better result was found during our ablation study (0.380856), which is NOT included in the table for fair comparison" and "For the sake of fairness in the comparison, we did not include it in Table 10". Upstream quotes the paper's reported table result. Anyone re-checking this row should read that sentence before filing anything.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING LOOKUP 2, and it is not a rounding question: upstream's [YKLBMWKCZGS2026] reference cites the URL test-time-training.github.io/discover.pdf, which is DEAD — it returns GitHub Pages' "Site not found" page, HTTP 200 with an HTML body of about 9 KB and the title "Site not found". This is the HTTP-200-is-not-the-artifact trap firing on upstream's own citation rather than on our fetch. The paper is live at arXiv:2601.16175v2, published 2026-01-22. A dead-link fix is a smaller and far less arguable correction than the rounding one.

WHAT THIS MAKES THE H2016 ROW. Not "one truncated cell among four truncated neighbours", and not "one truncated cell among four exact ones". It is this: the column's convention is to quote the source's own figure, four rows have a source that states six decimals, and H2016 is THE ONLY ROW WHOSE SOURCE GIVES FULL PRECISION (0.3809268534330870) — so it is the only row where upstream must CHOOSE a rendering, and on 2026-09-05 that choice changed from the round-up, which is bound-safe, to the round-down, which is strictly below the proved value and so is not a valid upper bound at the precision shown. The convention did not change; the one cell where the convention is silent flipped direction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REPORT SHAPE. The one-cell correction is now the supported shape and the convention-note shape is refuted: there is no column-wide truncation practice to write a note about. STILL GATED — nothing drafted and nothing sent. Next step is a decision, not a dig.

meta.loopArchetypeNote: Recorded 2026-08-25 (A-26). The user comes back when they are writing, refereeing or revising — a cadence of weeks to months, triggered by their calendar and not by ours. This is the most decision-relevant field in the evangelism bar, because it DISQUALIFIES the metrics the portfolio reaches for by default: a tool used at citation time SHOULD have a poor D7-return-rate, and optimising that number would push toward engagement mechanics that make the product worse. Share-rate and quarter-scale repeat visits are the right shape. Kept in items.json rather than health.json because health.json is GENERATED and a regeneration would silently drop it. Full reasoning in the evangelism bar doc under docs/.
meta.untrackedCommitsShapeNote: SHA-KEYED OBJECT, not an array — the shape continuity-check actually reads. It calls Object.entries() on this value and keeps only keys matching /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/, so an ARRAY of {sha, rationale} yields keys "0","1",... which all fail that test and every entry is silently discarded. This file carried the array form from 2026-08-15 until 2026-08-25, so the documented escape hatch never suppressed anything; the two entries it held also aged out of the 48h window, which is why nobody could tell. Do not 'tidy' this back into an array.
